News.title: Another female Trump Cabinet staffer booted after midterms thrashing
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Another high-ranking woman in Donald Trump’s administration is expected to leave her Cabinet role as part of the president’s staffing shakeup following the disastrous midterm election results.

White House Cabinet secretary Meghan Bauer - a lesser-known official whose influential role acts as the bridge between the president and his Cabinet members - will soon follow Susie Wiles out the door, MSNOW first reported.

Bauer’s anticipated departure comes after Trump “has grown increasingly frustrated” with her in recent months, according to the outlet. It follows remarks he made over the weekend that he would be making “a few changes” after the bruising midterm elections.

After Bauer departs the White House, she will join a growing list of former high-ranking female Trump officials fired by the president or who left of their own accord. They include former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, former Attorney General Pam Bondi, former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, former National Intelligence Director Tulsi Gabbard, U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberley Guilfoyle, and recently ousted press secretary Katie Zacharia.

A White House official described Bauer as a “valuable part of the team” who would “continue to work in a new role” when reached for comment by The Independent. The official did not elaborate on what the role entailed or why Bauer was leaving her current post.

open image in gallery White House Cabinet secretary Meghan Bauer (right) - a lesser-known official whose influential role acts as the bridge between the president and his Cabinet members - is expected to leave her role as part of the president’s staffing shakeup ( Art in Embassies/Instagram )

Wiles hired Bauer for the role in January 2025, according to a profile on her by the conservative nonprofit Independent Women’s Forum. “It’s such a privilege to work for the ﬁrst female chief of staff ever,” Bauer told the nonprofit. “She inspired me to get up every day and do my best.”

Her role could reportedly be absorbed by Trump’s new White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, who was elevated to the position last week.

Trump has fired or pushed out more than half a dozen high-ranking women from his second administration, most of whom have been replaced by men.

By contrast, his male Cabinet members and agency heads have largely survived scandals and controversies, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and FBI Director Kash Patel – a point commentators were quick to make online.

“Trump only fires women,” reacted one X user.

“Is a single dude going to be fired by him ever? Just one?” said another.

“Another woman. It's quite striking,” someone else posted.

Mike Waltz, the former National Security Adviser, took the fall for Hegseth’s Signalgate scandal, when he inadvertently shared sensitive military information with a journalist in a chat group. The Pentagon chief narrowly avoided impeachment after a vote failed Tuesday.

open image in gallery After Bauer departs the White House, she will join a growing list of former high-ranking female Trump officials fired by the president or who left of their own accord ( Getty )

Patel, meanwhile, was dogged by allegations of excessive drinking at the helm of the FBI, which he has vehemently denied and filed a lawsuit against The Atlantic for publishing the claims. The outlet is standing by its reporting. Elsewhere, Patel was accused of “misuse” of taxpayer funds for “luxury” expenses, including a fleet of BMW vehicles, while jet-setting on “official” business that includes jet ski trips and helicopter tours.

An FBI spokesperson said the allegations were “completely false” at the time.

Men in Trump’s cabinet are “not being held to the same standard” as women, Sarah Matthews, a deputy press secretary in Trump’s first administration, told The Atlantic.

“I’m not saying Kristi Noem and some of these women don’t deserve to be fired,” Matthews said. “But I think some of the men are not being held to the same standard. And it’s a pretty glaring disparity of who he’s willing to fire and who he’s not.”

Noem was fired by Trump after she gave a disastrous performance at a congressional hearing in March.

She was grilled by senators, including Republicans, over a $143 million taxpayer-funded ad campaign she featured in, on horseback, with full hair and makeup. Noem claimed the president was aware of her expensive ad campaign and had signed off on it.

Lawmakers also tore into Noem over her response to the killings of U.S. citizens during an immigration surge in Minnesota, where she called American citizens Alex Pretti and Renee Good “domestic terrorists” after they were shot dead by federal immigration agents.

Miller made the same claim but has since been promoted to the second most powerful position in Washington.

News.title: Hegseth’s group reprimanded for laughing during Veterans Day honoring at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Members of an entourage traveling with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth were publicly called out for laughing and taking selfies during a Veterans Day visit to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery, as reported by CNN.

In the CNN clip, an on-duty guard can be heard issuing a stern warning over the noise: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!"

It remains unclear if those involved will face repercussions.

The cemetery incident comes during a tumultuous week for the defense secretary, who narrowly escaped an impeachment vote in the House of Representatives on Tuesday night. The effort to advance articles of impeachment over unapproved military actions in Iran and the Caribbean was defeated 211–204 after 11 House Democrats failed to cast their votes due to a Washington traffic jam.

The missed vote drew criticism from fellow Democrats and progressive commentators toward the absent members and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

open image in gallery An Army Guard member posted at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier was forced to yell at a group traveling with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after they were caught laughing during a Veterans Day ceremony ( AFP/Getty )

"This is a major Hakeem Jeffries fail," wrote political commentator Krystal Ball on social media. "You could have impeached the war criminal Pete Hegseth but Dems didn't show up to vote."

Progressive journalist Mehdi Hasan added, "Please pick a different Speaker, Dems. Please," while Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed criticized his colleagues on CNN, saying, "You should show up and do your job."

This is a developing story. More to come.

News.title: Watch: Prolific Greggs shoplifter steals more than £2,000 worth of soft drinks from single shop
News.content:
A prolific Greggs shoplifter stole more than £2,000 worth of soft drinks from a single shop.

Tiffany O'Neill, 28, targeted the same Greggs store on Electric Avenue in Brixton, south London.

She pleaded guilty to a total of 80 offences and was handed a 26-week sentence at Croydon Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday (11 November), suspended for 12 months.

In addition to the suspended sentence, a Criminal Behaviour Order was granted, banning her from Brixton town centre and all Greggs stores in the UK for two years.

The Metropolitan Police estimated that officers spent more than 120 hours on this case since O’Neill’s arrest in May.

News.title: This is how the DWP check will bank accounts under new benefit rules
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) will have the power to check the bank accounts of millions of pensioners and benefit claimants under new government powers, it has been announced.

This is part of new benefit fraud rules, with powers created by the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Bill.

According to DWP, the department will share “eligibility indicators” with banks and other financial institutions.

These will be based on “benefit eligibility rules and help institutions identify accounts that may need to be checked by DWP”. It is planned to help ensure people receive the benefits they are entitled to.

The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) will have the power to check the bank accounts of millions of pensioners and benefit claimants under new government powers ( PA Archive )

Financial institutions will then check the information they hold on accounts receiving certain DWP benefit payments.

They will tell DWP when a personal account into which a relevant benefit is paid meets an eligibility indicator. This includes linked accounts.

The account may belong to either a claimant or a non-claimant.

What information will be shared?

Where an eligibility indicator is met, financial institutions will only share limited information with DWP for two reasons:

To help identify incorrect benefit payments To check benefit entitlement.

They may share:

the names of all account holders

details of any accounts you hold, including linked accounts and joint accounts

account numbers

sort codes, if the accounts have these

information about how much money is in the relevant accounts

the date of transactions that took place in another country

It is important to note that DWP cannot log into your online banking or see your account in real time.

Banks and other financial institutions cannot share:

full statements or transactions

how you spend your money

sensitive personal information about your background, such as political opinions or religious beliefs

specific transaction locations

Banks and other financial institutions can be fined if they do share this information.

How DWP collects and uses your information:

DWP will only use the data to help check benefit entitlement, help identify incorrect payments and support any enquiries into those payments, if needed

DWP cannot ask for information that breaks data protection laws

where information is shared with DWP that is not directly relevant to a benefit claimant, it will be destroyed in line with DWP’s Information Management Policy

DWP will not share your personal information with banks or other financial institutions

An independent reviewer will check that DWP, banks and other financial institutions have followed the law, amongst other things. Its reports will be presented to Parliament.

News.title: David Walliams’s former friend Jonathan Ross ‘horrified’ by allegations
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jonathan Ross has said he was “horrified” by the allegations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand, two men he says he was once “friendly” with.

Walliams, 55, has been accused of sexually inappropriate behaviour from a number of women, including two who claimed they were “groomed” by the comedian when they were 15.

The allegations came a day after Brand, 51, was jailed for 10-and-a-half years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

Walliams has denied any wrongdoing and insisted he is “not a sexual predator”, adding he is “devastated” that the allegations, published by The Guardian and ITV News, have been brought against him. His lawyers had taken a case to the High Court to try to stop the allegations being published.

During ITV’s reporting, a photograph resurfaced showing Ross alongside Walliams at an event also attended by one of the women who later accused Walliams of “highly inappropriate” behaviour. Lawyers for Walliams have said he denies behaving inappropriately.

open image in gallery Ross said he had previously been on ‘friendly terms’ with Walliams ( Shutterstock )

In a statement on Tuesday night, Ross, who has appeared on TV shows with Walliams, said: “I am as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation. There was a time in my life when I was on friendly terms with both men, and during that period I was genuinely unaware of their conduct.

“My thoughts are with the many, many women who have bravely come forward.”

The Metropolitan Police confirmed it contacted The Guardian and ITV News to “ensure that any potential victims” are “made aware of how they could report any criminal allegations to police”, after the sexual misconduct claims were made.

open image in gallery David Walliams was named this week as part of an investigation by journalists involving accusations of grooming teenage girls as young as 15 and abusing his position to pursue women ( PA )

In the wake of the allegations, media minister Ian Murray said there is a “cultural problem” in the entertainment industry that needs to be “stamped out”.

He said: “There should be a zero-tolerance approach with support for the brave women, support for whistleblowers, and making sure the industry can clean up its own act.”

Mr Murray added that non-disclosure agreements are a “major part of the problem”.

He said: “If you’re up against a major star such as Russell Brand, it’s very frightening to be able to report that.

“But also, you have to be confident the systems are in place for you to be able to do that confidently. That you’ll be listened to, and then there’ll be action taken.

“In all of these instances, it appears that people are frightened to take on that Goliath, and you can understand why when people are in positions of power, particularly men.

“It’s frightening. It’s career-damaging, career-limiting, if not even career-ending.

“And these are the things that government are wrestling with in terms of how we put the best possible framework in place to support people, but also to make sure the culture changes, so we don’t have to support people because it doesn’t happen in the first place.”

open image in gallery Brand was jailed for 10-and-a-half years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others ( PA )

Bridget Phillipson, equalities minister, paid tribute to the “bravery” of victims who have shared their experiences in recent days.

Speaking in the Commons, she said: “Women and girls should never have to shrink our lives or ambitions because of outdated, misogynistic attitudes, and the appalling testimonies we have heard in recent days underline how much further we have to go.

“I pay tribute to all of the women who have shown such bravery in coming forward and sharing their experiences.”

In light of the allegations, Downing Street said every organisation should “look hard at whether they are doing enough to keep people safe” and take any allegations seriously.

News.title: 911 call released after Ohio State frat pledges set ablaze: ‘They put gasoline on him and lit him on fire’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Police have released a 911 call that reported fraternity pledges being set on fire in Ohio.

​A video of the incident quickly went viral on social media after it was recorded at a gathering of members of an Ohio State University fraternity on Saturday. Authorities are now investigating whether two students left with deep burns during the incident were victims of hazing.

​In a Sunday 911 call obtained by CBS News, a woman can be heard telling a Columbus Division of Police dispatcher about the 35-second video filmed at a gathering linked to the Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity.

​“They set their pledges on fire, and there's a video of it. And I just want to send it in so that something gets done about it,” the caller said. “They put gasoline on him and lit him on fire, and then just kind of stood there and laughed.”

​The caller noted that she saw the video through a sorority group chat and was not there when it was filmed.

open image in gallery Police have released the 911 call reporting that frat pledges at the Ohio State University had been set on fire ( Getty )

​In the audio clip, which was also reviewed by CNN, the caller also detailed the condition of the two men in the video.

​“It’s hard to tell,” she said. “One of them got the fire out pretty, pretty easily, and the other one was stripped naked and still on fire when the video ended.”

​In the clip, a hooded man can be seen with his pants engulfed in flames. He jumps to his feet and lunges at another hooded man, knocking them both to the ground.

​When they stand up, both men's clothes are aflame, though it is unclear whether the second man’s clothes were on fire before they collided. One of them eventually begins rapidly removing their clothing. All the while, a ring of people watches them. Many of them are in the university’s distinctive red and white colors.

​“Oh s***, oh s***, oh s***,” an onlooker can be heard saying.

​Both students have been treated for “moderate” second- and third-degree burns, a Columbus police report states.

​Ben Johnson, a spokesperson for Ohio State University, has confirmed that the Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity has been placed on an interim suspension while it investigates the incident.

open image in gallery An investigation has been launched into the incident by the university (campus pictured here). The Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity has also been placed on an interim suspension ( AFP/Getty )

​“The university is aware of this extremely concerning incident, and the individuals in question are receiving needed medical care," Johnson said. “Ohio State is committed to a safe and healthy environment and expects students and student organizations to uphold that commitment and the university’s values.”

​Steve Mitchell, CEO of the national Sigma Alpha Epsilon, said that the organization is aware of the video and is working with university officials and authorities.

“Sigma Alpha Epsilon holds its collegiate members to high standards of conduct and accountability,” he said. “Behavior that violates these standards has no place in our organization.

​“We are committed to holding those responsible accountable and will take appropriate action based on the findings of the investigation.”

The fraternity has been sanctioned at least seven times since 2001, according to The Lantern, which examined its own previous reporting and archives.

Fraternity culture has become the subject of a national debate following the Cornell 7 case, which involved a woman accusing seven male members of Cornell University’s Chi Phi chapter of gang-rape.

The unnamed woman says the incident occurred while she was intoxicated with alcohol and ketamine. The men accused in the case have denied the allegations.

The Independent has contacted Columbus police for comment.

News.title: Ebola could be raging in DRC for another year, expert warns
News.content:
The Ebola epidemic currently raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo could last at least another year, a leading UK epidemiologist has warned.

Experts have struggled to contain the current outbreak since the first cases of the rare Bundibugyo strain of the disease were reported in May.

There have so far been almost 11,000 cases including 5,000 deaths, making it the second largest outbreak in history, after the devastating West Africa epidemic of 2014-16. Cases have also been reported in Nigeria and Kenya, although transmission has not been widespread.

The outbreak is taking place across a vast area of DRC - North Kivu and Ituri - where conflict and widespread mistrust of authorities, including health workers, have hampered the response.

Neil Ferguson, professor of epidemiology at Imperial College, London, told a press briefing that at the current rate of disease spread that the epidemic could still be ongoing at the end of next year.

“Controlling Ebola outbreaks takes a long time so it is highly likely we’ll still be seeing transmission in a year’s time,” he said.

“We’re ticking over at about 70 confirmed cases a day at the moment and that’s almost certainly quite a significant underestimate of the true number of infections,” said Prof Ferguson, who rose to prominence at the beginning of the Covid pandemic when he advised government on the likely trajectory of the outbreak.

News.title: Many more cattle ranch workers infected with H5N1 than reported, says US farming union
News.content:
Far more US farm workers are infected with bird flu than officially reported, with some suffering “very severe” symptoms, according to the country’s largest farming union.

H5N1 is currently spreading rapidly across US cattle farms in dozens of US states.

Officially, just three people have been diagnosed with the virus in the past month, all following close contact with infected cows.

In total, 73 people in the US have been officially been recorded as infected with H5N1 since 2024, mostly dairy farm workers. Three have died.

But United Farm Unions (UFU), which represents thousands of workers across the US, said it was aware of many more farmers experiencing symptoms consistent with H5N1 who had not been tested.

“We have now connected with a number of workers and have confirmed that more workers are sick with avian flu symptoms who have not been tested,” the UFU wrote on X.

Symptoms range from “very mild to very severe”, the post added, including mild upper respiratory infections and conjunctivitis to severe flu-like symptoms, bone pain, persistent coughing and high fever.

The ongoing outbreak is worrying disease experts.

“H5N1 is not a virus to be casual about- or to let spread unchecked, given every mutation is like the virus buying a lottery ticket to acquire human-to-human transmission,” said Dr Devi Sridhar, a public health researcher at the University of Edinburgh.

Referring to the statement by the UFU, Professor Francois Balloux, director of the UCL Genetics Institute, added: “The most puzzling aspect to me is not even the incompetence and paralysis of the authorities but the resignation and fatalism. It feels like reading some chronicle by a mediaeval peasant.”

Of the roughly 1,000 people infected with H5N1 since the virus was first identified in the late 1990s, almost half have died. However, most historical cases have resulted from contact with wild birds, while the strain circulating in cattle, known as genotype B.12, is thought to cause much milder illness.

Concerns have nevertheless grown after an unidentified farm worker in Washington state died in late October from the cattle-derived H5N1 strain, raising questions about whether the virus may have mutated.

The Trump administration has been heavily criticised for allowing bird flu to run rampant through America’s wild and domestic animals, putting people at risk.

Deep cuts to the federal agencies responsible for managing human and animal health, the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and the Department of Agriculture (USDA), have resulted in the scaling down of surveillance and testing programmes amongst both livestock and farm workers.

Every infection, animal or human, raises the chance the virus could mutate and eventually gain the ability to spread between people – something which experts have long warned could trigger the next pandemic.

As flu season begins, experts are concerned a dairy worker infected with ordinary seasonal flu could catch H5N1 at the same time, and the two viruses could mix to create a new, more dangerous strain that could spread between people – a phenomenon known as “reassortment.”

“It is clear that workers are not being informed of the risks of handling sick cattle and infected milk. They are being given no information on flu shots or avian flu testing,” the UFU said.

Estimates suggest that over half of the 150,000-strong dairy workforce in the US are immigrant or undocumented workers, driven in part by high demand for intensive year-round labour and a lack of domestic applicants.

Many are reportedly worried about coming forward for testing over fears they will come into contact with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the federal agency emboldened under Trump, which has been tasked with deporting one million immigrants every year.

Yakima Valley, the region of Washington State where the three recent H5N1 cases have been reported and where the virus is spreading through dozens of dairy herds, is in the midst of an ICE crackdown.

News.title: Young women must ensure they are vaccinated as measles cases surge, doctors say
News.content:
But the dangers for pregnant women, say experts, are often ignored.

There has been relatively little data on maternal and infant measles deaths related to pregnancy in the West since the late 1960s, after the MMR vaccine was introduced and case numbers fell significantly.

Pregnant women are known, however, to be much more vulnerable to illness from measles than others, as the mother’s body, to stop it from rejecting the pregnancy, shifts its immune response significantly and becomes more susceptible to disease.

Between 2000 and 2025, 36 children and adults died from measles or related infections in England and Wales, according to NHS data, but whether or not any of those people were pregnant has not been made public.

“Given the recurrence of measles outbreaks and the number of cases occurring in adults, there may be value in better understanding the impact of measles infection during pregnancy in the UK,” Kirsty Le Doare, professor of vaccinology and immunology at City St George’s, told The Telegraph.

One study by the US CDC conducted in Namibia looked at 55 unvaccinated women who contracted measles during their pregnancies.

Of them, 53 required hospitalisation for complications arising from the virus, ranging from severe diarrhoea, pneumonia, and encephalitis (swelling of the brain).

Another meta-analysis, published in The Lancet in 2018, analysed data from 19 academic papers from countries including France, Germany, and the UK that had studied pregnancy-related measles between 1941 and 2012.

Of 420 pregnancy-related measles cases, 18 deaths occurred, mostly from pneumonia.

“Measles in pregnancy is serious and can cause stillbirth, premature labour and miscarriage,” the NHS website reads. “There is no medical treatment for measles; MMR vaccination is the best protection against becoming seriously unwell,” it adds.

“We know that if you catch measles during pregnancy, you are very likely to end up in hospital,” Professor Helen Bedford, a professor of children’s health at Great Ormond Street Hospital, told The Telegraph.

“You are much more likely to have pneumonia, and there are higher rates of encephalitis. These are all complications that can happen in adults with measles, but they do seem to occur at much higher rates during pregnancy,” said Prof Bedford.

News.title: Gaza floods are an “immediate humanitarian emergency”, warns Trump’s Board of Peace
News.content:
Donald Trump’s Board of Peace has accused Israel of an “insufficient” response to deadly floods that have hit the Gaza Strip.

In a rare statement, the US-led body, charged with ending war in Gaza and rebuilding the Strip, called on Israel “to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies”.

“The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” they said on Monday.

The Board has been pushing Israel for at least a month to speed up its “winterisation” policies so that residents in Gaza are better able to withstand the coldest months of the year.

The statement followed a weekend of torrential rain and winds that battered the decimated territory’s displacement camps, causing widespread flooding, landslides and several deaths.

A mother and her three young children were killed when a sand dune collapsed onto their tent in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. The children, aged four, five and eight died on Sunday. Their mother also suffocated under the sand.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

Sports.title: Tuchel committed to England but keen on club return in future
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel revealed he has no release clause in his England contract but is committed to leading them until Euro 2028 at least - even if a big club comes calling.

The Three Lions boss was asked the question in relation to incoming-Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino having a £7m buyout clause in his deal with the USA.

In response to the written media, Tuchel said: "No release clause. And there's no intention. I signed the contract - I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business."

Tuchel was then asked if there was "zero chance" he would leave England if a big club came in for him between now and the 2028 Euros. He said: "Yeah, I would say so."

Speaking about The FA's commitment to him after the World Cup exit, Tuchel added: "They made it very early in the World Cup. Even before the clause was activated, they just made it very clear. And it comes from a place of trust and that's what you look for as a coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel said he will field a strong side against Croatia in a 'beautiful' night for Harry Kane as he presents the Ballon d'Or to the England fans

"I love my group of players, I love my staff and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things.

"It's a lot, and I know how to appreciate it a lot, so it's in a good place, I'm in a good place. And like I said, I love the players.

"I miss my players and I miss my team and I miss the 50 matches that I'm not involved in in a year, but I'm desperate to win the Nations League and I'm desperate to play and try to win the Euros."

Asked if he plans to return to club management after England, Tuchel said: "Yeah, definitely. I miss the 50 matches, like I said. I miss these two minutes when everything is done. You go out the two minutes before the whistle goes, it's like the best two minutes, everything is done and you're in a full stadium, lights are on and you're just so excited and you're part of it.

"That's actually the two minutes where I kind of a little bit realise how lucky and how grateful I am and then the whistle goes and you're just in the tunnel again and you're trying to win the game for your team. And you do that every four days."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Kane was applauded by the media for his Ballon d'Or success as he entered Wednesday's press conference ahead of the Nations League game against Croatia

Tuchel also suggested that the FA could make a bid to bring the Nations League finals to England - something he hopes will happen.

He said: "We don't know where the final of the Nations League will be yet. The FA has an option to put their hat in the ring.

"We've talked before about this group of players struggling to bring their training performances to the field other England managers have spoken about the shirt being heavy.

"It's [the Euros] going to be a home tournament, the pressures of that tournament will be unique.

"It's almost like a dress rehearsal, playing in front of your own fans. Nations League helps in general for us. It would be exciting, it would be nice to have it here. First of all, we need to reach the final."

Sports.title: Australia dredge up past blunders as England learn from theirs
Sports.content:
As Australia dredge up the past, England seem determined to learn from theirs.

The build-up to this run of white-ball matches between the Ashes rivals, which starts with the first ODI in Perth on Friday, has been dominated by Usman Khawaja's claims in his autobiography about the 2018 Australia ball-tampering scandal in South Africa.

Khawaja says every member of the Baggy Greens team back then knew in advance about the plot to alter the condition of the ball in Cape Town and that sandpaper had even been used in the previous Test of that series against the Proteas, in Gqeberha.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia's Usman Khawaja has made extraordinary claims in his autobiography, saying the entire Australia dressing room knew about plans to tamper with the ball in South Africa in 2018

Mitchell Starc, one of the Australia bowlers eight years ago and still going strong now, disputes, as he always has, that he was aware of the scheme. This who-knew-what-and-who-didn't affair could rumble on for a while. There may never be a resolution.

England out to atone for last year's Ashes errors

Watching this unfold, presumably with more than a hint of glee, are England, who have returned to the scene of their own cricketing crime last winter. Not ball-tampering, of course, but a complete lack of acceptable preparation for a series as big as The Ashes.

Brendon McCullum was Test coach at that point - not now, having being sacked in July as the 4-1 Ashes debacle was followed by a 2-1 series defeat at home to his native New Zealand - and presided over a shabby lead-in to the first Test.

The sole warm-up was an intra-squad fixture on a docile deck at Lilac Hill which in no way teed the team up for the bouncy nature of the Optus Stadium surface they came up against across Perth in the Ashes opener. The result? England went down in flames.

Image: Ollie Pope trudges off after being dismissed during the 4-1 Ashes battering

A game they looked destined to win they ended up losing inside two days after a remarkable batting collapse induced by the unwise decision to continually drive on the up.

Even more unwise was not talking about dismissals driving on the up in between their defeat in Perth and the loss in the day-night game in Brisbane that followed.

After a pink-ball pummelling at The Gabba, the series was almost beyond them. When they retuned from a beach break in Noosa, which some observers claim was drink-laden, and they then lost in Adelaide, the series was beyond them. Ashes over.

This, though, might be a new England - with the same guy as coach in Brendon McCullum and a white-ball captain in Harry Book eager to bounce back from the chastening trip a year ago.

Michael Atherton told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast: "I think the Ashes was a bit of a wake-up call for players like Brook so he will come to this tour now a bit older and a bit wiser - and hopefully hurting to a degree where England are motivated to put on a show."

Image: Brendon McCullum remains England white-ball coach but lost the Test job last summer

Warm-up game shows change of approach from England

The laid-back McCullum was kept on as limited-overs head coach after losing the Test job and, bar a sticky tri-series in the subcontinent when they fluffed their lines with the ball in run chases versus Pakistan and Sri Lanka, things have been going swimmingly.

Three straight bilateral 50-over series wins and also top spot in the T20 rankings, first after routing India 4-0 in July and then again by sweeping Sri Lanka 3-0 in September.

England are, in the main, making shrewd calls on the field through Brook and shrewd calls off them, too, including the choice to play a proper warm-up ahead of the Australia ODIs - last Saturday's 92-run win over Western Australia at The WACA.

Image: England played a proper warm-up game ahead of the ODI series against Australia, unlike a year ago on the Ashes tour

That tune-up match is something that will be replicated ahead of the three-Test series in South Africa from December 17 as Joe Root's red-ball squad play a Cricket South Africa XI in Durban, while a practice game is also pencilled in when they return to Australia in March for the 150th anniversary Test in Melbourne.

On how better prepared they are for Friday's outing at the Optus than they were last November, captain Brook said: "The conditions [at the WACA] always feel a lot closer than Lilac Hill. The bounce, the carry, the pace of the pitch - it's miles away from what Lilac Hill offered us. Thankfully we got the opportunity to play there.

"The key is to try and be one of the fittest and strongest sides in the world. You can never guarantee [winning] but you can guarantee the off-field preparation can be a lot better."

Image: England have won their last three bilateral ODI series under captain Harry Brook but failed to make the final of the recent tri-series in Pakistan

Australia build-up dominated by 'Sandpapergate'

Australia's off-field preparations have surely been disrupted by Khawaja's blockbuster declarations, even if all but one of the men who played for the Baggy Greens in that Cape Town Test eight years ago are not involved in the three ODIs and five T20s.

Mitchell Marsh is the sole figure from the Newlands drama who will be around. He is captaining Australia against England and will no doubt be heavily quizzed on what he did or did not know about Cameron Bancroft's use of sandpaper on the ball.

Starc and fellow seam-bowling stalwarts (and fellow 'Sandpapergate' Test players, for that matter) Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins have been rested from the England white-ball contests - Starc has already retired from international T20s anyway.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia fast bowler Mitchell Starc responds to Khawaja's claims about 'Sandpapergate'

You sense Australia will miss them in the ODIs against a strong touring team, with the pace bowling attack looking a little raw in their absence. You also sense that their names will be mentioned a lot in the wake of Khawaja's headline-making claims.

Starc, Hazlewood and Cummins, along with spin bowler Nathan Lyon, issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any prior knowledge of the ball-tampering.

Will they feel compelled to release another official one, either as a group or individually, or has all their talking been done?

What is clear is that England have a chance to make a statement in the ODIs, by proverbially kicking Australia when they are down. Down because of the 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa and down because of 'Sandpapergate' rearing its head again.

We're quite young and inexperienced in many ways, so the more experiences we have on different surfaces, different situations in games, the more we'll learn, develop and become a more rounded team. We've come from Pakistan. We've learned a huge amount there. Over the course of this series, we're going to have to be really clear on how we want to get the best out of these three games.

Atherton added: "When England arrived a year ago, all the guns were trained on them, the classic Pommie-bashing.

"Average Joe" Root, never got a Test hundred here. Pictures of the 'New Zealand-born, whining' Ben Stokes coming through the airport. All the usual focus on England.

"Now the focus is on the home team - and for an Englishman there is no better time to be in Australia than when the Australian team are tearing themselves apart, as they seem to be doing right now."

Sports.title: Kildunne: It's 'harsh' to say England dropped me - 'My role just changed'
Sports.content:
England Red Roses World Cup winner Ellie Kildunne has said it is "harsh" to say she was dropped during their recent tour of North America, claiming she was just given a "different role."

The 27-year-old, who was named 2024's World Player of the Year and finished second to Rory McIlroy as 2025's BBC Sports Personality of the Year, played a starring role as the Red Roses clinched World Cup glory on home soil last year.

But during 2026's Global WXV series, full-back Kildunne was dropped from the starting side following defeat to Canada in Toronto - a first Red Roses loss for four years and 41 Tests.

Head coach John Mitchell revealed at the time Kildunne was "going through a difficult period" in the search for consistency.

Despite the Red Roses losing again to Canada in Ottawa, Kildunne remained on the bench for England's closing Test and emphatic victory over the USA.

"I think the word 'dropped' is probably a bit harsh," Kildunne said on Wednesday. "I still played the game, I was still part of the team, I still came on the pitch, so in no way have I been dropped. I've just been given a different role.

Image: Kildunne - a star of England's 2025 World Cup win - was dropped to the bench after a first Red Roses defeat for four years

"Of course, finding depth in the team is very important and I've been fortunate to play a lot of rugby and have a lot of minutes under my belt.

"People are going to say whatever they want to say because everyone wants a headline and everyone wants the clickbait that they're going to read.

"I saw 'Kildunne's been dropped' and I was like: 'I'm still in America, so obviously I've not been dropped'."

Upon removing her from the starting side last month, Mitchell highlighted form, consistency and behaviours.

He said: "Well, firstly it's undisputed that she adds huge value. She's just going through a difficult period at the moment. It's important for us to help her through that.

"She wants to become consistent as well and she'll get back. It's also important to create competition and to recognise that you have to become more consistent, especially when you're competing in the Red Roses.

"So it's really important to reinforce the behaviours that we think are necessary to our game. And that goes for everyone."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head coach John Mitchell explains why Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench for the third and final Test against Canada as the Red Roses look to bounce back from their first defeat in four years.

For Kildunne, who will make her debut for Bristol Bears in the Premiership Women's Rugby next week following an acrimonious departure from Harlequins, she says her main learning from 2026 is to "block out the noise."

"What's really been a learning point from the tour, away from rugby, is being able to block out that noise," she said. "I've been so used to the positive comments throughout my career and as soon as you don't score one try, people seem to be against you.

"I want to be a consistent player and that might not always look like scoring. Whether for the past few years I've consistently scored, it doesn't mean that I've played badly if I haven't scored.

"That's what people have seen and rated me on: the line-breaks and the tries, but the game doesn't work like that. Everyone's evolving and getting better.

"I'm happy with my performances this year. I've had to learn a lot as a player and work out a lot. Ultimately, I don't get the space that I once had so I can't always make the 60-metre line breaks.

Image: Kildunne says her main learning from 2026 is to 'block out the noise' after much scrutiny

"I think I'm very good at balancing what I'm doing, whether it's media or training and how to do them. But I guess from the outside, people always think that you don't have the balance right.

"I think as long as you know that you're a rugby player and that's the thing that you need to focus on and you're true to that, then there should be never anything to question. But I feel like externals love to find something that could potentially be wrong.

"I've probably had that period of working it out and I'm definitely in a space now where you do have to say no to things."

Sports.title: Jones: Japan aiming to 'make Twickenham sky fall in on distracted England'
Sports.content:
Former England head coach Eddie Jones has said his Japan side are aiming to "make the Twickenham sky fall in on" Steve Borthwick's "distracted" charges in Saturday's Nations Championship Test.

Jones, who oversaw England between 2016 and 2022, before being dismissed a year before the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France after a calendar year saw just five victories and England fans booing the side following defeat to South Africa.

The 66-year-old has since returned to Australia for an ill-fated and short second reign which ended in a first-ever World Cup pool stage exit for the Wallabies, and then returned as Japan head coach in 2024.

Ahead of his Brave Blossoms side facing England at Twickenham on Saturday, Jones has sought to stoke the flames.

"We're massive underdogs," Jones told the BBC. "We've got to find a way to disrupt an England side that's looking at New Zealand next week [Saturday November 21] and sometimes may be a little bit distracted.

"Our opportunity is to get in there, cause some havoc, cause some chaos, put off their game, get the crowd booing. Then the sky starts to come in on Twickenham and you never know what can happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maro Itoje gives a passionate defence of Steve Borthwick after England's defeat of Australia at Twickenham

"We've seen it happen with Italy and other countries [Italians beat England for first time in March].

"The noise does get to the team and it can be pretty loud in England. You've got a lot of newspapers, a lot of media, probably more than any other country in the world.

"Sometimes that can weigh down on the players and it's the job of the leadership to get the players thinking straight.

"Steve [Borthwick] is an outstanding coach and a very intelligent man, and a really good coach. So I've got the highest respect for him."

England's Nations Championship fixtures and results South Africa 45-21 England July 4 Fiji 8-73 England July 11 Argentina 24-31 England July 18 England 45-22 Australia November 8 England vs Japan Saturday, November 14 (4.40pm) England vs New Zealand Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie George told Sky Sports England's players were hurt by the 'shocking' report of a rift with Borthwick

Jones plays down Pollock's impact on the wing - 'Wouldn't read much into it'

England are entering Saturday's Test off the back of a much-needed, morale-boosting 45-22 victory over Australia in the Nations Championship.

In a week when Borthwick came under intense scrutiny following newspaper reports of a summer rift with his England squad - claims denied by Jamie George to Sky Sports - England responded with a seven-try performance and record point haul against Australia.

Back-row Henry Pollock also starred out of position on the wing for 40 minutes, having emerged at half-time to score two tries en route to victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Borthwick praises 'excellent' Henry Pollock after a standout performance on the wing for England against Australia

Jones was quick to play down Pollock's exploits, however.

"I wouldn't look too much into it," Jones added. "Everyone was licking the ice cream on Sunday. They were on the front foot, everyone's lining up to run the ball, there's no pressure in the game.

"He's a fast back-rower, he got the ball in space and he's a talented player, there's no doubt about it, but you couldn't read into it any more than that."

Sports.title: Hussain calls 'Sandpapergate' affair a 'complete mess'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain has called the Australia 'Sandpapergate' affair and its subsequent explosive fallout a "complete mess".

The 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, in which Australia's Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera trying to use sandpaper on the ball in order to make it swing, has been catapulted back into the spotlight following the release of Usman Khawaja's book.

Former Baggy Greens batter Khawaja, who played in that infamous Cape Town Test, claims the entire team knew about the scheme and not just those banned, in Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and David Warner, who was deemed the architect.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Khawaja's claims have come in his recently released autobiography 'Sabr'

Khawaja also said he was not quizzed at the time by Cricket Australia despite sitting next to Bancroft in the Newlands dressing room and that he urged the team to come clean and take collective responsibility before being talked out of it by Smith.

Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, former England captain Hussain said: "I think it's a complete mess.

"Let's be honest, for the history of the game, people have been trying to work out what to do with cricket balls to make it swing more, whether it be mints, sweets, throwing the ball to the ground on the bounce, Vaseline, dirt in pocket, whatever it might be.

"[But] how a side thought it was okay to take sandpaper out, how no one before that in a meeting went, 'I don't think this is okay, I don't think we're doing the right thing', how they thought they were going to get away with it with all the cameras around [I don't know].

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In 2018, footage emerged of Australia opener Cameron Bancroft using a foreign object to alter the condition of the ball against South Africa, later revealed to be sandpaper

"Then to lie about it after and for Cricket Australia not to speak to every player, not to speak to Khawaja who was sitting next to Bancroft. It just feels like a right mess.

"The team, the baggy green, the mateship and all that stuff - that was what playing Australia was like, so for an Australian team to say, 'no, it's just those three' when it was never going to be just those three [is surprising]."

'Worst of both worlds from Cricket Australia'

Hussain's fellow analyst, Michael Atherton, is currently in Australia ahead of England's white-ball tour of the country, which begins with the first ODI in Perth on Friday (3.30am UK time).

Atherton will attend what he anticipates being a "circus" of a press conference on Thursday as Australia white-ball captain Mitchell Marsh - the only player to have figured in the Newlands Test in 2018 in the hosts' squad to tackle England - fronts up.

Usual ODI skipper Pat Cummins has been rested, along with Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, all three of whom were involved in the sandpaper Test and released a joint statement back in 2021, with spinner Nathan Lyon, denying prior knowledge of the plot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia fast bowler Mitchell Starc denies any prior knowledge of the sandpaper use at Newlands

Sky Sports pundit Atherton was critical of Cricket Australia's handling of the situation eight years ago, saying it was always "going to come back to haunt them".

Smith and Warrner were banned for a year after 'Sandpapergate' with Bancroft suspended for nine months.

Atherton, who does not see a need for a new investigation to be opened following Khawaja's claims, said: "It was almost like the sandpaper was the straw that broke the camel's back.

"It was on the back of the team having become, and Khawaja talks about it in his book, slightly out of control, a bit unlikable and with a kind of win-at-all costs mentality.

"Then it was the worst of both worlds.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Australia David Warner took to his Instagram to back Khawaja's claims the entire team knew about 2018 ball-tampering plan (credit: @davidwarner31)

"They handed down unbelievably heavy sanctions - I thought hard-to-justify sanctions - and left three players to take the rap. But it left questions unanswered, left the door open for it to come back to haunt them, which it is doing now.

"It was eight years ago and there will be a weariness around the story eventually, because it's all over every newspaper, podcast, whatever.

"But I do think the particular point about not having people's backs is the thing causing the most disquiet [in the Australia public] and will rumble on for a while yet."

Atherton: Cracks in the Australia team

Australia have also toiled on the field, losing 2-1 in South Africa in their first Test series in the country since the ball-tampering scandal, with the out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne now dropped for the impending home clashes with New Zealand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Journalist Martin Samuel explains what impact Khawaja's book could have on next summer's Ashes series in England

Amid a relentless Test calendar that then features a five-match assignment in India, the day-night 150th anniversary Test against England in Melbourne in March, and an away Ashes series in June and July, Atherton feels the Baggy Greens are in a tough spot.

He added: "The schedule is brutal and unforgiving and already there's cracks in that team.

"It doesn't feel as though the team is robust enough to get through this period.

"This [the ball-tampering claims] is adding a little bit more fuel to the fire."

Ferguson has long admired Pochettino and often had long conversations with the former Spurs boss following his matches against United.

The pair were pictured at a Mayfair restaurant in May 2016 amid speculation about Pochettino, then Spurs head coach, taking over from Louis van Gaal at Old Trafford. United subsequently chose to appoint Jose Mourinho.

It is understood Pochettino loves his job with the USA but feels he cannot say no to United.

Sports.title: Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper
Sports.content:
A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino.

If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”.

The complaint, which has been seen by the Guardian and is supported by a number of documents, claims an individual “performed domestic work exclusively for Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his wife, Leena Infantino, at their Miami residence, while receiving compensation or benefits through a Fifa-affiliated entity”, and argues that “senior leadership, acting in their official capacity and on behalf of Fifa, have abused the entity’s tax-exemption status”.

Quick Guide How do I 

The complaint goes on to argue: “If organisational funds or resources were used to pay for services benefiting a leader’s household, the arrangement raises serious questions about private benefit, financial reporting, compensation, and governance. The materials also raise questions about the accuracy of representations in employment, payroll, tax, and immigration records. We ask the agencies to investigate the underlying records and determine what occurred.” The IRS has been approached for comment.

The news comes as Fifa’s activities, and specifically Infantino’s involvement in the failed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme and his relationship with the Trump White House, are to come under intensified scrutiny from Democratic politicians in the US after the “blue wave” at the midterm elections. A spokesperson for the ranking member of the House judiciary committee, representative Jamie Raskin, said the committee had not requested documents related to the housekeeper but was “looking closely at those developments”.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “Matters related to the Fifa president’s personal and home life are private; however, for the avoidance of any doubt, the costs of any domestic staff are met by the Fifa president personally.”

The complaint, if taken up, would probably take months to complete and commonly the results of IRS investigations are not published. Any action taken as a result, however, would be in the public domain. The complaint was submitted by the Washington DC lawyer Abed Ayoub, who works in immigration law and has served as the national executive director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC). Last year the ADC was part of the campaign Game Over Israel, which called for Israeli football teams to be banned from international competition.

Fifa said: “We urge the media to act responsibly. As Fifa stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president. Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading Fifa will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.”

Infantino has been described by his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, as a “dictator” who “no longer knows any borders”. Blatter, Fifa’s president for 17 years before resigning amid a corruption scandal at the organisation, made the remarks in an interview with the German magazine Der Spiegel. He criticised the FFE scheme, the Fifa peace prize and, most significantly in his opinion, the overturning of Folarin Balogun’s suspension for a red card during the World Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Fifa is suffering,” Blatter said. “It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded.” He described the peace prize as “embarrassing”, saying: “Why would he do something like that? Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards?”

In assessing the FFE scheme, which was abandoned after an international outcry, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this.” He described the Balogun controversy as “the worst”, saying: “Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”

FIfa has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Manchester United reach framework deal with Pochettino before settling Carrick’s fate
Sports.content:
Manchester United have a framework agreement with Mauricio Pochettino for him to become their head coach if Michael Carrick is sacked. Carrick is expected to be fired in line with the recommendation from Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Pochettino is the US men’s national team head coach and in August signed a contract to 2030 but he wants the United job after managing in the Premier League with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

Wilcox and Berrada are meeting Ratcliffe in Monaco, where the minority owner will be informed that Carrick should lose his job. Ratcliffe controls United’s sporting policy.

There is a growing sense among United players that Carrick will be sacked, with their expectation being that Pochettino will replace him.

A United board meeting is scheduled for Wednesday at which one or more of the six Glazer siblings, who are the majority owners, will be represented. There is an expectation within the executive and in Carrick’s camp that the sacking will be ratified there and that an announcement will follow.

Pochettino’s contract contains a release clause of about $10m (£7.5m), although the compensation United would have to pay will be higher if the Argentinian brings his own staff, including his longtime assistant and confidant Jesús Pérez, who has worked with Pochettino for 16 years.

Pochettino is due to take charge of the US in Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday in Miami and Cincinnati respectively, their first competitive fixtures of the 2030 World Cup qualifying cycle.

The US cancelled player media access on Wednesday, citing Veterans Day for changing a schedule released five days ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Carrick has overseen a disastrous start to United’s season which has the club in the relegation zone. The 45-year-old has won only one game in the league, against Ipswich in August, and three in all competitions. United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton in September.

Meanwhile, Marcus Rashford is recovering from a groin injury that has ruled him out since he came off during last month’s 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid. United are targeting the trip to Liverpool on Sunday week for the forward’s return, after he saw a specialist in Dublin last week and embarked on a tailored rehabilitation programme. The problem is related to a hip injury Rashford sustained at the World Cup this summer.

Sports.title: ‘I’ve had to prove people wrong’: Kane still striving before record England cap
Sports.content:
Harry Kane says he still feels a pressure to prove his worth, even as he prepares to become England’s most capped men’s player, as he outlined his determination to set records that will stand for years.

The captain will make his 126th appearance against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night, moving him ahead of Peter Shilton on the all-time list. Kane is England’s record goalscorer with 91, comfortably clear of Wayne Rooney, who retired with 53.

Kane will be presented with a memento of his historic cap by Shilton before kick-off against Croatia. Shilton has held the record since 1990 when he finished his 20-year career. Kane’s achievement of winning the Ballon d’Or last month will also be recognised.

“I don’t think it will ever leave me,” Kane said, when asked whether he continued to have points to prove. “It’s probably part of what makes me push myself to the limits that I do because in football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has.

“Whether it’s noise from the outside, from media or the fans … it just helps motivate me to realise there’s a lot more to achieve. My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more … if I could have just done that or done that. I want to make sure I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that whenever that day does come, I can say I’ve done everything possible. And I can sleep well at night.”

The 33-year-old Kane is conscious that two of his younger England teammates have won a significant number of caps. Declan Rice has 80 at the age of 27; Jude Bellingham 60 at 23. “I’ll try and give them a good number to catch,” Kane said. “The goal record, of course, is going to be one that’s difficult to beat for a while.

“I’ve spoken about leading by example and pushing a lot of these younger players. It’s by setting standards, being available every time, getting the caps and scoring the goals. That should help motivate the younger players. If I was younger and I had a player in front of me doing what I was doing, I know that would push me to think: ‘OK, I can score those goals, I can win the Ballon d’Or, I can break the cap record.’ Whilst I’m in this place, it is to try and set these records as high as I can and one day look back to see if anyone can catch them.”

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane receives the Ballon d'Or in London. Photograph: Franck Fife/AFP/Getty Images

Kane has been doubted at numerous points of his career, starting when he was released by Arsenal as an eight-year-old. He had difficult loans from Tottenham to Norwich and Leicester in 2012-13 and there were the one-season wonder jibes after his breakthrough campaign for Spurs and England in 2014-15.

Kane has been ridiculed for setting lofty targets. Such as in 2017 when he said he wanted to replicate the numbers of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. When he stated his ambition to win the 2018 World Cup Golden Boot. Or when he stood on the verge of his 100th England cap in September 2024 with 66 goals and said he wanted to score 100. There were questions about his place in the team after Euro 2024 when his performances were underwhelming and he was substituted in the final. Every time, he answered back.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It’s just my mindset,” Kane said. “Because I’ve had to prove people wrong my whole career. From early academy days proving coaches wrong, proving scouts wrong – it has just been installed in me. If someone tells me I can’t do something it motivates me more to do it.

“When you look at all the great athletes, I’ve spoken before about Tom Brady [the NFL icon] and it’s that unwavering mentality to be the best. Maybe with me, because I’m a calm person and you don’t see … like, the ego of some of these great players and I’m a bit more relaxed … but it doesn’t mean I don’t want it as much as everyone else. That I don’t put in the work and drive myself and everyone around me to be the best.

“Maybe getting released that early [by Arsenal] and proving them wrong and then maybe proving [wrong] my early coaches at Tottenham, who I wasn’t playing as much [under]. The loan moves that didn’t go well. Same thing. I’m going to show them.”

Kane brought up surely the lowest individual moment of his England career – the penalty miss against France in the 2-1 World Cup quarter-final defeat in 2022. “That was really tough but again it was the way I bounced back,” he said. “And even the fact I scored the next 30 [actually 31] penalties of my career. I changed the technique a little bit and it made me improve. There have been a lot of low points but maybe they are things that have helped me get to where I am now.”

Sports.title: Danny Kelly, football broadcaster and renowned editor, dies aged 69
Sports.content:
The journalist and broadcaster Danny Kelly, who helped define coverage of music and football in the UK for a generation, has died at the age of 69.

Kelly edited the NME and Q magazine, and launched the Football 365 website before going on to be a presenter and pundit on the BBC and TalkSport. He had been receiving treatment for oesophageal cancer.

Tributes were led by Kelly’s longstanding broadcast partner Danny Baker. “My great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew, Danny Kelly, died yesterday afternoon,” Baker wrote on social media, the pair having worked together on any number of radio, TV shows and podcasts. “I cannot believe I will never hear his voice again.”

Tottenham Hotspur paid emotional tribute to Kelly, a lifelong Spurs fan. A statement said: “The entire Tottenham family mourns the loss of one of our own, broadcasting legend Danny Kelly. Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time.”

TalkSport, for which Kelly worked as a presenter for nearly two decades, said it was “heartbroken” by the news. “A cherished part of TalkSport for so many years, Danny brought extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves,” the station said. “His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him.”

Another broadcaster, the former Sky Sports host Richard Keys, said Kelly “was all of the things – and more – being said about him – ‘warm, witty and knowledgable’”.

View image in fullscreen Danny Kelly at the launch of the Football365 website in 1998. Photograph: Patrick Barth/Shutterstock

Kelly was born in north London in 1956 and first made his name writing about music. He began contributing to the NME in his 20s and went on to edit the agenda-setting weekly newspaper at the end of the 1980s. From there he took charge of the top-selling music monthly Q magazine, where he was named British magazine editor of the year.

Manic Street Preachers paid tribute to “a brilliant broadcaster-writer-ideas factory. Danny was editor of the NME when we first started getting press, a wonderful man, his musical knowledge was vast and deep, his radio voice has been part of our lives for so long … We will all miss him.”

In the second half of the 1990s, Kelly threw himself into the nascent world of digital media and launched Football365, which became one of the leading online voices on the sport. In the noughties, he spotted another development – podcasts – and launched the Game, a weekly football podcast, for the Times.

Over the past 15 years Kelly became best known as a radio presenter and podcast host, including presenting the Tottenham-focused show View from The Lane. Paying tribute to “our host, our leader” on its X account, the View from the Lane said: “We all loved him as much as he loved Spurs.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel keeps laser focus on ‘unfinished business’ with England
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel will not be going anywhere before Euro 2028. Mauricio Pochettino is expected to leave his role as the USA men’s head coach to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, but Tuchel has not lost his passion for international football and has revealed he did not insert a release clause when he extended his deal as England’s manager this year.

It will not matter whether there is an approach from a big club before the next tournament. United can pay about £7m to get Pochettino out of his deal, but the Football Association does not have to worry about being forced to let Tuchel go. “There’s no intention [of leaving],” Tuchel said. “I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”

Tuchel, a Champions League winner with Chelsea in 2021, did not rule out a return to club management one day. He admitted to missing “the 50 matches” a season, “these two minutes when everything is done, before the whistle goes … it’s like the best two minutes”. But while he loves the daily grind, he added there were downsides to playing every four days and there was a twinkle in his eye when he was asked about potentially staying with England beyond the European Championship.

“I am open to everything,” he said, perhaps reflecting that it is not so long ago that people were calling for his head after England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina.

The mood has improved. Tuchel sounds energised after England’s bright start to their Nations League campaign. His contract contains a performance-related clause that would have allowed the FA to sack him had England underperformed at the World Cup, but Tuchel has support from Mark Bullingham, the chief executive, and Dan Ashworth, the chief football officer.

View image in fullscreen Jobe Bellingham (right) and Jude Bellingham will by aiming to earn England a point against Croatia or Spain to make the Nations League quarter-finals. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Ashworth and Bullingham reinforced the message in person during the summer. “They made it very early in the World Cup,” Tuchel said, explaining that the backing came while the sacking clause remained active. “They just made it very clear and it comes from a place of trust, and that’s what you look for as a coach.

“I love my players. I love my staff and I have bosses who trust me. I know how to appreciate it a lot. I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 matches that I’m not involved in a year. But I’m desperate to win the Nations League and to try to win the Euros.”

Tuchel, who is preparing for the Nations League game at home against Croatia on Thursday night, is thinking ahead. He is gearing up for a European Championship staged mainly in England, who would also like to be chosen to host the Nations League finals next summer. “To have it here would be exciting,” Tuchel said. “First of all, we need to reach the final.”

England need one point from their final two games in Group A3 to finish in the top two and qualify for the quarter-finals in March. Victory against Croatia would give them a chance of finishing top when they visit Spain on Sunday. The Croatia game will not merely be a celebration of Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or. Wembley will watch the captain break the England men’s appearance record, but other issues are at play.
