Tuchel needs Jude Bellingham to be careful given that England’s No 10 is on a booking and at risk of missing the Spain game through suspension. There are unknowns in central defence after Marc Guéhi’s withdrawal. Ezri Konsa is unavailable against Croatia and targeting a return against Spain. Tuchel, who added James Hill and Dan Burn to his squad this week, will use a new partnership against Slaven Bilic’s side.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Dan Burn (second right) is likely to play at left-back for England. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images

It is likely to be Jarell Quansah as the right centre-back and Jarrad Branthwaite could miss out to Burn on the left. “Jarrad is doing very well but it’s a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,” Tuchel said. “Dan Burn is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons where they followed in a high press.”

Burn led the team out when England trained on Wednesday. Among the group are exciting newcomers who inevitably command the attention. Tuchel has Rio Ngumoha and Josh King in attack. He is the first senior manager to work with the Bellingham brothers. Jobe Bellingham, who has impressed with his physicality and calm on the ball, plays a deeper midfield role than Jude. Jobe is likely to start on the bench.

Tuchel wants to reconnect with the values from the previous camp. It featured England impressing in a narrow defeat by Spain, before they crushed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka. One big highlight from the Croatia win was Alex Scott’s performance alongside Elliot Anderson in midfield.

Scott, who is out with a thigh injury, can challenge Declan Rice. The competition for places is fierce. Rice is back after missing the last camp. Tuchel said the Arsenal midfielder remained crucial.

“Declan understands the game like he’s almost a coach on the field,” Tuchel said, but a new identity is forming. It was interesting that Tuchel mentioned the young Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong, whose first call-up may not be far away. It seems Tuchel 2.0 is taking shape.

Sports.title: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
Sports.content:
The top four-ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed by Fifa.

Spain, the United States, Germany and England are currently ranked one to four in the world respectively, although the US and England still need to qualify for the tournament. The seedings will be based on 7 December’s updated rankings, meaning the standings could change before the draw, which will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.

The top four sides were also separated until the semi-finals of the 2026 men’s World Cup, which consisted of 48 teams, but it was not announced until Wednesday that the same rule would apply to the 32-team women’s tournament. In the men’s World Cup the top four – Spain, Argentina, France and England – all reached the semi-finals.

Record four-time champions the US face El Salvador on 27 November as they bid to confirm their place at next summer’s tournament. A victory, coupled with no changes to the world rankings, would ensure the Americans would be placed in the opposite half of the draw to the defending champions, Spain. That would mean if they win their groups the two teams could not meet until the final, which will be played at the Maracanã Stadium on 25 July. Neither Spain nor the US finished top of their group at the last World Cup.

England, the 2023 runners-up, must beat Ukraine over two legs on 1 and 5 December to ensure their qualification. The European champions hold a healthy 31-point advantage over fifth-placed Japan in the world rankings before the upcoming round of internationals.

France, the hosts Brazil and Sweden – who finished third at three of the past four World Cups, and face Scotland in their qualifying playoff in December – would complete the set of eight Pot 1 seeds for the eight groups, if the current top eight remains as it is. Canada, ranked ninth in the world, could pounce on a Pot 1 spot if anyone slips up.

Fifa have also confirmed that the draw will take place at 1.30pm local time (11.30am EST/4.30pm GMT) on 11 December, at Rio de Janeiro’s Museum of Modern Art. Brazil, as hosts, will be placed into Group A and will contest the opening match at the Maracanã on 24 June.

After the eight Pot 1 sides, the next eight highest-ranked teams involved will be in Pot 2, with the next eight below them in Pot 3. Pot 4 will include three places for the winners of the inter-confederation playoff tournament that will conclude in March, along with the lowest-ranked sides involved.

No group will be permitted to include more than one team from the same continent, except for European teams, of whom there can be a maximum of two per group.

Sports.title: ‘An eternal shame’: Bilic and Croatia aim to use 7-0 humbling as fuel against England
Sports.content:
As Croatia prepare to face England at Wembley on Thursday in the Nations League, wounds from a humiliating defeat by the same opponents last month are fresh and there is a lingering feeling of unease.

No one will say it – certainly not Slaven Bilic, who always believes in achieving goals that may seem unreachable to most others – but the impression is that Croatia would be satisfied to accept another defeat, provided it was gentle enough by score and hard‑fought by approach; that this game is not so much about the points as the (self-)respect they can regain.

Croatia lost 7-0 against England in Rijeka and were lucky not to concede more. After the game, Roy Keane commented that England looked as if they were matched against junior players, but that wasn’t it, and neither was the comparison to San Marino or Andorra pushed widely through the media here.

Croatia did not look like a weak or inadequate team – they did not look like a team at all. The best assessments about the game came from within that night. “I have to say this,” the captain, Luka Modric, said. “I’ve been here for 20 years and this is the first time I feel ashamed. You can lose the game; that is not the issue here – they are simply better than us at the moment. But to squander the reputation we worked so hard and so long building – that is unacceptable.”

Bilic agreed: “We were no match for them in any respect: challenges, aggression, technique, physicality … And then, of course, your confidence, your focus and your mental resolve all drop and everything falls apart.”

It seemed that even the head coach, known for his eloquence and persuasive style of communication, struggled to comprehend what had happened and to find the right words. “I am left with an eternal shame,” Bilic said in a later interview. But then there was a moment of unusual clarity, when he was asked what he had told the players in the dressing room.

View image in fullscreen Slaven Bilic could hardly believe what he was seeing at the Rijeka Stadium as England waltzed to a 7-0 victory last month. Photograph: SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty Images

“I told them that there are games which you simply need to forget and turn a new page as soon as possible, because you have the next match in a few days. But this is not one of those games. This one you should never forget. You should keep it in mind for the rest of your lives and always be reminded of it so that you do everything not to repeat something like that ever again.”

The question on everyone’s mind, even if they dare not admit it, is: what if there is a repeat?

The team responded well to the England implosion, producing a battling display against Spain three days later. Although Croatia lost, it was a close game and the world champions were pushed hard before Ivan Perisic was sent off after 79 minutes, with the score 1-1, for a second yellow card that means he is unavailable for the Wembley rematch with England.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was a good way to start their redemption but England pose challenges of a different kind. The weight is not only mental but very much physical. Bilic made some serious mistakes with his team selection and tactics in Rijeka and the players’ resolve was nowhere near the required level even before “everything fell apart”. But the way England play – when they play well – creates a clear mismatch for a team that still revolve around a 41‑year‑old playmaker, with no true defensive midfielder or top wingers; much more so than Spain’s methodical approach.

England may simply be too fast for Croatia, and Bilic faces the immense task of somehow slowing them, limiting their attacking capacity and reducing the game to isolated incidents as much as possible. He needs to be pragmatic, which may include heavier involvement for one of his assistants, the set-piece specialist Gianni Vio, but first and foremost the players need to show much more grit and intensity.

So get stuck in? Well, yes. That is what the public back home wants to see, rather than some clever idea Bilic may have up his sleeve. “We can hardly wait,” Bilic said, but he was uncharacteristically vague and avoided going into details about the team’s ambitions.

The real issue is proving that Croatia, despite the recent haunting trauma, are still a true team: one worthy of the glorious past and with hope for the future.

Sports.title: League One clubs aim for further curbs on spending as budgets continue to spiral
Sports.content:
League One clubs want to introduce new spending restrictions to reduce losses by limiting investment from owners.

Clubs in the division voted to tighten the rules last summer by reducing spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover, and removed a staggered approach to owner investment, so that only 50% of equity injections can be spent on squad costs, with the rest assigned to infrastructure projects. Less than six months later many want to go further.

The Guardian has learned that two proposed models are being considered: a fixed cap on owner investment or introducing a version of the Premier League’s squad cost rules, with a £1 levy on clubs for every £1 spent above 50% of their revenue. Sporting sanctions would be applied if spending reached 60%, with the money raised from the levy redistributed to other clubs in the division.

The move to introduce more spending curbs comes despite a legal challenge to the existing rules from the Professional Footballers’ Association, which launched proceedings in August on the grounds that the clubs had failed to abide by the terms of their membership of the professional negotiating and consultative committee.

An attempt by League One and League Two to introduce salary caps of £2.5m and £1.5m respectively was withdrawn in 2021 after the PFA took them to an independent arbitration panel.

Discussions over stricter controls have been taking place for some time, but have been given fresh impetus by last month’s publication of the State of the Game report. The first piece of work by the Independent Football Regulator showed that 94% of clubs in the EFL and National League are loss-making, and that 32 of the 96 would not survive for a month without owner funding.

Last summer’s changes reduced the percentage of clubs’ income that can be spent on wages, with managers’ salaries included for the first time, but there is a renewed move to reduce losses, which averaged £7.5m per club in League One last season, up from £5.3m the previous season.

One owner told the Guardian further regulation was necessary because the clubs had repeatedly shown they could not restrain themselves, pointing out that League One wage bills have increased by 15% this season, and that a top-six budget in the division five years ago would now rank in the bottom three.

Reading and Peterborough have long campaigned for tighter spending controls, but face opposition from clubs such as MK Dons and Wycombe, and it is unclear whether any proposal would gain the two-thirds majority required to be introduced.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A source at another League One club warned that an unintended consequence would be to create a cliff edge in terms of financial resources with the Championship, which loosened its regulations last season by permitting owners an inject up to £33m over three years, an equity allowance that does not count towards the 85% wage spending/revenue limit.

League Two clubs are also involved in the discussions, although it is unclear whether they will choose to align with League One.

The EFL confirmed discussions were ongoing, although formal proposals have yet to be put to the clubs.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola eyed for new manager’s job in dramatic swoop
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola eyed for new manager’s job in dramatic swoop

US Soccer want Pep Guardiola to replace Mauricio Pochettino as the men's national team head coach, talkSPORT understands.

Pochettino looks set to leave for Premier League giants Manchester United having agreed a deal in principle to replace Michael Carrick.



2 Guardiola could be on his way back into management as the United States eye a replacement for Pochettino Credit: AFP

Those overseeing the managerial change in the United States set-up want to hire Guardiola in what would be a sensational appointment.

The Spaniard has been out of management since the summer when he left Manchester City after a decade at the club.

Guardiola won six Premier League titles and the Champions League, and is regarded as one of the best managers in history.



He also lifted three consecutive league trophies with Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

Joining the USMNT would present a fresh challenge as Guardiola has never managed at international level.



However, it won't be as straightforward for the powers that be as he hinted before his City exit that he would take a break from football.

Could Guardiola join USMNT?

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025.



"I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

In a separate interview, he reiterated: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure."

"When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all," Guardiola added.

2 Guardiola is one of the most successful managers in history and would be a remarkable appointment for the United States Credit: Getty



Despite leaving the club, Guardiola has maintained support for City in recent months.

He sent an emotional message to fans after City were found guilty on all charges of Premier League financial breaches in September.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all," the 55-year-old said.

Guardiola then attended their Champions League league phase clash at home to holders Paris Saint-Germain last month.



However, he watched his former side lose 4-2 in what was their worst home defeat in the competition ever.

Should Guardiola take the USMNT job, he could be on the touchline in time for the Gold Cup next summer.

Sports.title: Harry Kane confirms 2030 World Cup plans and doesn’t rule out future Premier League return
Sports.content:
Harry Kane hasn't got retirement on his mind as he revealed his intention to play at the next World Cup in just under four years time.

The England captain and Ballon d'Or winner joined talkSPORT Drive for an exclusive interview, and he was asked a variety of questions by Andy Goldstein and Darren Bent in a brilliant, wide-ranging chat.

5 Kane was in good spirits ahead of appearing for the 126th time for England against Croatia Credit: talkSPORT

He recently put pen to paper on a new contract with Bayern Munich that lasts until the summer of 2029.

Kane said he doesn't believe this will be the final contract of his football career, although he doesn't have any intention of cutting short his agreement with his current club.

The England legend is very happy in Germany, but once that deal expires, he's not sure what will happen.

One thing he is determined to make happen is the 2030 World Cup.

We saw in the 2026 World Cup that Lionel Messi, Luka Modric and Cristiano Ronaldo all took part despite being in their late 30s or early 40s.

And Kane is targeting involvement in the tournament that is set to be hosted in Spain, Morocco and Portugal, saying: "I hope to still be around by then. I'd be 35 nearly 36, but I think that is pretty young, to be honest.

"There are examples of players playing well into their 30s at the highest level, and as long as I am performing and I deserve my place in the team, then I'll be here.

"If I am scoring 50, 60, 70 goals a season for my club, there is no reason why I won't be here to help the national team.

"My biggest dream is to win a major trophy with England. There are some great things I have achieved throughout my career, but there are many more that I want to win.

"I think it is fairly realistic that I'll still be here for the World Cup in four years, but as we know, we have the home Euros, and that is where the focus lies."

5 Kane was named the best player in the world in October after a stellar 2025/26 season for Bayern Munich Credit: Getty

5 Kane is England's record goalscorer and now a Bayern fans' favourite Credit: Getty

Premier League return for Kane?

After spending his entire career in England, Kane took the bold plunge to abandon Tottenham and join Bayern Munich in a £100m deal.

That happened in 2023, and though the Champions League has evaded him thus far, the move has been a huge success.

He has won the Ballon d'Or and two Bundesliga titles and has scored over 150 goals already.

Kane is loved at the club and by their fans, while his family are settled in Bavaria.

When asked about a potential Premier League return, he said: "I'll be honest, I am really not sure.

"When I think back coming back, it isn't just about the record (top goalscorer in the Premier League), there are things I haven't achieved yet.

5 A few of the questions threw Kane off, but he handled them well Credit: talksport

"But since I've been away, it has really opened my eyes that there is a big old world out there, and I think people are appreciating my game more.

"So, I think it would have to be a perfect situation for me to ever come back, and I can't see where that would be."

Goldstein pressed if that meant it was still possible, he said: "One day, anything is possible."

Right at the end of the interview, Goldstein tried one more question about Kane returning to the Premier League, asking him if he'd re-join Tottenham or another top-flight club.

It left Kane shaking his head before he said: "All the tough questions at the end before I go.

"Who knows, I can't tell you. Time will tell."

5 Kane is a club legend at Tottenham and fans would be desperate to have him back Credit: Getty

Record breaker again

Kane will start England's Nations League game on Thursday night against Croatia, live on talkSPORT.

And ahead of that match, Kane has been speaking about breaking Peter Shilton's record.

This game will be Kane's 126th cap, and in a pre-match press conference, he said: "It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement).

"I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career."

Sports.title: Harry Kane tells Manchester United fans exactly what to expect from ‘incredible’ Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has heaped praise on Mauricio Pochettino ahead of his potential appointment at Manchester United.

talkSPORT understands United players expect Pochettino to replace head coach Michael Carrick, who is likely to be told on Thursday that he has been relieved of his duties.



3 Pochettino looks set to replace Carrick in the Man United dugout and already reached an agreement in principle with United Credit: Getty

The Argentine is currently head coach of the United States national team, but has reached an agreement in principle with the hierarchy at Old Trafford.

Pochettino has a $10million (£7.5m) release clause in his contract, and an appointment is set to increase in value with his background staff.

Formerly of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, he has won 150 of his 294 matches in the Premier League, and also won Ligue 1 with Paris Saint-Germain.



The 54-year-old is mostly known for his stint at Spurs from 2014 to 2019, during which they had two league title challenges and reached their first ever Champions League final.

Kane flourished with him as his head coach having netted 169 goals in 242 outings under him, and since became the all-time top scorer for England as well as a Ballon d'Or winner.



With Pochettino looking likely to join United, Kane was asked about what their fans can expect from during an exclusive interview on talkSPORT Drive.

Kane on 'incredible' Pochettino

"I can't speak highly enough of him," Kane said. "At a stage in my career, he was massive to my development.



"He took a team that was extremely young and not seen as one of the top teams, to us having back-to-back title races, getting to a Champions League final. He took the club to the highest place it has almost ever been.

"For me, personally, he helped me develop as a player not just on the pitch, but also off the pitch. We built up a really good open relationship.

"It was my first time playing regularly at the highest level, all the demands and pressure that comes with that, he was a big help in dealing with that.

3 Kane credited Pochettino with helping him develop at Spurs and spoke on how he makes an impact off the pitch Credit: Getty



"He's an incredible manager, I think he has proven that over his career, but he's just a great person as well.

"I'm sure if it does happen, Man United will have a great coach that will do everything to get them back to the levels that they expect to be at."

Ex-England striker Darren Bent then spoke on how Pochettino comes across as both a manager and head coach, with the former role usually covering all bases rather than just tactics like the latter.

"He took a lot of the training, he took a lot of the tactical stuff and how he wanted us to play in pretty much every session," Kane revealed.



"But then he was a really good man manager as well. I think because we were such a young team at the time, I think he understood that there's a lot of players who would need guidance or an arm around the shoulder, or someone who's pushing.

"Even for me, to push me from a physical level, to do more at the gym. You always respected him and could have a talk with him, and be open with personal issues.

3 Kane has backed Pochettino to be a success at United and take them back towards the top of English football Credit: Getty

"For sure, he does both. I think that is the way that maybe more modern coaches are as well, you see that more and more."



Kane spoke ahead of England's Nations League clash against Croatia on Thursday night, which will be live on talkSPORT.

He is set to parade his Ballon d'Or trophy before kick-off, and then become his country's all-time leading appearance maker by winning his 126th cap.

Sports.title: Liam Delap outlines England ambition after frustrating Chelsea experience
Sports.content:
Liam Delap remains committed to earning a first ever England call-up amid his strong start to life at Nottingham Forest.

The striker, who signed in a £50million move from Chelsea during the summer, shone for his new club in their 3-1 win over Manchester City over the weekend.



3 Delap couldn't find his feet at Chelsea and, with only two goals scored for the club, he left after just one season for Forest Credit: Getty

Delap scored two thumping goals against his former side to help Forest rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

The double took his league tally to three for the season thus far, and he has already beaten his total from the 2025/26 campaign at Chelsea.

Having impressed at Ipswich Town, Delap joined the Blues for £30m in June 2025 but had an underwhelming spell at Stamford Bridge.



With two goals in 41 outings across all competitions, one of which was in the Premier League, the 23-year-old flattered to deceive.

Speaking to talkSPORT on White and Jordan on Wednesday, Delap honestly reflected on his tough time at Chelsea as he said: "When things don't go so well, you learn a lot.



"You're sitting there sometimes, frustrated and angry. But you've just go to get through those moments because football's not a linear path.

"I think it grows you as a man more than anything, to be honest, just staying focused and concentrating on yourself."



Delap reveals England hopes

Club football has paused for the international break for one final time in 2026, although Delap is still at Forest as he did not receive a call-up with England for upcoming matches against Croatia and Spain.

He has 14 goals in 38 appearances at youth level for his country and is yet to be involved with the senior side, but the honour is in his sights.

"Yeah, 100 per cent, it's the ambition as a little kid," he replied when asked of his aspirations to play for England.

3 Delap showcased his quality and potential with two excellent strikes against City on Saturday evening Credit: AFP



3 With his club form now on the up, the striker is looking to take the next step and earn a senior call-up with England Credit: Getty

"I've just got to focus on what I can control, focus on game by game at Forest, and then see what happens."

When could Delap play for England?

Nine-time England international Danny Murphy joined the show, and believes that Delap is capable of featuring for England at Euro 2028.

Qualification officially gets underway in March, with the tournament then being played from June 9 to July 9, 2028.



That gives Delap plenty of time to stake his claim for a striker spot in the England squad should they qualify, with captain Harry Kane set to remain as the no.1 choice.

And Murphy is confident that, should he maintain his current form at Forest, he will be in and around head coach Thomas Tuchel's plans.

"I think Liam's got a great chance of carrying on the way he is," Murphy said.

"If he's playing regularly and his confidence builds, I think he's got a great chance of being in the Euros squad."

Sports.title: Danny Kelly: Tottenham, Simon Jordan and Laura Woods among thousands to pay tribute
Sports.content:
Tributes for Danny Kelly have flooded in from far and wide following the tragic news of his death.

On Wednesday morning, it was announced that beloved broadcaster and talkSPORT presenter Danny had sadly passed away, aged 69.

6 Thousands have joined talkSPORT in paying tribute to Danny Kelly, who has sadly died aged 69

He was one of the most recognisable, respected and engaging voices across our network, having joined the team in 2007.

Danny stepped away from the mic in March following a throat cancer diagnosis and, during his last appearance, he urged men to go out and get themselves checked in what was an emotional message.

Like music, football was a massive passion of his, with Danny being a huge fan of Premier League giants Spurs.

His love of the game was clear for all to see in October 2008 as Aaron Lennon scored a last-gasp equaliser against their north London rivals Arsenal in the iconic 4-4 draw.

"I love football, Stan. I love it," he cried, and Spurs have offered their respect to Danny with a heartfelt post on social media.

Tottenham tribute to Danny Kelly

"The entire Tottenham family mourns the loss of one of our own, broadcasting legend Danny Kelly," they said.

"Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Danny."

talkSPORT's announcement on X drew in more than one thousand replies from listeners and fans of Danny to pay respect, a testament to his legacy.

Simon Jordan offered his own tribute on White and Jordan, and in doing so, he revealed his admiration for Danny.

"I knew Danny very well. He was a brilliant broadcaster, a brilliant editor, a brilliant writer. He was a brilliant friend.

6 Danny was a cherished member of the talkSPORT family, and brought great joy to listeners on the airwaves Credit: talkSPORT

"The reasons why I'm able to broadcast and occupy the space I'm in now are because I worked with Danny. When I came here and started working with you guys, it was with Danny.

"Danny nurtured me and developed me, and corralled me, and persuaded me, and educated me, and censored me in equal measure."

Danny Murphy worked alongside the broadcasting icon on Kick Off for talkSPORT, and he said: "Warm, charismatic, funny... so funny. He could make a really serious moment lighthearted.

"And educational, he had a story about everyone and everything, he met everybody there is to know. Every time someone famous got brought up, he'd tell a little anecdote about when he met them and talked to them, and he was just always engaging to listen to.

"It was a pleasure to work with him over the years, I didn't realise how knowledgeable he was not just on music, but football as well. He loved his football, and that came through in abundance."

Former Breakfast host Laura Woods also joined the show, and recalled how much Danny helped her during a difficult moment in her career.

6 Danny will forever be remembered as one of radio's biggest and best presenters, and leave a lasting legacy for all of us Credit: talkSPORT

"You don't meet a lot of broadcasters that will really be informed and interested in your own career, he was interested in mine and he was so caring."

Woods added: "When I got the Breakfast show, it was in COVID and it was a really tough time for everyone. I felt it a lot, I really felt like I needed an ear, I was struggling to get to grips with the job and, for a little while, I didn't think I was right for it.

"Danny messaged me, and he was like, 'How's it going? How are you? Are you okay? Are you getting enough sleep?' And I said, 'No!' He went, 'Right, call me after the show tomorrow and we'll have a chat'.

"I remember that call, and it was exactly what I needed. It was just an ear at a time where I needed guidance from this great man. I felt like I always had that at talkSPORT, and he was like that for all of us.

"It didn't matter who you were, you were part of his little family if you worked anywhere near him. If you were in touching distance of Danny Kelly, he was your guidance."

talkSPORT legend Adrian Durham joined the boys on Drive to pay tribute to Danny, who was a very close personal friend.

Adrian said: "I would consider him one of my closest personal friends, not just a brilliant broadcaster and a wonderful colleague.

"He had this natural warmth with his voice that was infectious, it made you want to get involved as well.

"I remember being on a train full of Palace fans back from Wolves one day, and they asked me who my favourite presenter was, and I said Danny Kelly.

"They said they loved Trans Euro Express, and it is by far the best show on the station partly because of the European expert opinion but also because of Danny's warmth and the fact he was so interested, and that is why he was such a great broadcaster. It felt like was sitting next to you in the car or in the living room.

"Three years ago, I was going through a really terrible time in my life, and I was with my son.

"I went over to Ireland to see Danny just because I needed to talk to somebody who I thought could help me, and Danny was there for me.

"He was a trusted colleague and we hadn't even broadcast together at that point, thankfully, we did afterwards , but he was so good to me and warm and welcoming to me and my son and incredibly helpful on a personal level.

"We were talking about The Smiths and Stevie Wonder, and all the people we love, and my son asks him if he had any gangster rap.

"He pulls out the Wu Tang Clan and puts that on, and they were in their element - it was sensational, and he just had time for everybody.

"We worked together at the Sports Book Award, which is particularly emotional for me because I was on the judging panel, and Danny and I are meant to be doing that show together later this month, and obviously, he won't be doing it.

"So, I sent the winning book to him, so he had it in his possession and then this terrible, truly shocking news broke today - it is just tough for everybody."

6 Adrian's emotion reflects how the talkSPORT family feel about Danny

6 Danny was famously part of the Trans Europe Express show on Sunday evenings, with his knowledge marking a perfect end to the week Credit: talkSPORT

Many of Danny's other talkSPORT colleagues also paid their respects on social media, with chief football correspondent Alex Crook saying: "This is so sad. Danny was a great broadcaster and a brilliant colleague and friend.

"Had a wonderful day with him watching Spurs' last game at White Hart Lane. talkSPORT will never be quite the same again."

"Absolutely heartbroken to hear Danny Kelly has passed away," added reporter Ian Abrahams. "One of the best broadcasters I’ve worked with. One of the most amazing, kindest, funny, passionate people I knew.

"Danny, we'll always have "I love Football". I will miss you my friend, sleep well."

Stan Collymore also gave a lengthy tribute to Danny, as he said: "This morning I was told of the passing of my good friend and colleague, Danny Kelly.

"The tributes to him in the coming days from those who knew him and worked with him will give you an idea of how much he was loved. I loved him too. Very much so.

"A man who I called "Dad" on air because I wished he was. I hope you give me a few minutes to read my thoughts, and I hope they do you justice, Dan.

"By 2008 I was a mess. I would sleep 18 hours a day, the other 6 mostly wanting to die. Once or twice a week I would open my laptop, organise football tabs, gossip and news as prep for jobs in broadcasting that I knew would never come, "just in case".

"When hope dies, we die, after all. Then Danny Kelly came into my life. I was driving out of London having been to see a psychiatrist about the state I was in and had BBC London on the radio.

"Danny was presenting with a guest, reviewing books. My name came up in the conversation, so I called in. We hit it off straight away, talked about football for what seemed like forever but was probably a standard 10-12 minute section.

"But for me it sparked a temporary respite from sleep and chronic mental health issues and even for that I was grateful. A couple of years later Danny joined talkSPORT to do the 7-10pm slot through the week.

6 Rest in peace Danny, and thank you for everything

"He told me he was offered a few co-presenters but he remembered that conversation we had and he wanted me to do it. A lifeline of work, passionately talking about our sport, having fun and feeling a value as a human again.

"Something lost for 7 long years. Danny gifted me that. Without that I know I wouldn't be writing this today. "Always fresh, never frozen" was the tagline in a Domino's read we had to do in the show, something we'd instinctively greet each other with until our last meeting, in a pub, broadcasting for talkSPORT around 3 years ago.

"I didn't know that time would be the last, but perhaps fittingly we hugged as I left, I'm glad I did. The shows were loved. They were funny, honest, insightful and I hope, along with Saggers after that, proof that Danny's belief in me was worthy.

"But to say my love for him was only thanks for a job doesn't even scratch the surface.

"His kindness, his phone calls late at night (Dan was a notorious night owl) of support, his man hugs, his indomitable spirit, his big brain on anything from football to music to geopolitics, his love, as I know many others will testify, came from the biggest of hearts and the biggest of souls housed in a giant of a man in every sense.

"Dan, thank you, thank you for the kindness, the fun, the hope, the support and for being someone to look up to and aspire to be. I love you very much, I know I'll hug you again some day. Thank you for everything. 'I love football Stan, I love it'."

Sports.title: How England could line-up against Croatia with Jobe Bellingham debut and Jordan Pickford decision
Sports.content:
How England could line-up against Croatia with Jobe Bellingham debut and Jordan Pickford decision

England return to Wembley for their penultimate League A Group 3 fixture with a much-changed team expected against Croatia.

The Three Lions enjoyed their best performance under Thomas Tuchel in the reverse meeting after thrashing Slaven Bilić's men 7-0.



5 England completely thrashed Croatia 7-0 in their third Nations League game of the last international break Credit: AFP

England have won three straight games in the Nations League since losing their first game of the September international break to Spain.

The hybrid behind-closed-doors game saw thousands of Croatian children in attendance in Rijeka for the Three Lions' masterclass.

Harry Kane scored twice, with the first of his strikes seeing him become only the fourth England player ever to find the net in six straight away games for his country.



However, the Ballon d'Or winner could start Thursday's clash on the bench to keep himself fresh for Sunday's blockbuster with Spain.

England know only a draw from their final two games will be enough to guarantee a spot in the last eight.



But Tuchel has already publicly outlined his goal to win the group, which will mean putting his full-strength team out against Spain.

As a result, the German could field an experimental team at Wembley, with several stars in line to make their full England debuts.



England predicted XI against Croatia

European football expert Andy Brassell has now outlined how the Three Lions could line up for the visit of Bilic's men.

Ezri Konsa has already been listed as an absentee for Thursday’s clash, with regular centre-back partner Marc Guehi also out injured.

The first question is whether Tuchel will pick James Trafford or Jordan Pickford in goal.

5 Konsa and Guehi have been Tuchel's preferred pairing, but neither will play a minute against Croatia Credit: Getty



Brassell told talkSPORT: "My feeling is that for the Croatia game, they probably need to pick a bit of a Carabao Cup-type team and then save the real stuff for Spain. So I'm starting with James Trafford.

"I want to see more of Jarell Quansah at right back.

"I'm really interested to see how he could be a challenger slash semi-permanent solution for England in that position.

"So obviously Ben White is in the squad, and you could have him there, but I just think the attacking part of Quansah's game is really, really good and we've seen that at Leverkusen.

"He's almost a reluctant right back, a little bit in the mould of Jules Koundé, in that really he feels that he's a centre-back still.



"But I think both his attacking aptitude and his physical characteristics lend to him doing very, very well in that position."

5 Quansah was named in England's World Cup squad after featuring 43 times for Leverkusen last term Credit: Getty

"My centre-half pairing: [Jarrad] Branthwaite and [Dan] Burn.

"Branthwaite, I think, is really hard to quantify for me how good he's gonna get because there's been that sense that he might go on to hit that absolute elite level for a while yet, and he's very good, but I don't think we're quite there yet.

"I'd love to pair him with Dan Burn, who's very experienced and much better at centre-back than he is at left-back.



"My left-back is Lewis Hall. I think the pair of them working together for Newcastle is quite a nice fit.

"I've gone for my second team, and I think not by a lot, but I think Hall is the second best choice for left-back in this squad."

5 Burn is back fit after an ankle injury disrupted his start to the season Credit: Getty

Jobe set for England debut?

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder, brother of Jude Bellingham, was handed his first England call-up along with uncapped Josh King.



The 21-year-old, who impressed in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich on Saturday, could now be given his full Three Lions debut.

Brassell continued: "My sitters are going to be James Garner, who's been really good over the last year and a half and Jobe Bellingham.

5 Jobe and Jude Bellingham will become the 22nd set of brothers to represent England Credit: Getty

"Jobe, even though he's adding these more attacking strings to his bow this season, I think long term, maybe that's where his future lies in, say a number eight role, because the doubt that I have about him at this point - he's still developing and we can't expect too much too soon - is sometimes he's a little bit casual on the ball in his own half, and he gives the ball away in quite compromising positions in his own half of the pitch.



"We saw that against Bayern in the Super Cup right at the start of the season; he got away with it once, the second time he didn't get away with it and they conceded a goal.

"But that will come with time - he's developing really nicely, and I think the combination of him and Garner feels quite rigorous.

"I want to see a bit of Josh King in this break; he's started the season really, really well, some good bits from him last season. We're seeing even more this season."

'A good opportunity for Rio Ngumoha'

"Any squad that Morgan Gibbs-White is not in makes a bit sad, really.



"I think he's going to have an interesting role in this team if Tuchel were to go with this team because I feel he would be the technical leader of the team just like he is with Nottingham Forest.

"That like-for-like situation, I think, will get the best out of him.

"Rio Ngumoha, who has been really good this season, I think, seeing more and more from him and a good opportunity for him to push for a place in the XI more regularly.

"Leading the line, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who is a great point of reference centre forward and the move to Leeds has really worked out for him."

Sports.title: Premier League panel reveals penalty should have been awarded in Gameweek 9
Sports.content:
Premier League panel reveals penalty should have been awarded in Gameweek 9

A Premier League panel has revealed two VAR errors were made in Gameweek 9, including the Alexander Isak penalty incident against Arsenal.

The Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled that Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty due to the striker being pulled back by Jurrien Timber.



3 Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty against Arsenal, the KMI Panel have confirmed Credit: Premier League

Referee Andy Madley did not award a penalty on-field, while the incident was taken to the video assistant referee Stuart Attwell before being checked and cleared.

The Panel voted 4:1 that the penalty should have been awarded on the field, while a 3:2 vote decided the VAR should have intervened.

However, the Panel unanimously voted that Timber's challenge did not warrant a red card.



Arsenal were leading 1-0 after an early goal from Kai Havertz, which proved to be the only goal of the game.

Following the match, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said: "There is a clear grab of the shirt. Alex was just in front of him. He was going to head in front of the goal, but couldn't because he grabbed the shirt.



"If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty, 100 per cent. It should be like this, but it is what it is.

"Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it. The answer is you have to dive. If you don't dive they won't call it."



The Premier League released a statement, which read: "The panel felt that a penalty should have been awarded for a holding action by Timber on Isak, 4:1. One panellist considered the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress.

" The majority also felt that VAR should have intervened to recommend an on-field review, 3:2, on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

"Two panellists considered that the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention."

3 Arsenal have dropped just three points in their opening nine matches Credit: Getty



The league says match officials should penalise any holding actions that have a 'clear material impact on play'.

They have directed referees to consider multiple factors when determining an offence, including whether a player is 'focused solely on an opponent rather than the ball, if they are holding an opponent with both arms and if the holding is sustained or impactful to an opponent or their clothing.'

On this occasion, the panel have decided that the Arsenal defender's challenge on the Sweden international met the standards for a holding offence.

Therefore, the Reds should have been awarded a penalty kick, both on-field and through VAR intervention.



The Gunners went on to win 1-0 at Anfield, and currently remain nine points clear of Iraola's side at the top of the league with 27 points.

Making multiple mistakes

Additionally, the Panel concluded that there was a second VAR error on 31 October in a fixture between two newly promoted sides - Hull City against Ipswich Town.

3 The Panel is made up of one Premier League representative, one Pro Ref representative, and three independent (ex-players/managers) representatives Credit: Getty

Referee Thomas Kirk failed to penalise a foul by Nobel Mendy on Dara O'Shea, with Neil Davies on VAR also failing to award the Tractor Boys a deserved penalty.



4:1 voted that the officials should have given the spot-kick on field, and the VAR should have intervened.

One member of the panel felt that the 'actions of O'Shea and Florentino Luis should have been taken into account, meaning no penalty'.

However, Ipswich went on to score the game's opening goal only four minutes after the incident through Luis.

The game went on to finish 2-2, with both sides currently sitting on an equal amount of 11 points.

Sports.title: Man United reach agreement in principle with Mauricio Pochettino to spark USA uncertainty
Sports.content:
There is uncertainty over Mauricio Pochettino's involvement with the United States in the international break, talkSPORT understands.

Pochettino is due to oversee the USMNT's CONCACAF National League quarter-final tie against Haiti, with the first leg scheduled for November 14 and the second on November 18.

2 Pochettino had been busy preparing the USMNT before United entered the fray Credit: getty

However, he has an agreement in principle with Manchester United to take over from Michael Carrick, who is set to be sacked.

The total compensation to bring Pochettino and his staff from the USMNT set-up to Old Trafford is expected to be around $12million (£9m).

With an agreement in the background, talkSPORT understands it is under discussion as to whether Pochettino takes charge of the USMNT against Haiti.

Mauricio Pochettino's journey as USMNT coach

Pochettino was appointed to lead the Stars and Stripes in September 2024 on a two-year contract which ran through to the end of the 2026 World Cup.

The 54-year-old's contract reportedly netted him a salary of £4.5million, which was partly funded by investment companies and commercial partners.

Despite the advantage of being a co-host, Pochettino took the US as far as the round of 16 at this year's World Cup where they were beaten 4-1 by Belgium.

The lead-up to the contest was overshadowed by Folarin Balogun having his suspension controversially overturned following an intervention from the White House after he was sent off in the round of 32 against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Pochettino then agreed to a new deal that kept him as the USMNT boss through 2030 in August.

But the proposition of returning to the Premier League and taking over United may prove to be an opportunity he cannot pass up.

2 Pochettino is all but certain to be back in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Should he not end up taking charge of the US in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, Pochettino would finish with a record of 22 wins, one draw and 12 defeats from his time in charge.

Four of those wins have come after the World Cup, with the US defeating Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

What has Mauricio Pochettino previously said about a Premier League return?

Pochettino had previously left the door open for a return to the English top flight in an exclusive interview with talkSPORT last November.

"Maybe it's possible, yes," Pochettino said.

"My challenge for the future is the World Cup and being now focused on the USA national team, maybe I come back one day to the Premier League."

Should he take the United job, it would mark his fourth Premier League role having previously taken charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

And if a deal is agreed in time, Pochettino's first match as Red Devils boss following the international break would be a daunting trip to Liverpool on November 22.

Sports.title: I won't do a Mauricio Pochettino! Thomas Tuchel insists there is 'zero chance' he will walk out on England for a Premier League job - but admits he misses club football
Sports.content:
I won't do a Mauricio Pochettino! Thomas Tuchel insists there is 'zero chance' he will walk out on England for a Premier League job - but admits he misses club football

Thomas Tuchel will stay loyal to England until the end of his contract at the 2028 European Championship but admits that he does miss the regular thrill of club management.

As Mauricio Pochettino prepares to activate a release clause with the USA national team to take the Manchester United job, England boss Tuchel has vowed to ignore all outside offers until the end of his deal with England.

‘There is no release clause,’ said Tuchel. ‘I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.’

After that Tuchel said that he is open-minded.

Asked whether he could stay longer with England, he said with a smile that: ‘I am open to everything.’

The chances are, though, that England will be looking for a new coach once the 2028 Euros are done.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he misses club football - but won't walk out on England

He enjoys the buzz of managing 50 matches per season but is contracted until 2028

‘I miss the 50 [club] matches a season,’ Tuchel said. ‘I miss those two minutes when everything is done. You go out the two minutes before the first whistle goes. It's like the best two minutes.

‘Everything is done. You're in a full stadium. Lights are on and you're just so excited and you're part of it.

‘That's actually the two minutes where I realise how lucky and how grateful I am. Then the whistle goes, and then you're just in the tunnel again, trying to win the game for your team.’

Tuchel originally signed a short-term deal through to last summer’s World Cup but extended it until the Euros in the months before the tournament that ended with a semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Asked if there was ‘zero chance’ of him leaving before the end of his contract, he said: ‘I would say so.

‘First of all, I'm very grateful for what I have here because I know how rare it is to be in love with your team and to have the trust and to be able to work freely with your coaching staff, which I am.

‘I love my group of players. I love my staff and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things.

Pochettino is set to become the new manager of Manchester United, replacing Michael Carrick

‘So, it's a lot. And I know how to appreciate it a lot.

‘It's in a good place. I'm in a good place. I'm desperate to win the Nations League and to play and try to win the Euros.’

England face Croatia at Wembley tonight in the Nations League before heading to Madrid for their final group game against Spain on Sunday. If England win both matches, they will top their group ahead of next March’s quarter-finals. At the very least they should progress as a second placed team.

The four teams emerging from next spring’s quarters will play Nations League semi-finals and final in one country next summer. With a venue yet to be chosen by UEFA, the FA are expected to throw their hat into the ring as a prospective host.

Tuchel has spoken before about the struggles England sometimes have in taking training performances on to the pitch and agreed that hosting the Nations League latter stages could act as a decent warm up before the challenges of playing a big tournament in front of a home crowd a year later.

‘The Nations League helps in general for us and I think to have it here could be exciting,’ Tuchel said.

‘It would be nice to have it here. So first of all, we need to reach the final before we play.

‘Playing at home is a challenge. It should be a home advantage when we go to the Euros and it should not become a home disadvantage that we feel in our brain.

‘It should be exciting and that's why it's also important what we are building at the moment and how the team plays.’

Sports.title: Tennis legend Steffi Graf seen in rare family photo with 'lucky' husband Andre Agassi... as her brother hides from cops in tunnels beneath Vegas
Sports.content:
Tennis legend Steffi Graf seen in rare family photo with 'lucky' husband Andre Agassi... as her brother hides from cops in tunnels beneath Vegas

Tennis legend Steffi Graf has posed for a rare family photo with husband Andre Agassi while her brother hides from police in the tunnels beneath Las Vegas.

The Graf family has been in the headlines since it emerged her younger brother, Michael, is living in the underworld while a warrant is out for his arrest.

Steffi, 57 and a 22-time Grand Slam winner, built a new life in Las Vegas decades ago with her husband, Agassi. They were followed by her younger brother Michael and his four children.

But disturbing new details of his life have recently emerged, with the 55-year-old sharing a string of rambling videos on his Facebook page seemingly in the tunnels under the city.

In one recent video, he took aim at his brother-in-law Agassi, recounting an alleged physical altercation between the pair. There is no evidence to support his claims the alleged incident took place. The Daily Mail contacted Agassi's representatives for comment.

Despite the family turmoil behind the scenes, Agassi shared a loved-up photo with his 1.2 million Instagram followers in front of a fireplace with the Nick Hustles song 'This Life is Wonderful' and wrote: 'Lucky to have you Stefanie' along with a love heart emoji.

Andre Agassi shared a loved-up snap with wife Steffi Graf in front of a fireplace on Instagram

Graf and Agassi live as a family in Las Vegas, Nevada with their two kids, Jaz and Jaden

Last month, he shared footage of them hitting the ball together on a tennis court and wrote: 'Perfect day with my love.'

Agassi has long been gushing in his praise of his wife, leaving her overcome with emotion back in 2004 when he introduced her at her International Tennis Hall of Fame induction ceremony.

'As I attempt to find words worthy to introduce the person that has changed my life, I realize the words have yet to be invented that are large enough, colorful enough, or true enough to express the heart and soul of this woman that I love,' Agassi said in his speech.

He called his wife the 'greatest person' he's ever known before she took the mic and said: 'Not that this occasion isn't emotional enough, but to hear you are loved so much is amazing.'

Back in 2014, Steffi Graf told Hello! about how her family settled in Las Vegas due to the strong family connection with Agassi 'born and raised' there.

She added: 'And then very shortly after my mum moved to Las Vegas, and then my brother and his four kids, so we have all the family there. All the cousins are together and growing up together - it's pretty neat.'

She told Tennis Magazine in 2008 that she never envisioned living in Las Vegas when her playing career ended.

'I literally had no idea where I was going to live,' she said. 'I just felt that I've been able to see so much of the world that I wanted to explore that more.

Graf's brother Michael recently shared a string of troubling videos from the tunnels of Vegas

Graf and Agassi got married in a small, intimate ceremony in 2001 before settling in Las Vegas

'Now living with two kids, and another great thing is my mom lives here, and so does my brother with his four kids. Andre, you know, [was] born and raised here, so we have such a tight-knit family and friend circuit. I feel very blessed.'

Just last month, Agassi gave Hello! an insight into his marriage to Graf and their private life together in Las Vegas as he prepared to take part in the Laver Cup.

'She likes seeing me happy, just like I like seeing her happy,' he said. 'She knows this is a week in Laver Cup that I value, that I bond with, that I connect to. It's a lot of work, but she's never been scared of me in work [mode].'

Sports.title: Prince William asks Aston Villa boss Unai Emery about the team EVERY DAY - as he reveals he's become a bigger supporter since becoming a father to football-mad George
Sports.content:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has revealed how passionate Prince William is about his beloved football club and opened up on their relationship. The Prince of Wales, 44, has been a fan of Villa since his days at Eton when he idolised club legend Paul McGrath - shunning the more conventional Premier League big beasts supported by his schoolmates. He regularly attends matches at Villa Park and across Europe alongside his son George, and he has been a prominent figure during their success under Emery in recent times. This included the Prince partying with Villa's squad after last season's Europa League triumph and he watched them against Barcelona in the Champions League at the Nou Camp last week. And, in a special edition of Country Life magazine, which was guest edited by the 44-year-old, Emery reflected on their relationship and how often they talk about the club. ’During the transfer window, he’s asking about the team every day,' the Villa boss said. 'How is the team? How are you? How are we going to play some players? How are we going to do? He is always so close to us and we appreciate it so, so much. Unai Emery has revealed how passionate Prince William is about Aston Villa and opened up on their relationship The Prince pictured alongside his son George at Villa's game against Barcelona last week A special edition of Country Life, guest edited by the 44-year-old, featured a piece on Emery ’When he’s with us, he’s a fantastic guy. We’ve had lunch together, he’s watched training sessions, we share conversations, everything about football. He shows his humble personality with us - I can’t forget it. For me, it seems unbelievable. 'He’s our boss, but he’s always trying to be at our level, respecting so much everything we are doing here. If he’s sitting with us to have lunch, he asks “Where am I sitting?” Wherever you want! It’s fantastic. ‘We are scoring, he is celebrating, it is fantastic for us. If we can give him good news, good results, good moments in football, we are proud of it.’ In the same article, the Prince of Wales went on to reflect on his love of football and Villa, revealing how he has become increasingly passionate over the years. He added: 'Football feels like a second family to me, I love the tribal nature of being among others who support the same team. We all experience the highs and lows of following that team together and you get the feeling that you belong somewhere. 'I used to be a defender, usually right back, and I’m hoping to play in a few fathers’ five-a-side matches. Since having children, I’ve become even more fanatical than I thought I would be about the game. 'I wasn’t like this when I was 18 or 20, I kept an eye from a distance. Now, I probably think and talk about Aston Villa every day. I enjoy looking to see what is going on: the stats, the players’ recovery, tactics and matches.' The Prince is regularly pictured watching his beloved team at Villa Park and across Europe When asked previously about why he settled on the Midlands club, Prince William shared that it was the thrill of supporting a club without season after season of successes which had brought him to Villa. 'A long time ago at school I got into football big time. I was looking around for clubs. All my friends were either Man United fans or Chelsea fans and I didn’t want to follow the run-of-the-mill teams,' he told the BBC in 2015. 'I wanted to have a team that was more mid-table that could give me more emotional rollercoaster moments. 'Aston Villa’s always had a great history. I have got friends of mine who support Aston Villa and one of the first FA Cup games I went to was Bolton v Aston Villa back in 2000. Sadly, Villa went on to lose to Chelsea (in the final). 'It was fantastic, I sat with all the fans with my red beanie on, and I was with all the Brummie fans and had a great time. 'It was the atmosphere, the camaraderie and I really felt that there was something I could connect with.'
