Sports.title: Harry Kane is annoyed at his '50-50' England team-mates who pull out of international duty, reveals Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is annoyed at his '50-50' England team-mates who pull out of international duty, reveals Thomas Tuchel

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Harry Kane is annoyed by team-mates who pull out of England squads – and says his captain would never do so.

Several of the head coach’s camps have been blighted by withdrawals, including Cole Palmer’s ‘load management’ excuse in September. The Chelsea playmaker was then left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League fixtures.

And Tuchel says Kane, who will become England’s record cap-holder with his 126th appearance against Croatia on Thursday evening, is not a fan of those who pass up the opportunity to play for their country.

‘He is always here and doesn’t like it if 50-50 decisions are taken by the players not to come to camp,’ said Tuchel.

‘We had this conversation very early when I took the job and it was one of his points, to make sure that players come and are proud to arrive because it’s the biggest honour.

‘We need to make sure that if it happens (withdrawals) we are so strong that we actually set the tone that everybody is desperate to be in camp, because everybody can lose their shirt if they miss out on a camp.

Thomas Tuchel (centre) has revealed Harry Kane's frustrations at his team-mates pulling out the England squad

Cole Palmer (right), pictured with Kane in 2024, has been criticised by Tuchel for missing too many England opportunities

‘So it was one of the first discussions and straight away he set the standard and made it very clear where the standards are for him. He would never pull out. Never.’

Kane, meanwhile, says his desire burns brighter than ever as he targets 100 England goals and records that will stand for generations.

He insists he is far from finished and has warned team-mates Declan Rice and Jude Bellingham that his caps record could yet reach 150.

‘This is no time to rest,’ said Kane. ‘I've got better year on year. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘Jude and Dec, they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are. So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! Before we know it, it’ll be the home Euros. I might be on 140 caps by then, and then we'll be talking about 150. My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I have an ego to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

Sports.title: HARRY KANE INTERVIEW: England captain opens up on having an 'ego', the secret behind Ballon d'Or glory, the 'tough' moments with his country - and why he isn't finished yet
Sports.content:
HARRY KANE INTERVIEW: England captain opens up on having an 'ego', the secret behind Ballon d'Or glory, the 'tough' moments with his country - and why he isn't finished yet

Harry Kane is contemplating his ego. England’s humble superstar, believes the outside world at least, does not have one. He laughs when reminded of his endearing habit of fiddling with his suit buttons during his Ballon d’Or acceptance speech.

But there must, surely, be one example beneath the modest exterior when he descends into a diva?

‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!’ he returns. ‘But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

Kane does have an ego, only it is measured in goals and self-improvement, not vanity and self-indulgence. He has the records because he wants the records, and he wants them more than all of his rivals. He played more games and scored more goals than Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal last season. After his 126th cap against Croatia tonight, he would have played more games and scored more goals than any player in England’s history. He wants those records to stand, too. Ego, you see.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ says Kane, as we chat at England’s base at the Tottenham Hotspur training ground. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record (currently 91) is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!’

It’s better than good, Harry. It is hard to believe now, but Kane was billed as a one-season wonder after his 31-goal breakthrough campaign at Tottenham 11 years ago. He remembers that, just like he does rejection by Arsenal aged eight years old, his missed penalty against France at World Cup 2022, the loan spell at Norwich when he was demoted to the reserves and the loan at Leicester when he sat alone in his flat and wondered if he was good enough for the Premier League.

England captain Harry Kane has admitted he has 'an ego to be the best' after winning the Ballon d'Or

‘I’ve had to prove people wrong my whole career,’ he says. 'If someone tells me I can’t do something, it motivates me to do it more. You look at all the great athletes, Tom Brady and that unwavering mentality to be the best. Maybe with me, because I’m a calm person and you don’t see the ego of some of these great players, it doesn’t mean I don’t want it as much as everyone else. It doesn’t mean I don’t put in the work and drive myself and everyone around me to be the best.

‘Getting released that early (by Arsenal) and proving them wrong. Proving my early coaches at Tottenham wrong, who I wasn’t playing as much under. Loan moves that didn’t go well. The World Cup in Qatar, missing that penalty was a really tough moment for me. After that, I scored the next 30 penalties! It’s the same thing, “I’m going to show them”, using all the negative stuff as motivation to push me to another level.’

Then there was Euro 2024, when Kane was substituted in the final defeat by Spain after an hour. The popular opinion went that his best days were behind him and England needed a new striker. He has since scored 25 goals from 27 international games. So much for the decline.

‘It was tough, getting taken off in a final,’ he says. ‘There was so much talk (before the final) around, “Maybe Harry shouldn't start”. I was like, “Well hang on a minute, I'm doing my best for the team here”.

‘I scored three goals and was joint for the Golden Boot. It wasn't like there were many other players doing crazy stuff that I wasn't doing. But from my own standards, I know I probably didn't quite reach the level that I could have. I don't think the team reached the level that we could have. After that, my position was under pressure. That motivated me to make sure that it wasn't. I was going to have to do even more to keep my place. From that moment, you've seen an improvement in me.’

Spend time with Kane, even just half an hour, and you realise he isn’t done yet.

’In football, you’ve never completed it,’ says the Bayern Munich star. ‘No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’

You could never accuse Kane of not giving his all. His ego, the best kind of ego, would never allow anything else. England's greatest player is the diva who makes only demands of himself.

Sports.title: Tom Brady breaks his silence on shock exit from Birmingham City as NFL legend posts heartfelt statement
Sports.content:
Tom Brady claims investing in Birmingham City was 'one of the most rewarding journeys' of his life as he addressed his shock exit from the Championship club for the first time.

It was revealed on Monday that the NFL legend had sensationally quit Birmingham just three years after joining as a minority investor.

In a statement, posted to Instagram on Tuesday, Brady paid tribute to Blues fans, players and manager Chris Davies.

'Being part of Birmingham City Football Club the last three years has been one of the most rewarding journeys of my life,' he wrote.

'Thank you to the players, Chris Davies and his staff, the front office, and to everyone working behind the scenes, whose commitment I saw up close at every level of the club.

'Most of all, thank you to the people of Birmingham. Your passion, your loyalty, and the way you show up for this club through every high and every hard day are what make it so special. I'll always be rooting for your success. Keep Right On.'

Tom Brady said investing in Birmingham City was 'one of [his] most rewarding journeys'

It was revealed on Monday that the NFL legend had sensationally quit the Championship club

His comments came after the Blues said in a statement on Monday night: 'Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

'It was amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.'

The seven-time Super Bowl winner joined Birmingham as a minority investor as part of a takeover spearheaded by billionaire Tom Wagner's Knighthead Capital in the summer of 2023.

Brady's presence in English football was detailed in a five-part documentary on the new ownership's plan to revamp the Midlands club, titled: 'Built in Birmingham: Brady and the Blues'.

Within the Amazon series, Brady notably questioned Wayne Rooney's work ethic after hiring him to replace John Eustace.

The fly-on-the-wall documentary showed Brady visiting the Birmingham training ground to observe Rooney's team meeting and training session. While driving away, he tells his business manager Ben Rawitz: 'I'm a little worried about our head coach's work ethic.'

Rawitz replies: 'Comes across as lackadaisical.' Rooney was sacked after 83 days in charge.

The documentary later saw Brady admit his error in replacing Eustace with the former England international and reveal that he was warned against making 'sweeping changes' so early in his time with the club.

'I had good advice, "Don’t go in there and make sweeping changes. You guys have time",' said Brady. 'But we made sweeping changes that put us in decline. That was our doing.'

In a statement on Instagram, Brady paid tribute to fans, players and manager Chris Davies [Source: Instagram/@tombrady]

He hired Wayne Rooney as manager but the former England captain was sacked 83 days later

Under the aegis of Brady and Knighthead Capital, Birmingham City have launched what the group see as a 20-year megaproject, with £3 billion ($4 billion) earmarked for investment in a 'Sports Quarter' in the city.

The 48-acre site in the east of the city is set to feature a new 60,000-seater stadium and training ground above a network of underground transport tunnels.

But since the plan was announced, there have been some wrinkles with the timeline – pushing the stadium's completion deadline from 2029 to 2031.

Daily Mail Sport understands that London-based architects Heatherwick Studio – in conjunction with Kansas City-based Manica – are set to work on a design with a 'chimney theme' in a nod to the city's industrial heritage.

Peaky Blinders creator and famous Bluenose Steven Knight is believed to be working with the team to ensure it is 'one of the most-talked about stadium designs ever'.

Last season, Brady had promised promotion to the Premier League. The club are top of the Championship going into the last international break of the year, though he has departed before they can reach the top flight again.

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Why Will Wright is the breakout star of Reds academy - LEWIS STEELE reveals club's plans for 6ft 3in hat-trick hero, his rise from Euxton Villa to Anfield and why coaches believe he's Andoni Iraola's next big thing
Sports.content:
On Will Wright’s last two trips abroad, he has needed to check in some extra baggage on the return flight.

Two UEFA Youth League away games, two hat-tricks and a pair of match balls to go with them. It’s now 13 goals for the season for 19-year-old Wright after his treble in a 5-3 win at Fenerbahce last week, and he has earned a first England youth call-up to boot.

Another hat-trick in one of those three games for the Young Lions? You wouldn’t bet against it – but Wright is used to these rapid rises.

Eighteen months ago, the 6ft 3in striker signed for Liverpool on a Friday, passed his driving test at 8am the next morning and then played for the first team the day after in a friendly at Anfield.

Now, the former Salford City striker is the name on everyone’s lips around Kirkby – with many thinking he could be the next cab off the rank from Liverpool’s famed academy.

So who is he – and how high can he go?

Will Wright has lit up the academy goal charts this season for Liverpool, scoring a pair of hat-tricks in the UEFA Youth League

The Under 19s captain struck a brilliant treble against Fenerbahce last week to take his season tally to 13

Wright was first spotted by Salford scouts when playing for local side Euxton Villa, a ninth-tier club who have two England internationals in their alumni in David Unsworth and Sam Johnstone. Wright’s father, Mark, coached at Euxton and is an ex-professional for Preston North End.

It was an unusual path as most future stars are normally signed up by their mid-teens but Wright had injury issues amid a growth spurt that took him to the lanky frame that now bullies defenders. He had heel issues and has worked with a specialist on fascia problems.

Wright made his Salford debut in an 8-0 FA Cup defeat by Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City in January 2025 but scouts had already been alerted by his 50-goal haul at youth level. Arsenal, led by then-academy chief Per Mertesacker, launched an aggressive approach to sign him.

At one point, Liverpool signalled to Wright and Salford that they were pulling out of the deal, given Arsenal’s interest was so advanced. But the Reds soon returned to prevent the Gunners signing their next ‘Wrighty’.

The deal was worth peanuts in the grand scheme of things, around £300,000. It is good money for League Two Salford, though, and they will be set for additional payments for first-team appearances, honours and future national team caps.

Wright, who has a younger brother and is a Nike athlete, is a throwback No9. It is easy to reach for comparisons to current players but the way he combines pace, power and prolific finishing is not too dissimilar to Erling Haaland.

He is a strong dribbler and scored a fantastic solo goal for Liverpool's Under 21s against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy in September, receiving possession on the touchline around halfway, tricking his way past two defenders and curling a sumptuous effort into the top corner.

He is the captain of the Under 19s team and I have watched him play live several times, including one game last season where he was clearly targeted by Atletico Madrid defenders. The striker was clattered, suffered a medial ligament injury and was sidelined for several months.

He is a strong dribbler and scored a fantastic solo goal for Liverpool's Under 21s against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy in September

Coaches have pinpointed hold-up play and heading as two things to work on, as well as instructing Wright not to ‘rise to the bait’ of bigger defenders who might try to ruffle him up

He has returned with a vengeance, with a hat-trick against LASK last month and then last week's effort against Fenerbahce. What impressed more in the latter was not his goals – one a penalty, the other two both true poachers’ finishes – but his assist.

Wright was on a hat-trick at the time but, instead of shooting, he played a ball to Finn Inglethorpe – son of academy director Alex – to score. Earlier, Wright and Josh Sonni-Lambie had argued over who was to take a penalty. Wright won the row and scored.

Under 21s boss Rob Page told the pair later that he would rather them show hunger to score and passion rather than shy away. Page is a huge fan of Wright and said: ‘There was a real maturity about his performance. One of the parts of the development for all the forwards is being unselfish in their actions.

‘As much as he wants to see the headlines and be successful himself, it is all about sharing that. Will has done that really well today with a hat-trick, a complete performance.’

Pressed on how far away Wright is from the first team, Page replied: ‘He doesn’t have to worry about that. Just bring the best version of yourself every day in training, give absolutely everything in games as he does. The rest will take care of itself.

‘He’s got a great support around him. His family are very supportive. Alex (Inglethorpe) is there to lean on, he’s got myself and Jay (Spearing, academy coach). He never gets carried away.’

Coaches have pinpointed hold-up play and heading as two things to work on, as well as instructing Wright not to ‘rise to the bait’ of bigger defenders who might try to ruffle him up. They have also worked on his off-the-ball runs to the back post.

So, what next? It is understood a January loan is being considered. Liverpool think toughening up Wright in a senior league could be a step worth taking, having used him in each of the last two pre-seasons. His agent was at the AXA Training Centre on Tuesday and there will be no shortage of clubs willing to take him on.

Liverpool think toughening up Wright in a senior league could be a step worth taking, having used him in each of the last two pre-seasons

Wright got six minutes off the bench against Como at Anfield in pre-season, coming on for Alexander Isak up front

Andoni Iraola will be consulted, too. He has called up the likes of Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and Luke Chambers this season and is eager to use young stars.

Iraola is in frequent dialogue with youth staff such as Page, Inglethorpe, plus Luiz Fernando Iubel who is often cited as the ‘link’ between the academy and first team.

The Brazilian has been spotted at several academy games this term, including for Wright’s hat-trick in Turkey where Iubel sat alongside sporting director Julian Ward and loans manager Gary Probert.

Whether a first-team breakthrough comes now or in the future, the future for Wright looks bright.

Van Dijk out, Szoboszlai to follow?

Dominik Szoboszlai’s participation with Hungary this week remains in the balance with the national team trying all they can to get their captain fit for crunch games.

The Hungarians take on Georgia and Northern Ireland in must-win Nations League games – and may have to go without their star boy. Szoboszlai hurt his knee in the win at Crystal Palace and, after an injury-hit six weeks, could do with a rest.

But he will try his best to be fit for national team duty and a decision will not be made until the 11th hour.

It comes after Virgil van Dijk pulled out of Dutch duty with a minor muscular issue. It is believed he has been managing the problem for at least a month and was surprised to be substituted on to the field against LASK — which might explain the team conceding three after he came on!

Virgil van Dijk (left) has pulled out of international duty and Dominik Szoboszlai (right) could be set to follow him

Loan watch: Harvey’s back!

Confidential readers will recall our musings on Harvey Elliott a fortnight ago, with Valencia sources telling us that the La Liga outfit might consider cancelling his loan in January.

The English midfielder had struggled in Spain for fitness and form. He was then sent off but, as we reported, Valencia would give him another chance to prove his worth.

He has started well, scoring a free-kick in what was his first start for any club in 285 days. It was part of a notable 6-0 win in the Copa del Rey.

Elliott ran over to fans and put his arms aloft appearing to apologise, which adds to his comments a week ago about the red card where he said: ‘I made a mistake and I’m truly sorry. It won’t happen again.’

Sports.title: Man United set to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach: Club reach agreement with former Spurs boss - with Michael Carrick's exit likely to be confirmed TOMORROW
Sports.content:
Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as head coach to replace Michael Carrick following a day of talks over both men. United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. Meanwhile, the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were in Monaco where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer. Carrick’s departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino’s appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday. Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday. It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester. Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager - but he took training as usual on Wednesday Pochettino, who has managed Southampton,Tottenham, and Chelsea, will succeed Michael Carrick Carrick checked in at Carrington at 7.45am on Wednesday with his fate in the balance He was pictured leaving Manchester United's training base at around 1.15pm Pochettino is pictured working on United States national team duty on Tuesday (Source: X/USMNT) The second leg is Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later. It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave. It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill. The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m. The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer. Amid the secret talks between United and Pochettino’s camp on Wednesday, there was more intrigue when the federation cancelled media access to the players at late notice but allowed cameras to film an open training session. Sources said the decision was made out of respect for Veterans Day in America, but it also meant the players didn’t have to field any awkward questions over their coach’s future. Bournemouth midfielder Tyler Adams was quoted by the US media as saying: ‘Why would his name not be on it (United’s list)? Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are meeting in Monaco for talks today The United execs meet in Monaco today (Pictured is the Casino Monte-Carlo in Monaco)

Your browser does not support iframes.

‘I mean, the credibility, the resume speaks for itself. It goes to show for us how lucky we are to be able to work under a manager of his quality and the person he is.’ Meanwhile, Berrada and Wilcox flew back to Manchester from Nice on Wednesday with United expected to announce Carrick’s departure imminently after 10 months in charge. The 45-year-old took training at Carrington for the second day running, arriving at 7.45am and leaving shortly after 1.30pm. However, it has been clear for some days that Carrick would lose his job after United dropped into the relegation zone following the club’s worst start in 40 years.

Sports.title: Harry Kane sets new England target as he admits he could lose Three Lions record
Sports.content:
Harry Kane sets new England target as he admits he could lose Three Lions record

Harry Kane will eclipse Peter Shilton as England men's most capped player of all time when he leads out the Three Lions vs Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night

View 3 Images England captain Harry Kane addresses the media

Harry Kane will write his name into the history books again at Wembley - and insists he is already eyeing his next target.

‌



‌



Kane, 33, will become England’s most-capped player of all time when he makes his 126th appearance and surpasses Peter Shilton’s record on the back of winning the Ballon d’Or.

‌



But Kane insisted that he will “never set limits” because he wants to put his own goal record out of sight and also lead his country to a major trophy during his international career.

‌



England captain Kane, who has scored 91 goals in 125 caps, said: “I think not setting limits is a big thing. At any stage, if you feel like you're going to slow down: ‘OK, you've reached that record, and now you’re going to slow down.’

“But ultimately, if anything, I've gotten better year on year, and the numbers have got better. While I'm feeling like this, there's no limit on it, why would I do any limit on it? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible.

"They've come around quick, even just from making 100 caps to now, breaking the records, it was only a couple years ago, so a lot of these things seem a long way away but the seasons go quick and before we know it, it’ll be the Euros in 2028.

‌



“To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream. It’s always been my biggest dream to win a European Championship, a World Cup or both hopefully. I know how difficult that is so I'm extremely motivated to do that.

View 3 Images Kane is already England's record scorer - with a tally that will be almost impossible to usurp

‌



“I’m surrounded by great teams, both club and country, so hopefully it is an exciting time ahead."

Kane admits that Declan Rice - who is on 80 - and Jude Bellingham - already on 80 aged just 23 - may catch him in terms of caps but he wants to put the goals record out of sight.

‌



The England striker will receive a celebratory cap during a pre-match presentation led by Shilton and, remarkably, Kane says he has never met the legendary keeper beige.

View 3 Images Kane has admitted the likes of Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice could eventually take his caps record

‌



Kane added: “When you look at Jude and Dec, for example, they're on 60-odd caps already and how young they are. So I'll try and give them a good number to catch. The goal record, of course, is going to be one that's difficult to beat for a while, I think that’s good.

“Whilst I'm in this place, of course, is to try and set these records as high as I can, one day look back and see if anyone can catch them.

Article continues below

“I don't think I've ever met Peter Shilton before. It'll be nice to have that presentation from him, but also hopefully get to catch him after and just have a brief conversation on how much it meant to him. I'm sure he's proud that I've broken it now.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane on still proving critics wrong and bouncing back from lowest moments of his career
Sports.content:
History-maker Harry Kane says he has enjoyed “proving people wrong his whole career.”

Captain Marvel Kane, 33, will become England’s most-capped player of all time when he makes his 126th appearance against Croatia at Wembley on the back of winning the Ballon d’Or.

But Kane referenced his early days when he was rejected by Arsenal aged eight, his difficult loan spells at Norwich and Leicester and being as nervous as a kid on his first day at school when he first reported up for England.

It was a fascinating insight into Kane’s mentality and also his reputation as a humble superstar as he insisted he could not think of any “diva moments” but maybe that was a question for his wife Kate.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the biggest England stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Thomas Tuchel confirms if he has Mauricio Pochettino clause with new hint on club return READ MORE :

Bayern Munich star Kane has been driven by targets throughout his rise from Tottenham’s academy and, even after reaching the very top, he is determined to carry on aiming for more.

Kane said: “I think it’s just my mindset, because I’ve maybe had to prove people wrong my whole career.

“From early academy days proving coaches wrong, proving scouts wrong – it has just been instilled in me. I think if someone tells me I can’t do something it just motivates me more to do it.

‌



“I don’t think that mentality will ever leave me. It’s probably part of what makes me push myself to the limits that I do because in football, you’ve never completed it, really.

View 4 Images Kane struggled during loan spells at the start of his career

“No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has or whatever it may be, I think there’s always something. But it just helps motivate me to realise there’s a lot more to achieve.”

Those early days and setbacks have also become part of Kane’s identity and the driving force behind his success. From being farmed out on loan to being nervous at his first England camp.

‌



“There’s been a few lows! The toughest part of my career to begin with was the Norwich and the Leicester loans,” recalled Kane. “But when I look back at it now it gave me a certain type of resilience to help me along the rest of my career.

“The World Cup in Qatar, I’ve spoken to you about this, missing the penalty was a really tough moment for me but again the way I bounced back. And even the fact that I scored the next 30 penalties of my career … I changed the technique a little bit. It made me improve.

“I felt nervous coming into my first England camp. I remember Wayne being the first one to talk to me. He was captain at the time and he told me to just be myself and you know it’s kind of relaxed here with the team.

View 4 Images After scoring on his England debut, the international goals have never slowed

‌



“But I was always confident once I got on the pitch. I felt this is my comfort zone, I know what I can do, I can score goals.”

Kane has not stopped scoring since. His record-breaking goal haul last season earned him the Ballon d’Or and long overdue recognition as one of the best in the world.

He shocked English football not so much by leaving Tottenham as much as opting to go to Germany with Bayern Munich and yet that has helped him take his career to another level.

Kane added: “‘The move has done a lot for me. I think it's made me appreciate European football more. Obviously, growing up in the Premier League, playing in the Premier League, sometimes we're all a bit guilty of just thinking the Premier League is the only thing that exists.

‌



“Going to Bayern, going to the Bundesliga, seeing the fans, seeing the reactions, playing the latter stages of the Champions League for a team like Bayern Munich, the pressure that comes with that, that has all elevated me to another level.

View 4 Images Harry Kane with the Ballon d'Or in front of his adoring Bayern Munich fans

“But going for £100 million and people saying, “He’s going for £100 million, he needs to score this many goals or he needs to follow in the footsteps of Robert Lewandowski and all these things.

“I know people say that Bayern are expected to win, but you still feel the pressure of big games in the title races, big cup games in the German Cup, playing in finals. There's still a big pressure that comes with that. I think that was maybe one of the things I did learn a lot.

‌



“I think I maybe under-appreciated how hard it is still to win even when you're in the best team. But yes, now I've won the trophies and I've been in those moments, I feel even more comfortable in those situations.”

Sports.title: Ben Kay responds to claims of England rugby team unrest - 'It can galvanise the players'
Sports.content:
Ben Kay responds to claims of England rugby team unrest - 'It can galvanise the players'

The build-up to England's win over Australia was dominated by a report in The Times claiming that senior players had demanded talks with coach Steve Borthwick and senior figures at the RFU.

View Image Henry Slade of England talks to Henry Pollock (Image: 2026 The RFU)

England had to batten down the hatches after reports of a toxic environment but a record points tally against Australia is just the tonic for any grumbling in the changing room.

‌



‌



The build-up to Sunday’s Nations Championship clash at Allianz Stadium was dominated by a report in The Times claiming that senior players within the England squad had demanded talks with coach Steve Borthwick and senior figures at the RFU. Vice-captain Jamie George questioned the contents of the report, as well as its timing, and England’s response on the pitch was emphatic with a 45-22 win over the Wallabies – the most points they have ever managed against Australia.

‌



For World Cup winner Ben Kay, the idea of a completely harmonious changing room where everyone is satisfied is naïve – highlighting his own experience with an all-conquering England side. However, he feels that any frustrations can be eased by the magnitude of this opening success.

‌



“From my experience, not everyone is always happy in a team environment,” said Kay. "There's a difference between things being catastrophically wrong and someone simply having a bit of a grumble because they'd prefer things to be done differently.

“For example, the most successful team I ever played in was coached by Clive Woodward. He deserves enormous credit for what he achieved and the system he put in place. But if you'd asked every player in that squad whether they thought Clive was doing a good job at any given time, there would have been some who felt he wasn't.

“I think what happens in that situation is that it can actually galvanise the players and bring them together a little bit more. They've all heard about it. Some will have read it, and some might feel they're part of the reason it's appearing in the media. But if you're desperate for your team to be successful and to go away and win a World Cup, you're not going to deliberately sacrifice your team's performance to make a point in the media.

‌



“I think it's also amazing what winning does for you. When you win together, that shared sense of achievement makes you forget the things you were moaning about a few weeks earlier.”

While the England players have been at pains to reject the contents of the report, which came after the country’s worst-ever Guinness Men’s Six Nations campaign, they did acknowledge that there have been some forthright conversations with the coaching staff. The 80 minutes against Australia, during which England ran in seven tries, was an indication of the bond within the team.

‌



And while Kay does not believe that the report was entirely unfounded, he does not feel that there will be a witch hunt to see where leaks are coming from in the changing room.

He added: “I think when you're involved in a sporting environment, it's very difficult to keep everything within the changing-room walls. These rumours don't necessarily start with players putting their hands up, ringing a journalist and saying, "I'm not happy here." It might happen because they speak to an agent or someone back at their club, and that person asks a question.

Article continues below

“They might have a bit of a whinge, it gets passed around, becomes a rumour, and then a journalist picks up on it and starts trying to establish whether there's any truth to it. As I said, when you see something written down in black and white, it looks catastrophic. But it's very rare that everyone in a team is always thinking, "This is the best it's ever been. Everything is great."”

Sports.title: Arsenal star forced to address exit rumours as £100m-rated replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Arsenal star forced to address exit rumours as £100m-rated replacement lined up

Arsenal star Martin Zubimendi has been linked with an exit from north London as the Gunners prepare to battle it out for Bournemouth's Alex Scott

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi's decrease in minutes has seen him linked with an Arsenal exit

Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi has made it clear that the transfer noise surrounding his next move is not impacting him and even he is surprised by some of the reports regarding his future at the Emirates.

‌



‌



The Spaniard has fallen down the pecking order and as a result links with Atletico Madrid and Chelsea have emerged. Zubimendi only moved to Arsenal last summer from Real Sociedad, with Mikel Arteta paying £60million for a player who had long been on his radar.

‌



But since being a regular, Zubimendi has seen Myles Lewis-Skelly start the Champions League final ahead of him and in the summer the club signed Bruno Guimaraes, limiting his opportunities even further.

‌



Zubimendi addressed the rumours about his future and said: “I haven't wasted any energy on outside thing. I'm busy enough trying to earn a place, get playing time, and fight to win this Premier League, which is looking so promising. I haven't spent any energy on it, nor have I contacted anyone."

He also added: “To be honest, I'm sometimes surprised by the press too,” he said. “I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I've also read that I might be close, but not at all.”

Gunners in Scott race

Arsenal have reportedly revived their interest in Alex Scott, who will retains the £100m price tag Bournemouth previously slapped on him. Theipaper understands that the Gunners are willing to do battle with Chelsea and Liverpool in the race for the 23-year-old.

‌



Scott scored for the Cherries when secured a statement win at the Emirates last season and has continued to blossom since joining the club from Bristol City.

View 2 Images Bournemouth star Alex Scott has been linked with several top Premier League sides (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



It was understood that Arsenal were keen on Scott in the summer but Bournemouth had made it clear he was not for sale. That stance has ultimately changed and the club are now willing to listen to offers in light of Scott turning down a contract offer.

Panel rule on penalty

An independent panel has ruled that Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt in Arsenal's victory at Anfield recently.

‌



The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel assesses refereeing incidents across every Premier League match and voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot kick, which could've changed the course of the game. The Gunners would secure a narrow 1-0 win.

The panel also voted 3:2 that VAR Stuart Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

Sports.title: England's Red Roses told what must happen now after losing four-year unbeaten streak
Sports.content:
England's Red Roses told what must happen now after losing four-year unbeaten streak

The world champions suffered their first defeats in nearly four years in October, with a 41-match unbeaten streak coming to an end at the hands of Canada, who recorded back-to-back victories to avenge last autumn’s World Cup final defeat.

View Image England's Red Roses lift the 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup trophy at Allianz Stadium (Image: World Rugby)

Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt feels England’s Red Roses will benefit from ‘a little shake-up’ as they seek to ‘energise and refocus’ following the loss of their invincible tag.

‌



‌



The world champions suffered their first defeats in nearly four years in October, with a 41-match unbeaten streak coming to an end at the hands of Canada, who recorded back-to-back victories to avenge last autumn’s World Cup final defeat. England bounced back with a convincing 55-12 win over USA and Hunt is looking forward to seeing how the squad continue to respond to unfamiliar adversity.

‌



Hunt said: “I don’t know if it’s a new challenge. We always pride ourselves on our performances, our standards, and go after what we believe is the right way to play. It is about getting back to the way we want to play, our determination on the pitch and showing how much it means to play for each other.

‌



“I’m not saying we’ve lost that by any stretch of the imagination, but a little shake-up is really important to energise and redirect our focus.”

Hunt, 37, returned to action against Australia in September after recovering from the knee ligament injury she sustained in the Six Nations opener against Ireland.

“I got injured playing for the Red Roses, so for my first game to be for England as well was pretty high stakes,” she said. "I’ve not had to come back from too many big injuries, so it was a challenge. It was something I had to get my head around.

‌



“I didn’t quite hit the ground running as much as I would have liked, but it’s an absolute honour to pull on the shirt. I'll do anything for that group of girls, my whole life has been dedicated to being the best I can be for the Red Roses.”

The scrum-half was speaking at Allianz Stadium as England’s men got the second half of their Nations Championship campaign underway with a 45-22 win over Australia.

‌



A proud alumnae of Dene Magna School in Mitcheldean, Gloucestershire, Hunt hopes the Allianz Kick Start Programme can help provide opportunities for fellow state school kids to follow in her illustrious footsteps.

The Kick Start programme offers teachers at primary schools resources to lead six lessons of non-contact rugby to introduce children to the sport.

Article continues below

Hunt, who is a qualified PE teacher herself, added: “In the boys’ and men’s game at private schools, rugby is a big part of their curriculum - whereas we’ve never had that in the girls' and women’s game. You might get three or four people that love the game, find a rugby club and go there. It’s all about access and opportunity.”

Allianz and England Rugby will support over 5,000 primary schools across the country through the Allianz Kick Start flatpack rugby programme.

Sports.title: Man Utd players 'wanted Unai Emery' as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on job
Sports.content:
Man Utd players 'wanted Unai Emery' as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on job

Manchester United are close to appointing Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager but several players were hoping to see Unai Emery hired from Aston Villa

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is poised to become the next Man United boss (Image: David Berding/Getty Images)

A bulk of the Manchester United squad were keen to see Unai Emery appointed as their new manager - but the club are closing in on Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



‌



The Red Devils' poor start to the season has them sat in the relegation zone, their lowest spot at this stage of a campaign for forty years, and Michael Carrick is set to pay the price as United's senior figures meet in Monaco.

‌



Pochettino has emerged as the frontrunner to replace him and the Premier League giants have struck an agreement to free him from his contract with the USA, which he recently signed. That will allow him to take over at Old Trafford.

‌



But whilst this has become public knowledge talkSPORT reports that a host of players at Old Trafford were keen to see Emery arrive at the club. He was among several names linked with the job and his work at Aston Villa has put him on the radar of every major club.

Ironically the Spaniard was left fuming on Sunday when he visited Old Trafford. His Villa team twice let a two-goal lead slip to draw 4-4 and Emery walked down the touchline before the final whistle after Villa conceded for the fourth time.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

During his time at Villa, Emery has bolstered his reputation with many seeing him and Arsenal's Mikel Arteta as the two outstanding managers in the Premier League. Emery has twice landed Champions League football with Villa and last term delivered another Europa League crown.

‌



He's done so whilst having to balance the books and again saw a host of his leading lights leave Villa Park this summer. His previous spells at Valencia, Sevilla and Villarreal have also contributed to his stock being so high.

The only red mark against his name are the underwhelming stints he had at Arsenal and PSG. He lasted two years in Paris, less in London, but in both jobs more was expected and handling the pressures that come with a heavyweight club has been cited as something he will want to address one day.

‌



View 2 Images Unai Emery has several admirers among the Man United players

Pochettino's last job in England was at Chelsea, where he lasted just one year. He led them to sixth before being moved on. However it was with Tottenham that the Argentine marked himself out as one of the best young managers on the planet.

Article continues below

He led the club to third and then second in successive seasons and that success in north London saw him linked with the United job, most notably in 2018 when he was seen as the man who should've replaced Jose Mourinho in Manchester. However Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's stellar interim spell, which included a win at Tottenham, saw him land the job.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua winner urged to face 'hard done by' rival next
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua winner urged to face 'hard done by' rival next

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally set to settle their decade-long feud in a mouthwatering heavyweight showdown on December 11 in Cardiff

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

The winner of Tyson Fury's mega-fight showdown with Anthony Joshua should fight Murat Gassiev next.

‌



‌



That is according to former professional boxer Paulie Malignaggi. Fury and Joshua will meet in a mouthwatering all-British heavyweight bout on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

‌



Ahead of the blockbuster clash, the WBA decided to sanction the Cardiff clash for their 'super' title. Gassiev initially won the WBA 'regular' title against Kubrat Pulev back in December. Earlier this year, two-time undisputed heavyweight Oleksandr Usyk shocked many by vacating his titles.

‌



Many felt as if Gassiev was the champion waiting in the wings until the WBA opted to unveil their bizarre plans for Fury's meeting with Joshua. And Malignaggi feels as if the Russian scrapper has been brutally snubbed and believes the winner of next month's fight should take on Gassiev next.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

‌



Daniel Dubois told to avoid Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury could be cancelled after late objections READ MORE :

"Yeah, I wasn't crazy about that. I think it's a bit of a political move by the WBA," Malignaggi revealed to talkSPORT. "I think Murat Gassiev was the one who deserves to be upped. I've seen that it's sort of the move that WBA makes in the past.

"So to just skip by Gassiev and make the WBA title fight, which now is the super title is unfair. But politics play these roles in boxing and money talks and bull***t walks as they say. So unfortunately, I think Murat Gassiev is being done wrong here because I think he should be the guy to be upped and in the very least have dibs on the winner. They should enforce that, but I somehow got a feeling that they're not going to do that."

‌

However, should Joshua find himself getting his hand raised in Cardiff - it appears that there is one name on his mind as to who he would ideally like to face next. And it isn't Gassiev. According to Eddie Hearn, Joshua wants to avenge his defeat to Daniel Dubois. The pair met two years ago, with 'Triple D' dropping 'AJ' multiple times before stopping his rival in the fifth stanza.

“I can’t speak on Tyson’s behalf, but for [Joshua], he still wants to be in the biggest fights of the sport,” said Hearn. “I’ve got to be honest with you, and I know it’s a very dangerous fight, but he wants to rematch Daniel Dubois. [Joshua] is a competitor, so he’s looking at that…and anyone who has ever beaten him, he’s rematched, apart from Daniel Dubois.

Article continues below

“He wants to have another go at Daniel Dubois, and this is second nature to him. He wants to try to avenge that defeat. It’s a dangerous fight, but if he goes through Tyson Fury and stops Tyson Fury, then why not? That would be for a title unification – or for a fight against [Filip] Hrgovic.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino ready to accept Man Utd offer as Red Devils open talks with USA
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino ready to accept Man Utd offer as Red Devils open talks with USA

Michael Carrick is set to be sacked as Manchester United manager following a summit of Red Devils chiefs in Monaco today and Mauricio Pochettino is favourite to replace him

View 2 Images Pochettino is ready to accept United's offer (Image: John Walton/Press Association)

Mauricio Pochettino is closing in on a deal to become Manchester United’s next manager. Pochettino has a £7m buy-out clause written into his contract with the US Soccer Federation and he is ready to accept United’s offer.

‌



‌



United have now opened talks with the US Federation but things are unlikely to move until Michael Carrick’s future is resolved.

‌



The United hierarchy are meeting in Monaco where they are expected to decide to part ways with Carrick and then press ahead with a move for Pochettino who has become their unanimous choice.

‌



United chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe are discussing the club’s plans but it has left Carrick hanging because he did turn up to the club’s training ground on Wednesday morning.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



There is also an issue for Pochettino because the United States two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti over the next week.

That means there is unlikely to be an immediate announcement on Pochettino but the US are fully aware of the interest.

‌



Pochettino, who has been linked with the United job on three separate occasions in the past 10 years, signed a new contract in August to stay in charge until 2030.

Argentine Pochettino did a good job with the United States at the World Cup and convinced the federation to give him a new deal until 2030 - but the ex-Spurs and Chelsea boss never hid his desire to return to club management in the future.

‌



That explains his buy-out clause in the contract and United is a huge appeal to Pochettino who loves English football, living in England and this is a job he has found impossible to resist.

View 2 Images Carrick is set to be sacked as United gaffer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



United are 18th in the Premier League - inside the relegation zone - after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August. It is United’s lowest position at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87 when they were 20th.

It is understood that, while United looked at other candidates like Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, it was Pochettino who actually had the most overwhelming support and the decision to move for him will be a unanimous one.

‌



There were reservations with all the other potential candidates and Pochettino’s style of play, personality and charisma have also made him a very popular choice with the fans.

Even though the next few days may drag out over Pochettino’s appointment, the hope is he will be in charge well before United’s next game which is at Liverpool on Sunday week.
