Sports.title: Frank Warren Must Protect Moses Itauma From Himself
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma wasted no time seeking redemption after suffering his first career loss, immediately lobbying promoter Frank Warren for a direct return bout with Filip Hrgovic. Warren, however, has other plans.

Warren revealed that the young heavyweight blew up his phone following the August stoppage.

“He was on the phone the day after, and the day after that, and the day after that, but as I said to him, we had to pay Frank Sanchez to step aside, and that’s the position,” Warren said to DAZN News.

Sanchez originally stepped aside to allow the initial clash to happen, securing his spot as the mandatory challenger for Hrgovic’s IBF heavyweight title. Reports indicate Hrgovic and Sanchez will likely collide in Croatia during early 2027. Itauma is slated to return to action early next year against a ranked contender.

Warren taking his foot off the gas is the only sensible move. Itauma looked sharp out of the gate against Hrgovic, banking the opening stanzas with poise. The wheels fell off in round 3 once Hrgovic began putting hands on him.

Itauma did not react well to incoming fire. A look of panic crept across his face, exposing a young fighter utterly bewildered by an experience he never anticipated. That reaction is the direct byproduct of soft matchmaking. Having bypassed elite amateur competition, Itauma spent his developmental run feasting on fragile opposition that fell apart under early pressure.

When Hrgovic stood firm, Itauma tried a Shakur Stevenson step back, giving up ground in a straight line with his head stuck on the center line. Hrgovic recognized the amateur defensive flaw instantly, closing the distance like a shark stalking injured prey. Trapped along the ropes, Itauma abandoned his boxing technique, loading up on wild individual bombs in a desperate bid to punch his way out of trouble. Hrgovic timed the predictable swings, walked him down, and closed the show.

Warren will not fix these glaring deficiencies in a single training camp. A lone confidence builder against a hand-picked opponent solves nothing. Itauma needs five to ten genuine, grueling learning fights against durable, prime contenders who will test his chin, force him past six rounds, and make him solve problems under real fire.

Rushing Itauma back into a rematch after blasting out an overmatched opponent would be promotional negligence. Until he learns how to survive under distress, another date with Hrgovic will produce the identical outcome.

Sports.title: Ben Shalom Says Chris Eubank Jr vs Kell Brook Terms Nearly Agreed
Sports.content:
Ben Shalom says terms are nearly agreed for Chris Eubank Jr. to fight Kell Brook, with Boxxer targeting February for a DAZN pay-per-view. Brook is 40. He has been out of the ring for more than four years. Boxxer is banking on domestic nostalgia to sell a bout detached from any legitimate world title picture.

“I think the fight happens. I think pretty much terms are agreed on both sides,” Shalom told Pro Boxing Fans. The Boxxer promoter expects Eubank to headline the February card, pitching Brook as the opponent fans want to see. The fight remains unannounced, and Shalom mentioned no weight limit.

Brook won his IBF belt at 147 pounds. He finished Amir Khan at a 149-pound catchweight in February 2022. Eubank operates at middleweight and super middleweight. Brook ventured to 160 pounds against Gennadiy Golovkin, suffering a stoppage loss along with a shattered orbital bone. Errol Spence Jr. fractured Brook’s other eye socket the following year. A strict catchweight below 160 pounds forces Eubank to cut harder, yet Brook still enters the ring against a naturally bigger man who leans, roughs up opponents inside, and unloads heavy volume.

Brook relies on his straight right hand to halt aggressive opponents. A timed counter over a lazy jab forces fighters to hesitate. Trouble arrives if Brook reacts a split second late. Eubank closes distance rapidly, chaining flurries together before an older opponent sets his feet. A four-year layoff destroys spatial timing and depth perception faster than punch resistance. Brook must measure distance against a larger fighter closing the gap, then absorb the return fire when the tempo accelerates.

Boxxer capitalized on Khan against Brook because British fans spent a decade arguing over the rivalry. That personal animosity made the pay-per-view an event. Eubank and Brook share zero history. Boxxer assumes name recognition alone generates buys, testing whether casual viewers will pay for an opportunistic, manufactured pairing.

Shalom cited Anthony Joshua against Tyson Fury as reason to shift the card off a crowded December calendar into February. Moving dates avoids domestic clashes, yet February puts the event directly into post-holiday consumer fatigue. Streaming subscribers must justify paying an extra fee for a non-title showcase between veterans.

For Eubank, the event represents a safe payday over risky bouts against active middleweight champions like Janibek Alimkhanuly or Carlos Adames. Beating an inactive 40-year-old former welterweight proves nothing at world level. A Brook win produces a memorable upset, yet offers nowhere to go next. Boxxer is simply wagering that old memories can carry a pay-per-view broadcast.

Sports.title: Zuffa Boxing Protects Carlos Adames With Warburton Mismatch
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames (24-1, 18 KOs) brings his WBC middleweight title into a non-title showcase Saturday in Riyadh against Gerome Warburton (16-2-1, 2 KOs) at a 165-pound catchweight.

The pairing delivers an immediate highlight-reel platform for Zuffa Boxing’s promotional arrival. It also freezes mandatory challenger Meiirim Nursultanov (20-0, 11 KOs) out of his rightful championship opportunity for a third consecutive year.

The tactical matchup offers zero competitive parity. Warburton is a domestic-level 160-pound fighter stepping up in weight against a champion who routinely rehydrates into a functional super middleweight on fight night. Warburton managed two narrow decision wins over Nathan Heaney earlier this year, but his technical limits were laid bare when Kieron Conway stopped him inside four rounds. Conway exploited Warburton’s low lead hand, backing him into the ropes with straight punches before finishing him with clean combinations.

Adames operates with far greater spite in the pocket, using heavy hooks around the guard to punish stationary targets. With two knockouts across 22 professional bouts, Warburton carries no offensive threat to discourage Adames from walking through his jab.

The promotional strategy mirrors Dana White’s traditional UFC playbook. Instead of risking a newly signed champion against an avoided mandatory, Zuffa imported the MMA formula of pairing an elite talent with an outmatched opponent to manufacture viral knockout content. Bringing that closed-league matchmaking into boxing directly compromises divisional legitimacy, substituting competitive merit for controlled promotional optics.

The sanctioning terms expose the financial machinery driving the delay. The WBC granted Adames a special permit to compete at 165 pounds just before an October 20 negotiating deadline with Nursultanov expired. Under these terms, Warburton cannot win the belt, yet an upset vacates it entirely. Adames shoulders all the physical risk for zero middleweight progression.

Nursultanov, who secured his mandatory status by defeating Julio Alamos in late 2023, remains unpaid on the sideline while the sanctioning body stacks administrative fees across interim titles, special permits, and delayed mandatories.

The middleweight division remains locked in an administrative holding pattern designed to protect commercial interests. If Adames scores the expected stoppage on Saturday, the WBC must immediately force the defense against Nursultanov rather than clearing the deck for another promotional detour.

Sports.title: Sugar Ray Robinson’s Schedule Could Send Jai Opetaia to Palookaville
Sports.content:
Dana White believes a standout victory over Deontay Wilder could launch Jai Opetaia into global stardom. Joseph Parker and Zhilei Zhang both defeated Wilder without achieving that level of fame.

Opetaia will certainly reach a massive viewership when he moves up to heavyweight on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua Netflix undercard in Cardiff on December 11. What remains uncertain is how much credit he will actually receive for toppling a 41-year-old Wilder.

“Imagine if on this Netflix card Opetaia knocks him out or wins this fight spectacularly, everything is open and available to Jai Opetaia,” White told Sky Sports. “He’s got Australia and New Zealand. The more he wins, the higher profile fights he has, the bigger he becomes, not just there but all over the world.”

Zhang already produced the highlight-reel finish White envisions, stopping Wilder in five rounds shortly after Parker outpointed the former champion. That victory earned Zhang plenty of attention, but the immediate aftermath focused on whether Wilder was completely washed up. Opetaia could finish Wilder even faster and run into that identical reaction.

Matching a peak, 31-year-old cruiserweight world champion like Jai Opetaia against a faded Wilder is pure matchmaking cynicism. Wilder has looked gun-shy, flat-footed, and empty ever since Tyson Fury knocked him out in their rematch in 2020. He was utterly neutralized by Joseph Parker and poleaxed by Zhilei Zhang.

If Dana White actually wanted to prove Opetaia can handle real, giant heavyweights rather than selling an empty illusion, names like Bakhodir Jalolov or Teremoana Teremoana would provide legitimate answers.

The 6’7″ Jalolov, with two Olympic gold medals, is an undefeated, razor-sharp southpaw with skills. He possesses elite technical pedigree, range discipline, and heavy hands from both sides. Facing Jalolov would force Opetaia to deal with real size, modern ring IQ, and a southpaw who actually punches back, rather than an aging slugger praying for one punch he rarely throws anymore.

Teremoana Teremoana, 6’6″, Australian Olympic silver medalist knockout artist signed to Matchroom, brings regional drama. A clash between Opetaia and Teremoana would interest Australian fans, pitting two undefeated, explosive punchers against each other in a genuine clash. Unlike Wilder, Teremoana is young, aggressive, hungry, and has zero miles on his odometer.

Beating an active, giant super-heavyweight like Jalolov or Teremoana would prove Opetaia belongs among the big men. Flattening an older Wilder simply proves Opetaia can clean up what Zhang and Parker already handled easily.

“He’s willing to fight all the time,” White remarked, referencing Sugar Ray Robinson’s relentless activity. “That’s how you become a legend. Jai is one of those guys.”

Robinson operated in a completely different universe. He fought 20 times in 1941 and 19 times in 1950 because that era demanded it. Fighters traveled by train, fought 10 or 15 rounds every two to three weeks, rarely engaged in grueling 10-week strength and conditioning camps, and lived off gate receipts. Robinson was a generational genius, an absolute physical freak of nature, and fighting was his primary livelihood.

Attempting to apply that template to a modern cruiserweight or heavyweight is absurd for several reasons. Opetaia already broke his jaw in two places against Mairis Briedis. If he tried to fight even five or six times a year against world-class opposition, his body would fall apart long before he made it to Robinson’s numbers.

Modern champions are paid millions per outing. Networks, streaming platforms, sanctioning body mandatory cycles, and multi-million-dollar guarantees simply do not support a champion fighting every month. Promoters cannot afford to stage an elite fighter seven or eight times a year unless they put him in non-televised gym wars against journeymen.

The Risk of Palookaville. Pushing a 31-year-old fighter to maintain an antique, frantic schedule against dangerous heavyweights is the fastest way to get him injured, burnt out, or knocked cold by someone who caught him on three weeks’ rest.

White comes from the UFC promotional model where the company owns the platform, controls the contracts, and wants talent constantly cycling through the machine. Dropping Sugar Ray Robinson’s name is just White trying to romanticize old-school grit while ignoring the stark medical and economic realities of 21st-century boxing. Opetaia fighting three times a year would already be considered hyperactive by championship standards; expecting anything resembling Robinson is pure nonsense.

Sports.title: Jarrell Miller Faces Tony Yoka in Ghana on December 20
Sports.content:
The WBA’s top-ranked heavyweight contender meets the 2016 Olympic gold medalist, with Jonathan Tetteh fighting Elvis Ahorgah on the undercard.

Jarrell Miller will fight Tony Yoka at The Grand Arena inside the Accra International Conference Centre on Sunday, December 20, 2026, live worldwide on DAZN. Matchroom and Legacy Rise Sports will promote the card in association with BXG and Queensberry Promotions.

The event marks Matchroom’s second show in Ghana. Miller enters after defeating Kingsley Ibeh by split decision and outpointing Lenier Pero in April, victories that helped him climb to No. 1 in the WBA heavyweight rankings.

The Brooklyn heavyweight now faces a former Olympic champion as he pursues a world title shot. The announcement does not name a championship opponent for the winner.

“This is a serious fight and one that will cap an incredible month of heavyweight boxing,” Matchroom Sport chairman Eddie Hearn said. “Jarrell Miller is ranked No. 1 in the world, and a win over a tough, former Olympic Champion in Tony Yoka will undoubtedly set him up for some major nights ahead in 2027. It will be an absolute war.”

Miller’s No. 1 position refers specifically to the WBA contender rankings.

Yoka captured super heavyweight gold at the 2016 Rio Olympics and recently defeated Kostiantyn Dovbyshchenko over six rounds. The French heavyweight has also boxed in Africa, stopping Patrick Korte in the opening round in Nigeria.

Jonathan Tetteh Meets Elvis Ahorgah

Ghanaian light heavyweights Jonathan Tetteh and Elvis Ahorgah will meet on the supporting card. The announcement lists Tetteh at 12-0 with 11 knockouts and Ahorgah at 15-4 with 13 stoppages.

Tokyo Olympic bronze medalist Samuel Takyi joins the bill at lightweight with a listed record of 9-0, all nine wins coming by knockout. Super flyweight Theo Allotey, listed at 15-0 with 11 knockouts, will also compete.

Liverpool super welterweight Odel Kamara will box for the second time after scoring a third-round stoppage on his debut. His mother comes from Ghana.

Cruiserweight Divine Omojor also returns after winning his professional debut by knockout in Sheffield. Dutch lightweight Jursly Vargas, listed at 10-0 with nine knockouts, heads back to Accra after stopping Isaac Dowuona there in April.

Legacy Rise Sports CEO Sharaf Mahama pointed to Ghana’s championship history, including Azumah Nelson, Ike Quartey and D.K. Poison, when discussing the event.

“We look forward to putting together another blockbuster on DAZN alongside our partners at Matchroom Boxing and BXG and giving Ghanaian, and worldwide, fans a night to remember,” Mahama said.

Sports.title: Jai Opetaia Gets WBC No. 2, Awaits Benavidez vs. Cieslak
Sports.content:
Jai Opetaia landing at No. 2 in the latest WBC cruiserweight rankings changes little about his immediate path. The Australian already holds a guaranteed crack at the winner between David Benavidez and Michal Cieslak courtesy of the WBC’s ruling in September.

The real drama scheduled for December 5 in Glendale is scale: whether Opetaia walks into a three-belt unification blockbuster against Benavidez over Cinco de Mayo weekend, or finds himself facing Cieslak solely for the WBC green strap.

Opetaia locked down official mandatory status by halting Noel Mikaelian in September. WBC bylaws dictate that occupying the top spot in the rankings does not automatically confer mandatory rights; the governing body must issue an explicit order. Opetaia holds that formal mandate in hand, giving him ironclad leverage regardless of who emerges victorious in Arizona.

“The fight that I got to honor first is the fight with Opetaia because I told him I’d fight him Cinco de Mayo next year,” Benavidez revealed on Brian Custer’s show.

Clinging to that No. 2 WBC ranking like a life raft looks completely neurotic when you look at the reality of the situation. Benavidez has not been playing coy. He got right into the ring with Opetaia in September, looked him dead in the eye, and told him they were doing this on Cinco de Mayo.

Fighters do not commit to a date on a holiday weekend in front of a live broadcast unless they genuinely want the scalp. He’s eager for this matchup because he looks at Opetaia and sees someone who is fundamentally vulnerable around the whiskers. He watched Opetaia get hurt by Huseyin Cinkara and Noel Mikaelian

To a volume puncher like Benavidez, who drowns people under relentless flurries and body punches, a guy with a suspect chin and an aggressive offensive style is tailor-made target practice. Benavidez does not fear Opetaia’s power; he thinks he can walk him down, clip him, and turn his lights out.

Yet Team Opetaia is acting like they need Mauricio Sulaiman and a WBC paper trail to save them from being bypassed. If Benavidez is practically begging to fight you because he thinks you have a glass jaw waiting to be cracked, you do not need to hide behind WBC bylaws or celebrate a No. 2 ranking. You just show up, let him sign the contract, and try to prove him wrong. Right now, all the anxiety coming out of Opetaia’s corner makes them look terrified that the cash-out might evaporate if Benavidez decides to look elsewhere.

All the holiday talk creates an ideal spoiler scenario for Cieslak. An upset in Glendale hands him the unified crown while shifting the WBC mandatory obligation directly onto his shoulders. Even with three belts on the line in December, Opetaia’s contractual entitlement applies strictly to the WBC belt under sanctioning bylaws, leaving any full unification terms subject to fresh administrative approvals.

A Benavidez triumph fulfills the public pact struck between the two fighters following the Mikaelian clash. Finalizing that Cinco de Mayo showdown would still require both promotional outfits to hammer out broadcast splits and purse distributions, with the looming threat of a WBC purse bid deadline if talks drag out. Before any contracts can be printed for May, Cieslak gets the first opportunity to tear up the script.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia’s $100M Bluff to Lure Floyd Mayweather Out of Retirement
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is daring Floyd Mayweather Jr. to put his spotless 50–0 record on the line for a theoretical nine-figure payday.

The reigning WBC welterweight champion insists he will put the 49-year-old icon to sleep, claiming Mayweather will wake up $100 million richer for his trouble. The catch is simple: nobody has stepped forward with that kind of capital.

Garcia laid out his pitch on Kick with signature bravado: “Then, you wake up, and you’ve got $100 million. That’s good. You’re just going to get knocked out real quick. You love money, right? I’m going to test that theory on how much you love money.”

The math makes that purse an enormous stretch. At $80 per purchase, 1.5 million pay-per-view buys yield roughly $120 million in gross revenue. Once cable platforms, satellite providers, and streaming distributors take their cuts, production overhead gets covered, and Garcia secures his own check, a $100 million guarantee for Floyd evaporates.

Live ticket sales and brand sponsorships bridge some of the divide, but any backer writing that guarantee is gambling heavily. They must bet that modern audiences will shell out premium cash to see an aging Mayweather enter a real contest after a decade of theatrical exhibitions. Garcia generated massive numbers against Gervonta Davis, yet that blockbuster relied on Davis bringing an equally rabid audience.

Mayweather built an empire around being untouchable, an aura he preserves through low-risk exhibition tours. An authentic 12-round championship scrap completely shatters that protective bubble.

Ryan’s signature left hook poses immediate physical danger to a fighter turning 50, testing whether Mayweather’s legendary shoulder roll and counter instincts can outrun Father Time. Floyd stepped into a pro ring last in 2017 to dispatch Conor McGregor. He has not fought an elite, active professional boxer since outpointing Andre Berto in 2015.

Sanctioning politics complicate the picture just as much. WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman signaled that Mayweather could challenge for the title pending medical clearance and standard licensing. Even so, the WBC would face intense scrutiny for greenlighting a 49-year-old on a nine-year professional layoff ahead of deserving, active welterweight contenders.

With a broadcast partner, host city, and signed contracts entirely absent, Garcia’s February 6 target date looks increasingly like theater. Pointing toward Mayweather keeps Garcia dominating headlines while he entertains a practical matchup against Teofimo Lopez. Mayweather loses nothing by ignoring the noise. Garcia is the fighter with a date to fill, and finding a partner to share the stage matters far less than finding someone willing to fund it.

Mayweather isn’t 39; he turns 50 in February. At nearly half a century old, the physical drop-off is a complete biological cliff. In his exhibitions over the last couple of years, the reflexes, the spring in his legs, and the twitch speed that defined his prime are simply gone. What remains is muscle memory, shell defense, and pacing himself against novices, YouTubers, and MMA fighters who do not know how to cut off a ring or throw punches with real professional malice.

Putting that version of Mayweather in a sanctioned 12-round fight against Ryan Garcia, who is 28 and carries genuine, explosive power in his left hook, is not a competitive sporting event. A shell defense only works when you have the hand speed and counter-threat to keep a puncher honest. If you cannot deter a prime fighter from walking you down, the shell just turns you into a static target along the ropes. At 147, Garcia would walk through anything Floyd threw back, find the gaps, and the fight would likely be over as soon as Garcia committed to an exchange.

The financial reality makes it an even bigger non-starter. Riyadh Season and the Saudi backers have shown that while they will pay astronomical figures, they are spending with a purpose: legacy unifications, undisputed clashes, and top-tier matchups that build sports authority. The era of writing blank, nine-figure checks for absurd circus acts has dried up, especially with tighter watch on returns.

Paying $100 million to a 49-year-old fighter to take a severe beating in a sanctioned professional bout offers zero prestige and terrible optics. Nobody with that kind of capital is going to underwrite a one-sided blowout, and Floyd’s business instincts are still sharp enough to know that 50–0 is worth far more intact than whatever embarrassment awaits him in a real ring.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Calls Cédric Doumbé a Tune-Up
Sports.content:
Jake Paul plans to let his jab dictate terms when he meets Cédric Doumbé in Dubai on Christmas Eve. During their press conference in Paris, Paul labeled the former GLORY kickboxing standout an easy tune-up, projecting a stoppage inside four rounds. In his breakdown, Doumbé relies on wide, winging hooks that carry obvious warnings and operates behind a porous guard.

“Yeah, a lot of wild looping shots, no straight shots; everything he throws is predictable. He telegraphs his shots. He doesn’t set anything up. But he does have power, you know, behind them sometimes. Doesn’t have a good jab, not so good defense, and his chin is in the air. The body is open. There’s a lot, there’s a lot,” Paul said.

That critique points out real technical gaps, but it glosses over how kickboxers control space. In kickboxing, the threat of low kicks forces an opponent to stay light on their lead leg, preventing them from sitting down comfortably on a straight left. In a pure boxing ring, Paul steps forward without that hesitation. That lets him establish lead-foot dominance, pin Doumbé to the ropes, and lean on his cruiserweight bulk to tie up the smaller man whenever exchanges get chaotic. Doumbé spent the bulk of his combat career competing near 170 pounds, meaning Paul holds a clear frame advantage to grind on him along the perimeter.

Doumbé cannot afford to stand at mid-range waiting to time a home-run shot, because Paul will simply bank rounds behind the jab. His genuine opportunity comes from exploiting Paul’s habitual flaw: dropping the rear hand to chest level when stepping out of a combination. If Doumbé utilizes twitchy shoulder feints to draw Paul’s jab into the same rhythm, he can slip inside the line and fire his overhand right while Paul’s lead shoulder is fully extended. That requires disciplined ring cutting rather than the sudden forward blitzes Doumbé often used in GLORY.

Doumbé made no secret of his primary motive, pointing out the odd dynamic of facing an executive who signs the paychecks. “My boss will pay me to knock him the fuck out,” Doumbé stated. He gets eight rounds to prove his explosive power carries into a 200-pound cruiserweight ring on December 24 at Coca-Cola Arena.

Ghana News.title: Account for failed 24-hour Economy before selling us ‘new 24-hour economy’ slogan – Dr. Amin Adam to Finance Minister
Ghana News.content:
Former Finance Minister, Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam, has fired a major salvo at the government ahead of tomorrow's presentation of the 2027 Budget, demanding that the Finance Minister first account for the failed promises of the 24-Hour Economy before asking Ghanaians to embrace the new "New Economy" slogan.

In a blistering open letter released today, Dr. Amin Adam accused the government of celebrating a "paper economy" while the "pocket economy" of ordinary Ghanaians continues to hurt, citing a KPMG pre-budget survey in which 71% of respondents named jobs and youth employment as their top priority.

He questioned the credibility of the government's proposed US$10 billion New Economy programme, the decision to cut the primary surplus target from 1.5% to 0.5% of GDP to fund it, and the recent reversals in inflation and the cedi, warning that the country cannot afford another repackaged promise without financing, milestones and measurable jobs.

The full letter is reproduced below:

Of Failed Promises and Repackaged Slogans: Ghana Needs Jobs, Not Another Economic Catchphrase - An Open Letter to the Minister for Finance

Honourable Minister,

Ghana does not suffer from a shortage of economic slogans. What we lack are sufficient productive jobs, thriving businesses, rising real incomes and the economic freedom that allows ordinary citizens to improve their lives through enterprise and hard work.

Tomorrow, you will present what your government has christened the "New Economy Budget." But before asking Ghanaians to embrace another grand economic slogan, perhaps you should first account for the promises of the old one.

Not long ago, the NDC government promised a transformative 24-Hour Economy, backed by ambitious investment and employment targets. Ghanaians were promised jobs, expanded production and new opportunities. Yet the government has not provided a sufficiently convincing and independently verifiable account of jobs created, investments mobilised or businesses transformed under that programme. Now comes the "New Economy." What exactly is new, beyond the branding?

The economic reality confronting ordinary Ghanaians is considerably less glamorous than the government's slogans suggest.

The KPMG pre-budget survey released today provides a sobering reality check. Some 71 percent of respondents identified jobs and youth employment as a national priority, while 54 percent cited the cost of living. These are not abstract economic indicators. They reflect the everyday anxieties of households struggling to make ends meet and young people searching for opportunities.

Inflation may have fallen substantially, but lower inflation does not mean prices have returned to affordable levels. October's headline inflation of 5.5 percent still masks sharper pressures in essential services. For households facing accumulated price increases and constrained purchasing power, macroeconomic stability must mean more than favourable statistics.

The findings from KPMG's survey highlight continuing pressure on household budgets despite the fall in headline inflation from its earlier peaks.

Indeed, the pocket economy is hurting whilst the paper economy is being celebrated.

Those concerns should be central to the 2027 Budget, rather than overshadowed by celebrations of macroeconomic gains.

Honourable Minister, we acknowledge the importance of policy continuity. Your government has maintained important elements of the economic stabilisation and reform efforts initiated under the previous NPP administration, including the Gold Purchase Programme and the debt restructuring process. Indeed, inflation had already declined from its peak of 54.1 percent in December 2022 to 23.8 percent by December 2024, before your administration took office. The fall in inflation was 31 percentage points. Under your government, it fell further to 3.2 per cent in March 2026, a decline of 19.8 percentage points. Therefore the subsequent disinflation represents further progress, but it did not begin in January 2025.

Yet recent developments also demand caution as we have observed a worrying trend of reversals in economic gains.

Inflation, having fallen to around 3.2 percent earlier in 2026, increased to 5.5 percent by October. The cedi, following its substantial appreciation in 2025, had depreciated by approximately 9.5 percent against the US dollar by September 2026. These developments do not erase the stabilisation gains entirely, but they demonstrate how fragile those gains can be.

Growth figures also warrant closer scrutiny. According to the Bank of Ghana, real GDP growth moderated from 6.6 percent in the second quarter of 2025 to 6.0 percent in the corresponding quarter of 2026. More importantly, non-oil GDP growth slowed from 8.5 percent to 5.4 percent, while agricultural growth declined from 7.1 percent to 3.9 percent.

Interestingly, ICT continues to contribute significantly to economic growth. The same digital economy that the NDC, the President, you and your foot soldiers once sought to dismiss as a distraction from economic management is today an important source of growth under its own administration. This should provide some perspective on the digitalisation agenda championed by Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. Economic progress is cumulative, and governments should acknowledge the foundations upon which they build.

Now comes your proposed US$10 billion New Economy investment programme, equivalent to approximately US$2.5 billion annually over four years. Where will the money come from, and how much of it is genuinely new?

The reported financing framework proposes reducing the primary surplus target from 1.5 percent to 0.5 percent of GDP, alongside additional revenue mobilisation. But relaxing a fiscal target does not create new wealth. It permits additional spending, potentially at the expense of faster debt reduction. Why should the country weaken an important fiscal anchor so soon after a painful debt restructuring?

If the government intends to amend the fiscal framework, it must demonstrate that the resulting fiscal space will finance genuinely productive investments, rather than recurrent expenditure, politically attractive projects or spending pressures ahead of the next elections.

And if the government has yet to convincingly demonstrate the financing and implementation of its earlier US$4 billion 24-Hour Economy ambition, why should Ghanaians embrace another US$10 billion promise without demanding a credible financing plan, clear implementation milestones and measurable employment outcomes?

The central issue is not the size of the announcement but the credibility of the financing, the quality of the investment and the economic returns it will generate.

Ghana certainly needs economic transformation. But transformation is not achieved by renaming programmes, multiplying policy acronyms or announcing increasingly ambitious investment figures. It requires fiscal discipline, competitive businesses, affordable credit, reliable infrastructure, productive investment and institutions capable of delivering results.

Economic growth is not a slogan. Jobs are not created by press conferences. Prosperity cannot be legislated into existence, and economic freedom cannot be delivered through political branding.

As you present the 2027 Budget, the real test will not be how compellingly you describe the New Economy, but whether you can demonstrate how it will be financed, how it differs from previous promises and how it will improve the lives of ordinary Ghanaians.

Before unveiling a New Economy, account for the 24-Hour Economy.

Ghana needs a functioning economy, not another freshly packaged promise.

Ghana News.title: We want to give them a show – Thomas-Asante pledges ahead of Somalia test
Ghana News.content:
Coventry City forward Brandon Thomas-Asante has said the Black Stars are eager to put on a show for fans in the Western Region, ahead of Thursday’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON 2027) Qualifier against Somalia.

Ghana, who are bottom of Group C with zero points, need to win both games against Somalia.

Speaking ahead of the game, Thomas-Asante said, ‘‘We want to make sure that we give them a show that everyone wants to see. On a personal note, I’d rather show than tell what I do, but I hope that people have been able to see over a period of time the energy and the passion that I bring on the pitch, mixed with always being a goal threat and also like to put on a show for the fans as well. I think that’s part of the Ghanaian way of making football beautiful.’’

Thursday’s match will be a first for Ghana at the Sekondi Sports Stadium, since hosting Lesotho at the venue in 2009.

On Wednesday, a section of the fans who attended the team’s training made a good impression on Thomas Asante, who was training in the stadium for the first time.

‘‘It’s a real blessing because even when we got off the bus for training, you could feel the atmosphere. There’s an energy. It’s a change. It’s positive. We also recognise that there’s support all across the country. To be able to have these two games here is a blessing.’’

Ghana will face Somalia at the Sekondi Sports Stadium on Thursday at 3 PM, before meeting at the same venue on Monday for the reverse fixture.

Ghana News.title: Kojo Brace officially declares intention to contest NPP parliamentary primaries in Ahanta West
Ghana News.content:
Former JoyNews presenter Samuel Kojo Brace has declared his intention to contest the New Patriotic Party (NPP) parliamentary primary in the Ahanta West constituency of the Western Region.

Brace announced that he had formally submitted his expression of interest to the party's National Elections Directorate on Friday, November 6, 2026.

In a video shared on his official Facebook campaign page, The Ahanta Pele, he thanked supporters for their encouragement and advice throughout the process.

“Thank you for the continued support, the love, the critique, the advice, and the prayers. They have indeed shaped the journey over the past months,” he said.

He added that his decision followed consultations with constituents and NPP members in the constituency.

“I did, after broad consultations with constituents and members of the NPP, having come to a conclusion that I have what it takes to take this constituency to a level that we all aspire it to be,” he said.

Brace said he hoped to work with the party's constituency executives and members to strengthen the NPP's appeal in Ahanta West.

The former journalist expressed confidence in his ability to secure the party's nomination and win back the parliamentary seat for the NPP.

“I know that with God on my side, I will be able to take this seat back to the NPP. I know that you and I will work together to take this constituency to where it has to be,” he said.

He cited his background in the constituency as a reason for seeking the seat, saying he was born and raised in the area and understood the challenges confronting residents.

“I understand the issues that confront this constituency, so I believe I can help provide solutions to our challenges better than anyone,” he added.

Brace also expressed appreciation to supporters who had contacted him to find out whether he had completed the submission process.

The NPP opened its portal for prospective parliamentary aspirants to declare their interest from November 1 to 10, 2026.

The party is expected to hold its parliamentary primaries ahead of the 2028 general elections, with successful aspirants seeking to represent the NPP in constituencies across the country.

Brace's submission marks the beginning of his bid to secure the party's ticket in Ahanta West.

Ghana News.title: Interim Black Stars coach admits challenging circumstances
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s interim manager Kim Lars Bjorkegren has admitted the unique challenges ahead of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers against Somalia.

Bjorkegren was appointed as interim Black Stars coach after Carlos Queiroz resigned from his role as Black Stars coach last month.

Speaking ahead of his first match in the men’s game, Bjorkegren, who is also the current Black Queens coach, said, ‘‘Yeah, of course there has been less preparation for me, but I am doing my best.’’

‘‘I have been around a little bit, in Europe to watch some players. I have tried to connect with more or less all the players by phone, and now they are here in Ghana where we have had two training sessions, and we will have another one.’’

Ghana are bottom of Group C, having lost their opening two matches to Ivory Coast and The Gambia.

The Black Stars need to win their next two matches – both against Somalia- to stand a chance of qualification.

While acknowledging the challenges, Bjorkegren also sounded confident his team will execute his game plan on Thursday.

‘‘There have been some meetings, of course, where we have discussed how we want to play, how we want to create chances, score goals and how we want to win this game.’’

Ghana will face Somalia at the Sekondi Sports Stadium on Thursday at 3 PM, before meeting at the same venue on Monday for the reverse fixture.

Ghana News.title: ENNY Foundation wins award for autism advocacy and special needs support
Ghana News.content:
The ENNY Foundation has received the Paragon of Autism Advocacy and Special Needs Excellence award at the fifth edition of the Eminent Awards, in recognition of its work supporting children with diverse learning needs and promoting inclusive education.

The award was presented on October 31, 2026, at the National Theatre in Accra during the awards' fifth anniversary celebration, known as the Quintessence Edition.

According to the foundation, the recognition reflects years of work providing intervention and support for children and families, training parents, teachers and caregivers, and promoting more inclusive learning environments.

The citation traced the foundation's beginnings to the volunteer work of its founder, Emmanuel Ntow Nyarko, who worked with children requiring additional educational support before establishing ENNY as a platform for intervention, training and advocacy.

The foundation provides home- and school-based support to children, with programmes targeting communication, play, attention, social interaction, academic skills and participation in everyday activities.

It also works with families and schools to help extend children's learning beyond individual intervention sessions and into their home and educational environments.

ENNY's work also includes autism awareness activities, professional development and engagement with educators and caregivers to promote understanding and inclusive practices.

Through its ENNY Beyond Borders initiative, the foundation says families from outside Ghana have travelled to the country to access intensive intervention and family support.

The programme brings children, parents and the foundation's team together for focused intervention, alongside transition planning to help families continue supporting children's development after returning to their home countries.

The Eminent Awards, which operates under the theme “Celebrating Excellence, Encouraging Hard Work & Creativity,” recognises individuals and organisations for their contributions to society.

ENNY said the award was dedicated to the children and families it serves, as well as the schools, partners, staff, volunteers, educators and caregivers who have contributed to its work.

The recognition comes as the foundation approaches eight years since receiving its operating permit and completing its legal registration.

It says the award will encourage it to expand its work in family support, professional training, autism advocacy and inclusive opportunities for children in Ghana and beyond.

Ghana News.title: Mahama woos Thai investors for 12,000-hectare oil palm plantation in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has encouraged Thai investors to pursue plans to establish a 12,000-hectare oil palm plantation and a modern processing mill in Ghana.

He said the government was ready to support the proposed investment, which is being discussed between the Tree Crops Development Authority and prospective Thai investors.

President Mahama made the appeal when he welcomed Thailand's new Ambassador to Ghana, Thirapath Mongkolnavin, and reaffirmed Ghana's commitment to strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries.

He said Ghana was keen to deepen cooperation with Thailand, particularly in areas that could promote economic growth and development.

“The growing interest of the Thai business community in Ghana is appreciated and I encourage further investment in manufacturing, agriculture, agro-processing technology and infrastructure,” he said.

The President acknowledged the contributions of Thai companies operating in Ghana, including Thai Union Group and Indorama Ventures Packaging, describing their investments as valuable to the Ghanaian economy.

He also expressed support for ongoing discussions towards a bilateral investment treaty and the establishment of a Ghana-Thailand Business Council.

According to him, the proposed arrangements would help facilitate trade, protect investments and strengthen partnerships between businesses in the two countries.

President Mahama further encouraged the continuation of engagements between the Tree Crops Development Authority and potential Thai investors on the proposed oil palm project.

“I encourage you to continue the engagement between the Tree Crops Development Authority and prospective Thai investors in advancing the proposed establishment of a 12,000-hectare oil palm plantation and a modern processing mill in Ghana,” he said.

He assured the Ambassador of the government's readiness to provide the necessary support to strengthen economic ties and ensure a successful tenure.

“Ghana is ready to work closely with you and reaffirms its commitment to deepening bilateral ties with Thailand, which are founded on mutual respect, shared interests and a common desire to promote economic growth and development,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Ghana committed to strengthening bilateral relations with South Africa despite postponement of BNC – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says Ghana remains committed to strengthening its longstanding friendship and bilateral relations with South Africa despite the postponement of the third session of the countries' Bi-National Commission (BNC).

He says the postponement was due to prevailing challenges affecting people-to-people relations between the two countries.

Receiving Letters of Credence from South Africa's new High Commissioner to Ghana, Ms Linda Vuyolwethu Shongwe, and ten other envoys, President Mahama said Ghana remains committed to deepening the partnership in the interest of the longstanding bonds of friendship and solidarity.

He said, “The third session of the BNC (Bi-National Commission) was postponed due to the prevailing challenges affecting our people-to-people relations.

However, in the interest of our long-standing bonds of friendship and solidarity, Ghana is committed to further enhancing bilateral relations between our two countries”

President Mahama acknowledged a virtual senior officials meeting held in the first quarter of 2026 between the two countries to discuss the status of implementation of decisions reached at the second Bi-National Commission.

He reaffirmed Ghana's commitment to the partnership, which he said was anchored on longstanding friendly relations dating back to the struggle against apartheid.

"I warmly welcome you to Ghana and reaffirm our commitment to the strong partnership built with your country, which is anchored on long-standing friendly relations and dates to the era of the fight against apartheid," he said.

The Bi-National Commission(BNC) is a formal bilateral cooperation mechanism between Ghana and South Africa, through which the two countries discuss and coordinate areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, security, education, tourism and diplomatic relations.

The postponement of the third Ghana-South Africa Bi-National Commission followed heightened diplomatic tensions between the two countries in June and July 2026, after renewed anti-foreigner protests and xenophobic attacks in parts of South Africa.

Ghana’s government said the prevailing atmosphere could overshadow the objectives of the bilateral engagement, originally scheduled for August 4-7, 2026, in Accra.

President Mahama also congratulated South Africa on the successful conclusion of its G20 presidency and commended its efforts in advocating for Africa's priorities on the international stage.

Ghana News.title: AFPNC founder calls for expanded NHIS coverage, longer maternity leave for mothers of premature babies
Ghana News.content:
Founder and Executive Director of the African Foundation for Premature Babies and Maternal Care (AFPNC), Selina Bentoom

The Founder and Executive Director of the African Foundation for Premature Babies and Maternal Care (AFPNC), Selina Bentoom, has called for expanded National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) coverage, increased investment in neonatal care and longer maternity leave to improve survival outcomes for premature babies in Ghana.

She said the high cost of neonatal intensive care, gaps in health insurance coverage and inadequate support for parents after hospital discharge continued to expose premature babies and their families to significant challenges.

Speaking on the sidelines of the 3rd Purple for Prematurity Summit 2026, Ms Bentoom said some essential and expensive aspects of neonatal care, particularly medications, were not covered by the NHIS, leaving families to bear substantial out-of-pocket expenses.

She called for urgent expansion of the scheme to cover essential neonatal services, including psychological support and follow-up care, to ensure that babies receive holistic support both in health facilities and after discharge.

She warned that some babies were abandoned in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) because their mothers could not afford the cost of care or even transportation for regular hospital visits.

Ms Bentoom acknowledged government and stakeholder efforts but stressed the need for greater urgency and investment to prevent babies from dying because their parents could not afford essential treatment.

She also called for stronger family-centred care, urging healthcare institutions to introduce initiatives that encourage fathers to participate more actively in caring for premature babies.

According to her, some fathers withdraw from their families because of fear and a lack of understanding of the challenges associated with prematurity, rather than deliberate neglect.

She said healthcare facilities should provide an environment that educates and empowers men to support mothers and their babies instead of judging them.

On workplace policies, Ms Bentoom advocated an extension of maternity leave beyond the current three months, particularly for mothers whose babies are born prematurely, sick or underweight and require prolonged hospital care.

She said employers must introduce family-friendly policies that allow parents sufficient time to support their babies' recovery and development.

Ms Bentoom further urged businesses, pharmaceutical companies and other private-sector players to support maternal and newborn healthcare through innovative products, services and public-private partnerships.

She explained that broader stakeholder involvement was necessary because the needs of premature babies and their mothers extended beyond the hospital environment to workplaces, homes and communities.

The AFPNC founder said the third edition of the summit, held under the theme Small Babies, Big Potential: Invest in Follow-up Care to Protect the Future of Our Babies, was aimed at expanding stakeholder engagement and treating prematurity as a national development and healthcare priority rather than merely a charitable cause.

She recalled that recommendations from the previous summit, organised in collaboration with JoyNews National Dialogue, were presented to Parliament's Select Committee on Health, which unanimously approved them and referred them to the Ministry of Health and the National Health Insurance Authority.

This year's summit expanded participation to include the Association of Ghana Industries, the Ghana Armed Forces, healthcare professionals, parent advocates and international participants from Uganda.

Ms Bentoom said the foundation would sustain its advocacy through media partnerships, public education, community outreach, fundraising and engagement with government institutions and private-sector organisations.

She disclosed that the organisation's Purple Basket Project had, over the past decade, distributed more than 10,000 baskets containing essential supplies to over 20,000 babies and families across seven regions in Ghana.

The initiative is intended to reduce the financial burden on families by providing basic items for mothers and babies in NICUs, allowing parents to redirect some of their resources towards medical expenses.

She said the foundation would also intensify public education on prematurity, combining scientific information with personal experiences of parents to help families make informed healthcare decisions.

Ms Bentoom urged educational institutions, particularly engineering students, to develop practical solutions to challenges in maternal and newborn healthcare.

Reflecting on the foundation's 11-year journey, she said it had completed more than 50 projects and reached over 700,000 babies and families through collaborative interventions.

She expressed optimism about expanding the foundation's work beyond Ghana and encouraging other African countries to adopt sustainable approaches to improving newborn healthcare.

She stressed that prematurity and maternal health must receive sustained attention and investment, regardless of where babies are born or their parents' financial circumstances.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
