“You must be custodians of order, not champions of disorder; protectors of institutional dignity, not contributors to its erosion,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The director-general said the security of an institution depended not only on its physical infrastructure but also on the character, discipline and commitment of personnel entrusted with its protection.

He reiterated NILDS’ commitment to strengthening the capacity of parliamentarians, legislative staff and the wider National Assembly bureaucracy through research, training and institutional support.

Mr Sulaiman said that more than 300 National Assembly staff had benefited from the institute’s supported master’s and doctoral programmes on a pro bono basis.

He described the initiative as a significant investment in human capital development, adding that a stronger National Assembly required a more competent workforce.

He said NILDS had evolved into a world-class legislative capacity-building institution that had attracted attention from parliaments and legislative institutions across Africa.

The director-general, however, expressed disappointment over the alleged unruly behaviour of some participants following a temporary power interruption experienced on the first day of the training.

He said although participants had the right to express grievances, the manner of communicating concerns must reflect the discipline and professionalism expected of public officers.

“Social media is a powerful communication platform, but it comes with responsibility.

“The unruly behaviour, inappropriate comments and social media posts by some participants were inconsistent with the professionalism expected of officers entrusted with sensitive security responsibilities.

“It was contradictory for personnel responsible for maintaining order and protecting the National Assembly to engage in conduct capable of generating disorder and embarrassing the institution,” he said.

According to him, public officers must understand that their conduct, comments and social media engagements have implications for the institutions they represent.

The director general urged participants to become ambassadors of institutional discipline, professionalism and positive change, ensuring that lessons acquired are reflected in their conduct and operational decisions.

Also speaking, the Secretary of Human Resources and Staff Development, Essien Essien, who represented the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, urged participants to demonstrate the knowledge acquired through improved workplace performance.

Mr Ogunlana said the success of the programme would be measured by participants’ ability to apply the knowledge and skills acquired in discharging their responsibilities.

Quoting John Maxwell, he said: “Training ends, but the impact begins the moment the trainee returns to his desk.”

He commended the NILDS Director-General for facilitating the training programme.

The Clerk also urged participants to exercise their rights responsibly, emphasising that grievances should be communicated through appropriate channels and with respect for constituted authorities.

He said staff had the right to question decisions, seek clarification, and demand accountability, but such rights must be exercised responsibly and fairly.

He consequently directed participants to stand up and apologise to the NILDS Director-General over their alleged unruly conduct during the programme, which they did.

He said the training had achieved its objectives and equipped participants with the knowledge needed to discharge their duties effectively.

(NAN)

World.title: IGP orders additional deployment to communities affected by terror attacks
World.content:
The Inspector General of Police (IGP), Tunji Disu, has ordered the immediate deployment of additional police personnel, operational vehicles and air support to communities affected by terrorist attacks across Nigeria.

Mr Disu gave the directive on Wednesday during a livestreamed monthly strategic conference with senior officers of the Nigeria Police Force in Abuja. The conference was livestreamed on the police’s official Facebook handle.

He also directed commissioners of police in affected states to submit updated security threat assessments and operational requirements to the Force Headquarters within 72 hours.

Mr Disu acknowledged that bandit attacks were continuing in some states, warning that the police would not ignore the threats facing affected communities.

“Bandit attacks are ongoing in some states across the federation, and communities in those areas continue to face real threats to their safety and livelihood,” he said. “This is a challenge we are confronting directly, and I will not allow this conference to pretend otherwise.”

He directed the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police in charge of operations to coordinate the deployment in consultation with the affected state commands.

“The DIG in charge of operations is to coordinate the immediate deployment of additional personnel, mobility and air support to the most affected areas, in consultation with the commands concerned,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Disu said intelligence-led operations must be intensified, while every police command must maintain a standing operational plan for its high-risk areas.

He also called for stronger community intelligence, directing police commanders to engage traditional rulers, village heads, hunters’ associations and local vigilante groups to improve information gathering.

“The people know who the bandits are. We must give them the confidence to tell us,” he said.

Mr Disu said the police must demonstrate its commitment to protecting affected communities through concrete action.

“The bandits do not rest. Neither shall we,” he added.

The directive comes as the federal government seeks to strengthen the police to enable the military to gradually withdraw from internal security operations.

Defence Minister Christopher Musa said last week that the armed forces were overstretched by prolonged deployments across the country and would gradually return to their primary responsibilities as the police improved their capacity.

He said the government was investing in police recruitment, training and equipment to enable the force to handle domestic security challenges more effectively.

Police record operational successes

Despite the security challenges, Mr Disu said the police had recorded operational successes through intelligence-led policing, strategic deployment and collaboration with other security agencies.

He said that since the last strategic conference, the police had arrested 218 suspected bandits and terrorists, 85 suspected armed robbers, 129 murder and culpable homicide suspects, 59 suspected kidnappers and 120 suspected cultists.

The police, he said, also rescued 95 kidnapped victims and recovered 306 firearms, 630 rounds of ammunition of various calibres and 116 stolen vehicles.

Mr Disu commended police personnel for their courage, professionalism and commitment, saying their efforts had contributed to the achievements.

He also paid tribute to police officers killed in the line of duty since the last conference.

“Behind every successful operation are personnel who continue to put their lives on the line in the service of our nation. Let me also pause to honour our fallen colleagues, officers and men who paid the supreme price in the line of duty since our last conference,” he said.

World.title: 2027: IGP cancels leave for police officers, restricts movement of senior officers
World.content:
The Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, has cancelled leave for police personnel assigned election security duties ahead of the 2027 general elections and restricted the movement of senior officers outside their commands.

The police chief disclosed this on Wednesday at a strategic conference with senior officers of the Nigeria Police Force in Abuja. The conference was livestreamed on the police’s official Facebook page and monitored by PREMIUM TIMES.

Mr Disu directed all commissioners of police and other senior officers to remain in their respective commands until the conclusion of the electoral process, warning that anyone travelling outside their area of responsibility must obtain express approval from the Force Headquarters.

“All leave is cancelled for officers and men deployed for election security duties, effective immediately,” he said.

“All Commissioners of Police and senior officers are to remain in their respective commands until the conclusion of the electoral process. Any travel outside your command requires express approval from Force Headquarters,” Mr Disu added.

He also directed commissioners of police to verify the readiness of election security equipment, communication facilities, operational vehicles and protective gear and submit their reports by the end of the week.

Mr Disu further ordered police commands to establish direct coordination with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the military, the State Security Service (SSS, also known as DSS) and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Warning against political interference

The IGP warned police officers against allowing politicians to use them to compromise the electoral process, facilitate thuggery or interfere with voters’ rights.

He said the police would remain non-partisan and provide equal protection to candidates, political parties, their supporters, and eligible voters, regardless of political affiliation.

“I will not tolerate any officer using the authority of the police to advance the interest of any political party, candidate or sponsor,” he said.

“Any officer found to be colluding with political actors, facilitating thuggery, compromising the integrity of the electoral process or interfering with the rights of voters will be disciplined according to the law,” the police boss warned.

Mr Disu cautioned officers against allowing politicians to exploit their positions, stressing that the police would apply its disciplinary procedures against erring personnel.

“The Nigeria Police Force is not a tool for any politician, any party or any interest. If you allow yourself to be used, you will face the consequences alone.

“Protect the process, protect the people, and protect your own career and reputation. Do not be used,” he said.

World.title: Hezbollah chief calls Trump’s midterm defeat ‘an opportunity’
World.content:
Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP.

Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem hailed on Wednesday President Donald Trump’s recent midterm defeat, describing it as “an opportunity” for his Iran-backed Lebanese movement and other opponents of the US in the region.

Trump’s Republican Party suffered massive losses in last week’s elections, in which the Democrats seized control of Congress.

The president has admitted that the war he launched with Israel against Iran in February was a key factor in the defeat.

“Today, we have a good opportunity. Trump was defeated in the elections… an earthquake has occurred in America,” Qassem said in a speech broadcast live to supporters.

“The one confronting Iran, Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen… has lost,” he added, arguing that Trump could “no longer continue as is”.

“His defeat has ramifications for us that are in a way positive.”

He added that Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu “has been broken” after he too suffered a loss in a recent election.

Netanyahu’s bloc fell well short of the 61 seats it needed to stay in power in the October 27 vote, and the Israeli president has since tasked his rival Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government.

Hezbollah, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by two wars it waged against Israel since 2023.

Most recently, the group drew Lebanon into the broader Middle East war in March by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.

Israel continues to occupy swathes of southern Lebanon.

Lebanon and Israel concluded a framework agreement in June under US auspices, providing for the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces and the disarmament of Hezbollah, but its implementation has stalled.

Qassem reiterated on Wednesday that he refused to disarm his group before an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon.

World.title: ‘Your turbaning comes with responsibility’ – ‎Tinubu tells son Seyi
World.content:
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

President Bola Tinubu has congratulated his son, Seyi Tinubu, on his turbaning as Dan Zaki Gwandu by His Royal Highness, Alhaji Muhammadu Iliyasu Bashar, the Emir of Gwandu, in Kebbi State.

‎

‎The President told him that the honour goes with responsibility as the title of Dan Zaki Gwandu carries the values of courage, leadership and service.

‎

‎The traditional title, which translates to Son of the Lion of Gwandu, was conferred on Seyi Tinubu on Wednesday at the historic Abdullahi Fodiyo Palace in Birnin Kebbi.

‎

‎President Tinubu thanked the Emir and the Gwandu Emirate Council for the honour, which the traditional ruler described as the first of its kind in the Emirate’s history.

‎

‎The President noted that the honour carries a responsibility that extends beyond personal recognition and reflects the enduring bonds of friendship, mutual respect and unity among Nigeria’s diverse peoples.

‎

‎He acknowledged Seyi’s efforts in youth engagement, community development and empowerment, particularly through his involvement with the City Boy Movement and other initiatives supporting young Nigerians.

‎

‎“As a father, I am pleased to see my son recognised by a traditional institution with such a distinguished history.

‎

‎“But I also remind him that every honour comes with responsibility. The title of Dan Zaki Gwandu carries the values of courage, leadership and service. I urge him to live up to those values, remain humble and continue to dedicate himself to the well-being of others.

‎

‎“Our traditional institutions remain important custodians of our history, culture and national unity. I thank the Emir of Gwandu and the good people of Kebbi State for extending this honour to my son,” the President says.

‎

‎President Tinubu encouraged Seyi to regard the title as a call to deepen his commitment to youth development, peaceful coexistence and service to Nigeria.

‎

‎He wished him wisdom, humility and strength as he assumes the responsibilities associated with the traditional title.

World.title: 2027: ‘I may leave government if we’re not performing’ — Amaechi
World.content:
Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi.

By Adegboyega Adeleye

The Vice-Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, says he is prepared to resign if an Atiku Abubakar-led government fails to perform, making accountability a central part of the opposition ticket’s pitch to voters ahead of the 2027 election.

Amaechi made the comment in a recent interview with News Central TV, where he discussed the ADC’s plans and the record he would ask Nigerians to assess when deciding whether to support the party. The former Minister of Transportation said Atiku knew his character and predicted that Nigerians would hail the former Vice-President as a hero within the first year of an ADC government, if elected.

“I’m sure the presidential candidate (of the ADC) knows my character that if we’re not performing, I may likely leave government if we’re not performing,” Amaechi said.

Asked whether he meant he would be open to resigning as Vice-President if the Atiku-Amaechi ticket failed to perform, he replied authoritatively: “Yes, I’m not joking. But the way the situation is, and the way I know Atiku, our first year in office, he will be hailed as a hero.”

Amaechi also said Nigerians would regret not voting for Atiku sooner if he emerges President and when asked whether he would fulfil his promises, Amaechi challenged anyone who said he had made and failed to honour a promise to come forward. He also called on voters to assess his record in previous public offices, including as governor, minister and Speaker.

“Atiku will be hailed as a hero. Nigerians will regret not voting for him earlier before before this time,”

“Let any Nigerian who said I made a promise to him and I refuse to fulfil come forward. Any Nigerian, that’s one. Two, let this be a referendum on all of us, not just the current administration. Yes, all of us. Let it be a referendum. Go back and say Amaechi was once a governor. Amaechi was once a minister. Amaechi was once a speaker,” he said.

The former Rivers Governor further urged voters to judge his record against their own standards and withhold their votes if he did not meet them.

“Judge, assess all that I have done in this office. If I don’t meet your criteria, if I don’t meet what can convince you to vote for us, don’t vote for us,” Amaechi said.

World.title: ‘Dictator’ Infantino needs psychiatric help, says former FIFA chief Blatter
World.content:
Infantino (Photo by Nhac NGUYEN / AFP)

Former FIFA boss Sepp Blatter has slammed current chief Gianni Infantino, calling his successor a “dictator” and suggesting he needs psychiatric help, in an interview with Der Spiegel published Wednesday.

Blatter, 90, criticised Infantino’s decision to create the FIFA Peace Prize award for US President Donald Trump in the lead-up to this year’s World Cup, hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico.

He was also critical of Infantino’s post-World Cup plans to sell off part of the commercial rights of the competition in the future, which was scrapped after a fierce backlash.

“FIFA is suffering. It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded,” Blatter told the German magazine.

The Peace Prize, he said, was “embarrassing”.

“Why would he do something like that?,” Blatter asked. “Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards? That’s madness.”

Blatter said it was easy for Infantino to secure support for his own re-election from national football bodies.

“‘If you vote for me,’ he tells the national associations, ‘you will get much more money than before.’

“He is a dictator. People in FIFA tell me that no one is allowed to ride in the elevator with him. He is ‘untouchable’.”

Speaking of Infantino’s World Cup sale plans, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this.

“I mean, maybe Infantino should be sent to a psychiatric ward one day.”

Blatter was also critical of FIFA’s decision to suspend a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun after Trump intervened ahead of a crucial match at this summer’s World Cup.

“The red card. That’s the worst. Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”

– ‘Fulfilling his duties’: FIFA –

When contacted for comment by AFP however, FIFA pointed to its previous response to Der Spiegel, which countered Blatter’s statements.

FIFA rebutted allegations Infantino had acted inappropriately, saying he “is fulfilling his duties as president through his travels,” while adding: “The suspension imposed on Folarin Balogun following a red card was lifted by independent FIFA judicial bodies.”

“Mr. Infantino does indeed use the elevator at FIFA, but does so when other people are present,” FIFA said in the statement.

President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations, including accusations he had sought to buy votes for his presidency.

Charges were brought against him but Blatter was eventually cleared in two trials but was banned from football by FIFA’s ethics committee.

Blatter told the magazine he had “no regrets” from his time in charge of the organisation.

Japanese official Kozo Tashima has announced plans to run against Infantino in his re-election bid, but Blatter named World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as his pick to take over FIFA.

“It is not important who is running. What is important is that the incumbent president is no longer elected.

“Coe was also chairman of the FIFA Ethics Committee. He is a strong personality. A president from the motherland of football, England, would be good.”

Blatter said he had not spoken with Infantino since early 2016.

Vanguard News

World.title: Uganda ruling party rejects plan for son to succeed president
World.content:
The leadership of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni’s party has rejected his plan to designate his son, known for boasting of kidnapping and torturing rivals, as his successor, five party sources told AFP on Wednesday.

The president’s son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, 52, is currently head of the army, and wields huge and growing influence as his 82-year-old father plays a declining role in governing the east African country after four decades in power.

“Muhoozi”, as he is widely known, has vowed to run in the next presidential election scheduled for 2031, but many are unnerved by his flouting of the law, and inflammatory posts on social media, where he frequently boasts of torturing opponents in his “basement”.

In recent months, he has had political rivals imprisoned, threatened to behead opposition leader Bobi Wine, and forced the closure of the country’s leading independent media group for several weeks.

Although Museveni has ruled with an iron grip since 1986, many within his party, the National Resistance Movement (NRM), have voiced concern at the apparent moves to hand power to his son.

In a closed-door meeting of the NRM’s executive committee on Tuesday, convened to determine a successor, a vote on the son’s candidacy had to be abandoned as several of the 28 members spoke against the plan and received loud cheers, according to five people present.

Four people had voted in favour of the son, three had voted against, by the time the vote was called off, the sources told AFP.

“The combative nature of the (army chief) has created uneasiness among some people. He is fighting and threatening people on social media. Let him start convincing people but not using coercive means to capitulate the population,” said one source.

NRM vice-chairman Calvin Echodu told Museveni to retire the son from the army and give him a civilian assignment to get acquainted with the population and prepare himself well for leadership,” said another participant.

Echodu also reportedly advised the president that he should stand again in 2031 “as his son is not yet ready,” the source added.

The attendees say it was an unprecedented show of defiance against the long-ruling president, who first broached the subject of his succession by presenting a paper to the party grandees in late October, in which he suggested his son had the right credentials for the job.

In recent days, Kainerugaba has once again drawn attention with bellicose posts on X, threatening Vice President Jessica Alupo with arrest over claims she was involved in a plot to overthrow the government.

World.title: Lagos targets 2,000MW power boost by March 2027, engages 22 investors
World.content:
Governor Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

​The Lagos State Government has announced plans to add 2,000 megawatts (MW) of electricity to its power supply by March 2027, as part of ongoing regulatory reforms and private-sector partnerships aimed at ending chronic power shortages.

​Speaking at the Lagos Energy Summit 2026, themed:“Lagos Energy Evolution: Transforming the Future,” on Wednesday, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Barrister Abimbola Salu-Hundeyin, said reliable electricity remains critical to sustaining the state’s economic growth.

​”Manufacturers, small businesses, and households have continued to bear the burden of unreliable electricity and high energy costs.

“Our administration has been intentional about creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive through improved power infrastructure, regulatory reforms, and increased private-sector participation,” Sanwo-Olu said.

​He noted that the state’s market restructuring is designed to establish clear frameworks for licensing, consumer protection, and accountability among electricity providers, while urging stakeholders to move beyond policy discussions to practical solutions.

​Providing further details on the state’s roadmap, the Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Biodun Ogunleye, disclosed that Lagos is currently engaging approximately 22 investors to close energy-sector transactions and is working with federal authorities to resolve outstanding Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) bottlenecks.

​Ogunleye added that the state’s strategy extends beyond generation to strengthening transmission and distribution networks, automating energy assets to curb electricity theft and vandalism, and promoting renewable alternatives such as solar, wind, and hydropower.

​Highlighting the scale of the deficit, the Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Ibilola Kasunmu, revealed that Lagos, home to an estimated 22 million people with an electricity demand of about 6,000MW—currently receives less than 1,000MW from the national grid.

​She attributed the shortfall to inadequate generation, gas supply constraints, weak transmission infrastructure, and poor collection systems, noting that “the state is leveraging embedded generation, waste-to-energy projects, and a joint technical working committee with the federal government to bridge the gap.”

World.title: Otu sacks task force over demolition of private property
World.content:
By Emma Una

CALABAR — Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, has dissolved the state’s Planning and Development Control Task Force following the demolition of a private property nearing completion by officials of the agency.

The governor also ordered the immediate suspension of further demolition activities on the affected property and directed the payment of compensation for damages caused by the demolition.

Otu announced the decisions on Wednesday, describing the action of the task force, headed by Akiba Ekpenyong, as a “brazen, unconscionable and reprehensible demolition”.

He characterised the incident as an abuse of power and an assault on the rights of a citizen, saying such conduct was incompatible with the principles guiding his administration.

In a statement signed by his Chief Press Secretary, Linus Obogo, the governor said violations of physical planning regulations could not justify lawlessness or give public institutions the authority to disregard citizens’ rights.

“Violations of physical planning regulations cannot constitute a licence for lawlessness, nor can any public institution arrogate to itself powers that trample upon the rights and dignity of citizens,” the statement quoted him as saying.

The governor consequently ordered the immediate dissolution of the entire task force, holding it responsible for what he described as gross team failure.

He also directed that no further demolition should be carried out on the affected property and that compensation be paid for the damage already done.

Otu reiterated that no individual or public institution was entitled to exercise governmental powers recklessly or outside the limits of established laws and due process.

He warned that his administration would not shield or excuse official misconduct, stressing that public office must not be used as an instrument of intimidation or oppression.

The governor further directed government agencies to operate with discipline, professionalism and respect for citizens’ rights, assuring residents that his administration would uphold justice and accountability.

World.title: Maternal deaths: Women doctors demand action as Nigeria loses 75,000 mothers yearly
World.content:
… Women physicians must move from hospital wards to policy-making tables — Wright

… Says one Nigerian woman dies every seven minutes from pregnancy-related complications

… Calls for urgent reforms in maternal and child healthcare

By Chioma Obinna

Women physicians on Wednesday in Lagos called for urgent reforms in Nigeria’s healthcare system to stem the rising burden of preventable maternal and child deaths, with a warning that the country loses about 75,000 women annually to pregnancy and childbirth-related complications.



The call was made at the 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Scientific Conference of the Medical Women’s Association of Nigeria (MWAN), Lagos State Branch, where the keynote speaker, Professor Kikelomo Ololade Wright, challenged female doctors to move beyond clinical practice and take their rightful place in healthcare policy formulation and strategic decision-making.



Speaking on the theme, “Women Physicians at the Forefront of Health Equity: Advancing Women, Children and Community Health”, Wright said the scale of maternal mortality in Nigeria demanded more decisive action from government, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders.



According to her, United Nations figures showed that approximately 75,000 Nigerian women died from pregnancy and childbirth-related complications in 2023, representing nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths recorded globally.



“That is one woman every seven minutes,” she said, describing the situation as alarming, particularly because many of the deaths were preventable.



Wright, a Professor of Public Health and Community Medicine at the Lagos State University College of Medicine, insisted that women physicians must not limit their contributions to treating patients but should also influence the policies and decisions that determine healthcare delivery.



“Not on the sidelines, not behind, not supporting, but we’re at the front,” she declared, stressing that women doctors must be represented in hospital boards, health committees and other decision-making platforms.



“We deliver most of the care. We must also shape the decisions. It is non-negotiable,” she added.



She said Nigeria’s maternal mortality ratio of estimated 993 deaths per 100,000 live births was about five times the global average and significantly higher than the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 70 deaths per 100,000 live births.



The professor expressed concern that despite the presence of some of the countries best medical facilities in Lagos State, maternal deaths remained unacceptably high, with some communities recording particularly disturbing figures.



According to Wright, the tragedy raised critical questions about the ability of primary healthcare facilities to recognise and manage obstetric emergencies, availability of blood, emergency referral arrangements and access to life-saving treatment.



She said the incident underscored the need for functional referral systems linking primary healthcare centres with secondary and tertiary hospitals.



“Our goal is not just to safely leave you. Our goal is to ensure that everyone who leaves us goes home with her baby or with her babies,” she said.



Wright identified obstetric haemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, sepsis, unsafe abortion-related complications and ruptured uterus among the major causes of preventable maternal deaths.



She also raised concerns about Nigeria’s child health indicators, noting that under-five mortality declined only marginally from 132 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2018 to 110 in 2024.



She described the progress as inadequate, especially against the SDG target of 25 deaths per 1,000 live births.



The professor further disclosed that Nigeria had an estimated 2.2 million zero-dose children in 2025, more than any other country, warning that the figure reflected the failure of the healthcare system to reach millions of vulnerable children with essential immunisation services.



She also highlighted malnutrition, poor access to clean water, household air pollution, adolescent pregnancies and inadequate youth-friendly healthcare services as major challenges affecting vulnerable populations.



According to her, women in low-income settlements, adolescent girls, young mothers, children under five and residents of riverine and peri-urban communities bear a disproportionate burden of healthcare inequalities.



Explaining the difference between equality and equity, Wright said providing the same healthcare resources to everyone did not necessarily guarantee fairness because individuals and communities had different needs and faced different barriers.



“Health is your right. It is not a privilege. It is not a privilege based on your postcode, or based on your purse, or based on your pocket,” she said.



She urged MWAN members to adopt underserved communities, strengthen maternal and child health interventions, support nutrition programmes, promote health insurance and monitor the impact of their interventions.



She also called for improved funding, adequate medical equipment, increased healthcare personnel and better remuneration to address the impact of the migration of Nigerian doctors.



Wright urged female physicians to support younger colleagues through mentorship and professional development, stressing that women must create opportunities for one another rather than compete destructively.



“When women physicians lead, women, children, and communities thrive,” she said.



Earlier, the President of MWAN, Lagos State Branch, Dr Ime Maria Edwin Okon, said the conference provided an opportunity for women physicians to renew their commitment to improving healthcare access and outcomes for women, children and communities.



Okon stressed that women doctors occupied a strategic position in healthcare delivery because they understood the challenges confronting families both as medical professionals and as mothers.



“We are mothers in the land. We understand the health challenges confronting women and children, not only from our professional experiences, but also from our engagement with our families and communities,” she said.



She advocated greater adoption of artificial intelligence, telemedicine, digital health platforms and other technological innovations to improve healthcare delivery, particularly in Lagos, where population growth continues to put pressure on available medical personnel.



The MWAN president also expressed concern over the continued migration of Nigerian doctors, popularly known as the Japa syndrome, urging government to improve hospital infrastructure, equipment and the welfare of medical professionals.



“Support the people that are still here, that have not travelled out, by making sure that infrastructure is very okay,” she said.

She warned that doctors could become frustrated and seek opportunities abroad if their working conditions and welfare needs were not adequately addressed.



Okon also advocated expanded health insurance coverage to reduce out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure, which she identified as a major barrier preventing women, particularly those in rural and underserved communities, from accessing timely medical attention.



On women’s professional advancement, she urged female doctors to embrace technology, continuous learning and leadership opportunities.



“If they don’t give you a seat on the table, bring your seats. You just have to be there to present,” she declared.

World.title: BusinessDay Names ICRC DG Ewalefoh Winner of 2026 Public Service Award
World.content:
The BusinessDay Awards Committee has selected the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh, for its 2026 Public Service Award in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Nigeria’s infrastructure development.

The selection was conveyed in a letter dated November 11, 2026, signed by the Publisher of BusinessDay, Frank Aigbogun, and addressed to Ewalefoh.

According to the letter, the award recognises his “distinguished public service, strategic leadership and contributions to Nigeria’s infrastructure development.”

It added that the selection acknowledges his leadership at the ICRC, particularly in advancing Public-Private Partnership (PPP) frameworks, strengthening infrastructure concession regulation and promoting private-sector participation in public infrastructure development.

“Your selection recognises your leadership and stewardship at the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), particularly in advancing Public-Private Partnership (PPP) frameworks, strengthening infrastructure concession regulation, promoting private-sector participation in public infrastructure development and creating an enabling environment for sustainable investment in critical national infrastructure,” the letter stated.

BusinessDay said the award was established to recognise public-sector leaders whose commitment, professionalism, innovation and leadership contribute to measurable progress in governance, economic development and national transformation.

The ceremony is scheduled for Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at the NAF Conference Centre and Suites, Kado, Abuja.

The letter disclosed that the event would bring together senior government officials, policymakers, business leaders, institutional heads, diplomats, investors and other stakeholders.

It also stated that the occasion would be chaired by former Vice-President of Nigeria, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo.

Explaining the importance of the recognition, BusinessDay noted that infrastructure development remained fundamental to Nigeria’s economic growth, competitiveness and national transformation.

“Bridging the country’s infrastructure deficit requires innovative financing models, effective regulatory frameworks and stronger collaboration between government and the private sector,” it said.

The letter further highlighted the strategic role of the ICRC in facilitating private-sector investment in public infrastructure through PPP arrangements.

It noted that through regulatory oversight, project development support, concession monitoring and the promotion of best practices in infrastructure procurement, the commission helps ensure that projects are transparent, commercially viable and capable of delivering sustainable value to Nigerians.

BusinessDay said Ewalefoh’s leadership carried significant national responsibility in strengthening the PPP ecosystem, unlocking private capital, improving infrastructure delivery and positioning Nigeria as an attractive destination for infrastructure investment.

The recognition is also expected to highlight the commission’s contributions to promoting investor confidence, strengthening collaboration among government institutions and private investors, and addressing Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit.

World.title: Banditry: IGP Gives Commissioners of Police 72 Hours to Furnish Him with Updated Threat Assessments
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has given some Commissioners of Police 72 hours to furnish him with updated threat assessments of their commands and operational requirements at Force Headquarters.

Disu gave the directive during his conference with police strategic managers in Abuja on Wednesday.

The IGP revealed that no fewer than 611 suspected criminals had been arrested by operatives of the Force across the federation in just one month.

Giving a breakdown of the arrests, rescued kidnap victims and recovered arms and ammunition, the IGP said: “Since our last conference, our personnel have arrested 218 banditry and terrorism suspects, 85 suspected armed robbers, 129 suspects for murder and culpable homicide, 59 suspected kidnappers and 120 suspected cultists. We also rescued 95 kidnap victims, recovered 306 assorted firearms and 630 rounds of ammunition of various calibres, along with 116 stolen vehicles. I commend all officers and men whose courage, professionalism and commitment have contributed to these achievements.”

He added,”I must now speak plainly. The statistics I have just read represent progress, but they do not tell the full story. Bandit attacks are ongoing in some states across the Federation, and communities in those areas continue to face real threats to their safety and livelihoods. This is a challenge we are confronting directly, and I will not allow this conference to pretend otherwise.

“I am therefore directing as follows, with immediate effect: All Commissioners of Police in affected commands are to submit updated threat assessments and operational requirements to Force Headquarters within 72 hours.

“I want specifics, not generalities. The DIG in charge of Operations is to coordinate the immediate deployment of additional personnel, mobility and air support to the most affected areas, in consultation with the commands concerned. Intelligence-led operations must be sustained and intensified. Every command must have a standing operational plan for its high-risk zones.

“Community intelligence must be deepened. Traditional rulers, village heads, hunters’ associations and local vigilante groups in affected areas must be engaged and incorporated into our intelligence architecture. The people know who the bandits are. We must give them the confidence to tell us.”

He emphasised that the Nigeria Police Force remains a strictly non-partisan institution, adding: “Our allegiance is to the Constitution and the Nigerian people.”

He said every candidate, political party, supporter and eligible voter is entitled to equal protection under the law.

Disu said he would not tolerate any officer using the authority of the Police to advance the interests of any political party, candidate or sponsor.

“Any officer found to be colluding with political actors, facilitating thuggery, compromising the integrity of the electoral process or interfering with the rights of voters will be disciplined according to the law,” he said.

World.title: PFN President Seeks Inclusion of Private Varsities As Beneficiaries of TETFUND, NELFUND
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The National President, Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria (PFN), Archbishop Francis Wale Oke, on Wednesday, called on the Federal Government to include private universities as beneficiaries of Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFUND) and their students in Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND).

This is just as he said the Precious Cornerstone University (PCU), Ibadan, is committed to producing skilful, moral graduates that are critical thinkers that will be solutions to societal problems.

Archbishop Oke, who is the Chancellor of PCU, while speaking with journalists at the fifth convocation ceremony of the university, lamented that the exclusion of private universities as well as their students from the two agencies of the Federal Government amounts to depriving the students their rights as citizens of Nigeria and the institutions of what they should also enjoy.

According to the President of the Sword of the Spirit Ministries, the Federal Government has no reason to exclude private universities and their students from the interventions as they also contribute their quota to the growth of the country, stating that private institutions needed the intervention to develop their infrastructures while the students are also bonafide citizens of Nigeria.

He said: “The TETFUND should not be meant for public institutions alone but for private universities also. Excluding them from the fund is a discrimination, it is bad, as the private universities are equally training the future leaders of our country. The time to include the private universities in TETFUND should be now as the fund is generated mostly from taxes paid by the private sector such as banks and oil companies.”

Archbishop Oke, who maintained that PCU is producing graduates that will be professionally sound and self-independent and be employers of labour and not a burden to the labour market, disclosed that the National Universities Commission (NUC) has granted approval for the institution to commence admissions into seven additional undergraduate programmes.

“These new programmes are Nursing Science, Public Health, Medical Laboratory Science and Community Health Science under the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences and Christian Religious Studies, Music and Performing Arts under the Faculty of Arts,” he said.

He described the approvals as a major milestone in PCU’s academic expansion and contributions to national manpower development, noting that the institution will continue to foster a culture of innovation, encouraging students to become job creators through research-driven learning and entrepreneurial development.

Archbishop Oke explained that PCU insists on getting the best lecturers to teach the students and hence does not play with academic excellence, stating that the institution encourages students to register a company where they are going to practise their own businesses while they are still in the university and likewise register them for professional courses to enable them to become gurus in their chosen career.

He added that a total of 148 students graduated in the epoch set of 2026 comprising 25 first class, 69 second class upper, 44 second class lower and 10 third class, bringing the university’s cumulative graduate population to 604.

According to him, “Here in PCU we produce skilful, talented, professional graduates that will be employers of labour and job creators and not people that will just carry a certificate looking for a job. Students from all over the country are thus welcome into the institution.”

World.title: Tinubu Rescued Nigeria from Economic Collapse, Restored Stability with Bold Reforms, Says Fasuyi
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

The Chairman of the Senate Committee on the South West Development Commission (SWDC), Senator Cyril Fasuyi, has said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu rescued Nigeria from the brink of economic collapse through bold and far-reaching reforms that have restored macroeconomic stability and repositioned the country for sustainable growth.

Fasuyi made the assertion while receiving the National President of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Professionals’ Forum, Dr. Isa Yuguda, and members of the forum during a stakeholders’ engagement in Ekiti State, where he defended the economic policies of the Tinubu administration.

According to him, the administration inherited an economy burdened by crippling fuel subsidy payments, multiple foreign exchange windows, dwindling public revenues, rising debt obligations and declining investor confidence, warning that the nation was heading towards a dangerous economic precipice.

He said President Tinubu took politically difficult but economically necessary decisions by removing the fuel subsidy, unifying the foreign exchange market and introducing structural reforms aimed at restoring fiscal discipline, rebuilding investor confidence and laying the foundation for long-term national prosperity.

Fasuyi acknowledged that the reforms came with temporary hardships for many Nigerians but insisted that they had prevented a far worse economic crisis.

“Without those courageous decisions, Nigeria would have faced a much deeper economic disaster. President Tinubu chose to save the country instead of postponing difficult choices. Today, the economy is becoming more stable, government revenues have improved and investors are gradually regaining confidence in Nigeria,” he said.

He added that increased revenue accruing to the federal, state and local governments had strengthened the capacity of governments to execute critical infrastructure projects, improve public services and stimulate economic activities across the country.

The senator urged Nigerians to exercise patience with the administration, expressing confidence that the gains of the reforms would become more evident as implementation deepens and economic activities continue to rebound.

He maintained that history would remember Tinubu as a leader who took bold decisions at a critical moment to prevent economic collapse and place Nigeria on the path of recovery and sustainable development.

Also speaking, the National President of the APC Professionals’ Forum, Dr. Yuguda, commended the Tinubu administration for pursuing reforms aimed at rebuilding the economy despite the political risks involved, urging Nigerians to support policies designed to secure the country’s long-term economic future.

He said the Renewed Hope Agenda remained focused on creating a stronger, more competitive and resilient economy capable of delivering inclusive growth and improved living standards for all Nigerians.

World.title: At Akure’s APC-PCC Rally, Shettima Says Tinubu’s Focused, Supercharging State Coffers, Fast-tracking Growth
World.content:
* Reveals Ondo’s federation account receipts rose by over 22% in first 9 months of 2026

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has stressed that President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms are bolstering the fiscal strength of state governments, accelerating critical infrastructure and expanding economic opportunities across Nigeria.

According to him, the economic policies of the Tinubu government have supercharged state-level revenues, unlocking vital investments in roads, agriculture, power, education and healthcare, with Ondo State recording a significant increase in revenue from the federation account.

Speaking on Wednesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, Shettima recalled that Ondo received over 22 per cent more from the Federation Account in the first nine months of 2026 than in the same period in 2025.

Representing the president at the campaign rally, the vice-president told the mammoth crowd that gathered at the Akure Township Stadium that the gains recorded so far demonstrate the importance of sustained reforms and cooperation between the Federal Government and subnational governments.

“Our promise to prioritise the welfare of Ondo State has been demonstrated through the increased revenue accruing to Ondo State. This has come with President Tinubu’s reforms. Even in the first nine months of this year, Ondo received over 22 per cent more from the Federation Account than it did in the same period last year,” he stated.

Shettima lauded Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa for deploying the additional resources towards development projects, noting that the administration’s interventions are addressing longstanding infrastructure and economic challenges.

On agriculture and rural development, he disclosed that the Federal Government, working with the state government and development partners, had constructed, rehabilitated and maintained more than 386 kilometres of rural roads to improve access to farms and markets.

“We are aware that a cocoa farmer in Idanre knows how much of his earnings a bad road can swallow. We have worked with your governor and our partners to build, repair and maintain more than 386 kilometres of rural roads,” he declared.

The vice-president also highlighted the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, which he said had reached Ajegeri in Ilaje, the revalidation of the Port Ondo licence and the completion of 48 kilometres of concrete pavement on the Sagamu–Ore Road.

In the power sector, Shettima announced the completion and inauguration of the Ode-Erinje transmission line and substation, while noting that pipes had begun arriving for the Owena water supply project in Akure.

He further listed the operationalisation of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) Teaching Hospital, five TETFund projects at Rufus Giwa Polytechnic, Owo, and healthcare support through 203 public facilities under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund.

The vice-president said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), student hostel projects, MSME financing and grants are expanding opportunities for students, traders, artisans and small businesses across the state.

On security, Shettima reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to strengthening security institutions and improving personnel welfare, citing the legislation providing statutory backing for the Police Training School in Oyin-Akoko.

“We inherited a compromised security system, no doubt, and Ondo State paid a regrettable price. But we overcame all the attacks on us because we stood together and declared that never shall we let the enemies of the state triumph,” he said.

The vice-president thanked the people of Ondo State for their continued support, assuring them that President Tinubu’s administration remained determined to consolidate its reforms and complete ongoing development projects.

“Our economy is stable now. We have put the naysayers to shame. And the cause is not magic; it is your choice, your vote, your trust, your patience, your faith, and the leadership of President Bola Tinubu” he declared.

“We will never take you for granted as we march together to the polls again to renew the mandate of our leader, His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and finish what we have begun,” Shettima further said.

Earlier, Ondo State Governor Aiyedatiwa vowed that the people of Ondo State would turn out en masse to vote for President Tinubu because the state is a progressive state, just as the president is a progressive, even as he applauded the ongoing reforms the Tinubu administration has embarked on to revamp the nation’s economy.

Recalling that the people of Ondo State voted massively for the president in 2023, the governor said: “We voted for you because we believe in you, because we know what you can do, and because we know your track record as a former governor of Lagos State. Mr. President, you have not disappointed us at all. You have also done well here in Ondo State by giving us three ministers.”

Aiyedatiwa acknowledged that the reforms undertaken by President Tinubu have been effective and have brought prosperity to the nation, even as he promised that the people of Ondo “will all go to the mountains, to the hills, and everywhere to tell the people about,” the president’s re-election.

Also speaking, National Chairman of the APC, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, waxed rhetorical, saying of the 18 presidential candidates lined up for the 2027 presidential poll, President Tinubu remains the most experienced, exposed, and prepared among them, as well as the only person who can take Nigeria to the next level.

“We are here because 18 candidates have been presented as presidential candidates by 18 political parties ahead of the January 16 presidential election. The question is: Among those 18 candidates, who has the wisdom of experience, wisdom of exposure, wisdom of preparation and wisdom of purpose? Who is the person that can take us to the next level? That is why today I am here to present a candidate who is fearless; a candidate who does not run from any problem.”

Describing the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as the most competent, Yilwatda also characterised President Tinubu as the most prepared candidate, possessing all the leadership qualities Nigeria needs at this defining moment.

Also, Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF) and Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, urged the people of Ondo State to go to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and collect all their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) still piled up at the commission’s office in order to vote massively for the president in the January 16, 2027 presidential poll.

“Going by the last count, we have 2.4 million registered voters in Ondo State. Out of 2.4 million voters, only 1.4 million have collected their PVCs. The question is, without your PVCs, how would you support President Bola Tinubu?

“I, therefore, want to urge you to go to the INEC office and collect all your PVCs that are lying there so that on January 16, 2027, you will be eligible to vote. I have seen the enthusiasm of all the leaders in those states in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu—an incredible goodwill I have seen,” he stated, calling for unity among party leaders.

For his part, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, highlighted President Tinubu’s development strides in Ondo State and wished the president had brought similar infrastructure projects to his home state of Zamfara.

“My state will grow and become like Ondo State. People of Ondo, on the 16th of January, you need to come out—youths, women, and the elderly—to ensure that Asiwaju wins. We are not looking for Asiwaju to win by a small margin. We are looking for Asiwaju to get millions of votes that will secure the presidency,” the DG urged the people.

Yari appreciated the leaders for all the mobilisation seen from entering Akure to the venue of the campaign rally, urging them to work together to ensure maximum votes for President Tinubu.

World.title: Southwest Monarchs Back Tinubu’s Re-election Bid
World.content:
*Support state police, fuel subsidy removal

Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

Traditional rulers from the South West region yesterday threw their weight behind the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027.

This formed part of tbe resolutions of their neeting held at the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rasidi Ladoja, in Oke-Aremo, Ibadan.

The meeting had in attendance the host, Oba Ladoja; Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi; Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Afolabi Ghandi Olaoye; Olu of Ilaro, Oba Kehinde Gbadewole Olugbenla; Deji of Akure, Oba Aladetoyinbo Ogunlade Aladewusi; Aseyin of Iseyin, Oba Sefiu Adeyeri; Ebumawe of Ago Iwoye, Oba Abdulrasaq Adenugba; Ewi of Ado Ekiti, Oba Rufus Aladesanmi and Owa Obokun of Ijesaland, Oba Adesuyi Hastrup.

Others are Elegushi of Ikate-Elegushi Kingdom, Oba Saheed Ademola; Oniba of Ibaland, Oba Sulaimon Raji-Asade; Ogoga of Ikere-Ekiti, Oba Samuel Adejimi Adu- Alagbado; Balogun of Ibadanland, Oba Tajudeen Ajibola; and Orangun of Oke-Ila, Oba Adedokun Abolarin.

Also present include the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo; Akarigbo of Remoland, Oba Babatunde Ajayi; Alara of Ilara Epe, Oba Olufolarin Ogunsanwo; Osolu of Irewe, Oba Abideen Durosinmi; Olofin of Isheri, Oba Sulaimon Adekunle Bamgbade; Oniru of Iru Kingdom, Oba Abdulwasiu Omogbolahan and Ajero of Ijero-Ekiti, Oba Adebayo Adewole.

Oba Gbadebo while reading the 10-paragraph communique issued at the end of the closed door meeting, on behalf of the monarchs, said they acknowledged the efforts of the Federal Government in addressing national challenge and advancing the development agenda of the country.

The communique read in part, “Traditional rulers of the Southwest met to deliberate on matters of regional and national importance. After extensive discussions, the council resolved as follows:

“Reaffirmation of support for the President: The council unanimously reaffirmed its unwavering support for His Excellency, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and his administration. The traditional rulers acknowledged the efforts of the Federal Government in addressing national challenges and advancing the development agenda of the country.

“Mobilization of citizens in support of government programs: The council urged all Southwest kings and traditional rulers to continue sensitizing and mobilizing citizens within their respective domains to support government programs and policies that are designed to promote economic growth, national stability, and social development.

“Support for the state police initiative: The council expressed support for the proposed establishment of state police as a strategic measure to strengthen internal security. Traditional rulers were encouraged to prepare and sensitize youths across the region to take advantage of future employment and service opportunities that may arise from the initiative.

“Position on fuel subsidy: The council noted the economic realities confronting the nation and expressed support for the Federal Government’s current position on fuel subsidy. The meeting resolved that the reintroduction of fuel subsidy would not serve the long-term interest of national economic development and fiscal sustainability.

“Protection and advancement of Southwest interests: The council discussed the need for continued vigilance and strategic engagement in national affairs to ensure that the political, economic, and developmental interests of the Southwest region remain adequately represented and protected within the Nigerian Federation.

“Promotion of national unity and cohesion: Recognizing the importance of national integration, the council called for stronger collaboration and mutual understanding among all regions of the country. The traditional rulers pledged to foster constructive engagement with their counterparts in Northern Nigeria and other parts of the federation in the interest of peace, unity, and national development.

“The council observed that the principle of rotational presidency has over the years contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness, and national cohesion across Nigeria. In the interest of fairness, equity, and the continued strengthening of national unity, the council expressed the view that the rotational arrangement should be sustained and the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria in the next electoral cycle, in line with the spirit of power rotation that has helped preserve peace and stability in the country.

“The council emphasized that the position is intended to promote national balance, mutual trust among federating units, and the continued progress of the Nigerian state.

“Commitment to peaceful elections: The council underscored the importance of peaceful, free, and credible elections at all levels. It condemned all forms of electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying, and other electoral malpractices, urging political actors and citizens alike to uphold democratic values before, during, and after elections.”

While appreciating the President for the establishment of new military formations in Ekiti and Oyo States, the traditional rulers noted that the development would significantly enhance security architecture within the Southwest and contribute to the protection of lives and property.

On infrastructure development, the monarchs commended President Tinubu and the Federal Government for ongoing infrastructure projects and developmental initiatives across the Southwest and other parts of the country, stating that the positive impact of these projects on economic activities, connectivity, and overall national development cannot be overemphasized.

The traditional rulers then reaffirmed their commitment to promoting peace, good governance, national unity, and sustainable development, calling on all citizens to remain law-abiding, support legitimate government initiatives, and work collectively towards a more prosperous and secure Nigeria.

World.title: Nigerian SMEs Face Digital Management Gap Despite Widespread Adoption of Electronic Payments, Visa Report Shows
World.content:
Despite the widespread adoption of digital payments among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria, many businesses still struggle to integrate their financial and operational activities, relying on disconnected systems to manage their daily operations, a new Visa report has revealed.

The Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, based on a survey of 251 Nigerian SMEs, found that only 29 per cent of businesses surveyed use integrated platforms that combine payment services with other business management functions.

The findings highlight a digital management gap among Nigerian businesses, with 94 per cent of respondents expressing interest in an all-in-one platform that would enable them to manage payments and day-to-day business operations in one place.

According to the report, the fragmented approach to business management has contributed to administrative difficulties, particularly in tracking outstanding invoices, organising payroll records and preparing financial reports.

It found that 14 per cent of SMEs struggle with tracking outstanding invoices, 19 per cent face challenges organising payroll records, while 16 per cent have difficulties preparing financial reports.

The report also identified some of the reasons businesses have yet to adopt integrated platforms, including satisfaction with existing manual processes (eight per cent), concerns that new systems could disrupt their operations (eight per cent) and a lack of trust in relying on a single provider (seven per cent).

However, SMEs already using integrated solutions appear to be recording improvements in their operations. The report found that 93 per cent of Nigerian SMEs using such platforms were satisfied with their experience, while 88 per cent reported improved operational efficiency, including reduced time and effort spent managing their businesses.

Commenting on the findings, Vice President and Cluster Head, Visa West Africa, Andrew Uaboi, said the next phase of digital adoption among SMEs would depend on connecting payment systems with the tools businesses use to manage their daily operations.

“Digital payments are now a core part of how many SMEs in Nigeria operate. The next opportunity lies in helping businesses get more value from those transactions by connecting payments with the tools they use to manage their day-to-day operations,” he said.

Uaboi added that integrating payment and business management systems could provide financial institutions with better insights into cash flow patterns, improve decision-making and create opportunities to offer more relevant products and services, including financing.

Similarly, Group Head, SME Banking at Access Bank, Abiodun Olubitan, said the focus for Nigerian SMEs should shift from merely adopting digital payments to using technology to improve business management and support growth.

“We remain committed to supporting businesses with relevant financial solutions and digital capabilities that help them navigate challenges, scale sustainably and contribute more meaningfully to Nigeria’s economic development,” she said.

The study was conducted through face-to-face interviews with business owners and financial decision-makers between March and April 2026 across 11 markets.

World.title: Breaking: Tinubu Rewards U-17 Female World Cup Champions, Flamingos, With N100m For Each Player
World.content:
.Head coach gets N100m cash award, other technical crew members get N50m each

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday rewarded the U-17 Female World Cup Champions, the Flamingos, with a savings certificate worth N100 million for each player.

Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, announced the reward while receiving the world champions at the State House in Abuja on behalf of the President.

According to her, each player will receive a savings certificate worth 100 million naira each with GTBank, while the head coach got 100 million naira cash reward

Other members of the team’s technical crew, she explained, will receive 50 million naira each.

Nigeria made history by defeating Japan 2-1 in last Saturday’s final in Morocco, becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

Among those at the presidential reception held at the Banquet hall were the wife of the Vice President, Nana Shettima; Ministers of Women Affairs, Industry, Trade and Investment; State for Education; Comptroller-General of Customs; Director-General and chairman of the National Sports Commission, among other top government officials.

World.title: Gonubie Beach closed as sharks feed on whale carcass
World.content:
A beach near KuGompo City (formerly East London) has been temporarily closed following reported sightings of sharks.

Per a public safety notice issued by the Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality, Gonubie Beach has been closed to the public after sharks were observed feeding off a whale carcass floating offshore near Black Rock.

“For the safety of beachgoers and the public,” the safety notice reads, “swimming and other water activities are prohibited until further notice.”



As such, members of the public are strongly urged to keep out of the water. They are also asked to adhere to all safety instructions issued by lifeguards and local authorities.

No reopening date has been announced as of the time of publishing. However, the municipality stressed that the beach will remain closed until it’s deemed safe to do so.

PRESENCE OF SHARKS

The closure of Gonubie Beach comes nearly a month after a 65-year-old woman was tragically killed in a shark attack at Orient Beach in KuGompo City.



Janine Lochrenberg, a retired nuclear radiographer and musician, had been swimming in open water alongside others when a shark fatally attacked her.

Nearly two weeks after Lochrenberg’s death, a shark was sighted at Nahoon Beach in KuGompo City, prompting a temporary closure of the beach.

TAKE PRECAUTIONS

While shark attacks are rare, taking a few simple precautions can reduce the risk further. Coast KZN recommends that you follow these safety tips:



Swim in a group, as attacks are often directed towards individuals.

Swim at beaches with lifeguards and stay within the safe swimming areas.

Avoid swimming at night, dawn or dusk, as sharks are most active during these times.

Sharks can smell and taste blood, so avoid swimming if you are bleeding.

Refrain from swimming at sewage-contaminated beaches, as sewage attracts baitfish, which in turn attracts sharks.

Obey warnings/requests to leave the water by lifeguards and shark spotters if sharks are seen.

Stay safe out there, folks!

World.title: Oswin Appollis continue to struggle at Pirates this season
World.content:
Orlando Pirates winger Oswin Appollis has struggled to replicate last season’s form.

The 25-year-old has managed just two goals and three assists this campaign, a poor return for a player of his calibre.

In his first year with the Buccaneers, Appollis was consistent throughout the season, netting 10 goals across all competitions and also adding eight assists.



In recent matches, Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou decided to start him from the bench. The Moroccan has defended his decision to bench the star, saying it was not the lack of form but player management.

“Appollis is one of our best players. Appollis is one of the best players in South Africa. He is full of quality, but Appollis we don’t have to forget is a human, he is not a robot,” Ouaddou said.

“So Appollis played a fantastic season for his first season in Pirates. He comes from Polokwane, where you know a lot of things have changed for him, and he managed to handle all these things. He did a wonderful, a fantastic season.

“Straight away, he went to the World Cup, and it’s not only him, many players in Europe, many players in other clubs. He played the games. He gave everything for his country. So it’s a guy who is not cheating. So we can understand one moment that sometimes a player can maybe have this fatigue.

Appollis yet to have a solid match for Pirates this season

With Relebohile Mofokeng gone, Appollis has struggled this season. In terms of goals, he has taken more shots at goal than any Pirates player but often failed to find the target.

At Bafana, he also failed to recapture his form, which helped the team in the 2025 AFCON.



Will Appollis find his form?

World.title: Zimbabwe targets South African tourists in fresh Victoria Falls tourism drive
World.content:
South African travel agents participated in a Familiarisation (FAM) Tour of Victoria Falls. Image: ZTA

Zimbabwe is stepping up efforts to attract more holidaymakers from neighbouring South Africa through a tourism marketing initiative targeting travel agents who sell international holiday packages.

The Zimbabwe Tourism Authority (ZTA) said South African travel agents recently participated in a familiarisation (FAM) tour of Victoria Falls, organised in partnership with South African Airways (SAA) and local tourism industry players.

The programme gave the agents first-hand exposure to the resort town’s tourism products and experiences, which they can use to package and recommend Zimbabwe to prospective travellers.



Zimbabwe strengthens tourism ties with South Africa

According to the ZTA, the initiative aims to strengthen business relationships between South African travel agents and Zimbabwean tourism operators.

The authority said the programme would help agents better understand the country’s tourism offerings and promote them to customers in the South African market.

The initiative also seeks to turn greater destination awareness into increased bookings, tourist expenditure and economic returns for Zimbabwe’s tourism industry.

South Africa is an important source market for Zimbabwe’s tourism sector.

In March 2025, The Herald reported that Zimbabwe had hosted another group of South African travel agents on a three-day familiarisation tour of Victoria Falls.

The earlier programme included visits to hotels, a guided tour of Victoria Falls, a Zambezi River sunset cruise, game drives and helicopter excursions.



South Africa remains an important tourism market

Zimbabwe’s tourism industry continues to attract international visitors, with South Africa playing a significant role in regional travel.

According to figures from the Zimbabwe Tourism Authority cited by the United States International Trade Administration, the country recorded 1,613,901 international tourist arrivals in 2024, compared with 1,602,781 in 2023.

This represented a one percent increase in international arrivals.

The tourism sector generated an estimated US$1.2 billion (approximately R19.86 billion) in revenue during 2024, highlighting its contribution to the country’s economy.

Meanwhile, SAA’s route information lists Victoria Falls connections with Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban, giving South African holidaymakers several air travel options.

The airline’s involvement in the latest familiarisation programme could help strengthen links between travel agents and Zimbabwean tourism suppliers.

Victoria Falls remains one of Zimbabwe’s major attractions, alongside Hwange National Park, Lake Kariba, Matobo National Park and the Great Zimbabwe Monuments.

By targeting travel professionals who influence holiday bookings, Zimbabwe hopes to increase its visibility among South African travellers and generate more business for local tourism operators.
