World.title: Government Calls for Concerted Efforts to Curb Illegal Mining
World.content:
Muchinga Province Deputy Permanent Secretary Grants Chisapa says the formalisation of gold mining activities in the province will bring significant benefits to both Muchinga and the country at large.

Mr Chisapa said the government is committed to formalising all gold mining activities in the province and to ensure the process is undertaken without delay.

He, however, indicated the need for all miners to first vacate the mining sites before the formalisation process could commence.

Mr Chisapa said this during a stakeholders’ engagement on mineral regulation, compliance and formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining held at Northern Rock Hotels in Mpika today.

He said formalisation would help bring sanity to the mining sector by ensuring that all mining companies operating in the province were properly identified and regulated.

Mr Chisapa said this would also make it easier for authorities to hold mining companies accountable whenever they violated mining regulations.

He expressed concern that unregulated mining activities had contributed to water pollution and exposed miners to unsafe working conditions.

Mr Chisapa further noted that illegal mining activities had provided a haven for prohibited immigrants and facilitated other illegal activities.

He called for concerted efforts among stakeholders to curb illegal gold mining in Muchinga Province.

Meanwhile, Minerals Regulation Commission Minerals Security and Protection Manager Malfred Moola said illegal mining deprived the Government of much-needed revenue that could otherwise contribute to national development.

Mr Moola said illegal gold mining needed to be stopped without delay to ensure that the benefits from the country’s mineral resources reached all citizens.

He emphasised that the government would not discriminate against anyone during the removal of illegal miners from mining sites.

Meanwhile, Chief Chikwanda of the Bemba speaking people in Mpika expressed concern over the conduct of some mining companies operating in the area.

The traditional leader said some companies had been granted licenses to undertake mineral exploration but had instead engaged in actual gold mining in violation of the law.

Chief Chikwanda called on the government to urgently intervene and stop the companies from engaging in illegal mining activities.

“What these people are doing is a serious violation of the law,” he said.

The engagement was held under the theme of mineral regulation, compliance and formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining.

Gold deposits have been discovered in several districts of Muchinga Province, presenting economic opportunities for local communities while also raising concerns that require urgent regulatory intervention.

World.title: Government Reiterates Commitment to Youth Skills Development
World.content:
Government has reaffirmed its commitment to empowering young people through enhanced skills development programmes funded under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

Acting Chinsali District Commissioner Brenda Silwembe, says the government remains determined to expand access to skills training through the CDF Skills Development Bursary Component and Technical Education, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Training (TEVET) programmes.

Speaking during the 2nd graduation ceremony of the Chinsali Youth Resource Centre held in Chinsali today, Ms Silwembe stated that the event is a testimony of the government’s resolve to decentralise skills development opportunities and ensure that youths from all parts of the country acquire practical skills for sustainable livelihoods.

Ms Silwembe noted that the initiative is in line with the Grow Zambia Agenda which seeks to strengthen the country’s economic growth through skills development, entrepreneurship and productivity.

“As you leave this institution equipped with practical competencies in trades such as carpentry, tailoring, bricklaying and other disciplines, I challenge you to embrace a fundamental mindset shift and utilise the skills acquired here to improve your livelihoods and contribute to national development,” she said.

And Muchinga Provincial Youth Coordinator Malikana Akatama, disclosed that a total of 232 youths among them 14 in-mates, had successfully completed training in various fields under Government-supported youth empowerment programmes.

Ms Akatama said the beneficiaries were drawn from different parts of Chinsali District and were selected on merit to benefit from the CDF-sponsored skills training programme.

She charged that the government will continue supporting young people, particularly vulnerable but ambitious youths to access vocational and tertiary education opportunities.

“I also wish to encourage our graduating youths to take advantage of the many empowerment programmes that the Government has continued to provide in order to improve their lives and become productive citizens,” she said.

Meanwhile, Chinsali Youth Resource Centre Manager Benson Mambunji, commended the government for providing scholarships to all the graduates through the CDF Skills Development Bursary Component.

Mr Mambunji explained that the support had significantly improved access to skills training among youths in the district, enabling many of them to acquire competencies that will help them become self-reliant.

He also appealed for increased stakeholder support towards expanding the institution’s training capacity in order to accommodate more youths.

“I urge our graduates to value this opportunity and utilise the skills acquired to create meaningful change in their communities through entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation,” he added.

And one of the graduates in tailoring, Emma Siatwinda, praised the government for introducing the CDF Skills Development Bursary Component, describing it as a life-changing initiative for many vulnerable youths.

Ms Siatwinda said the programme enabled her to complete her studies without financial challenges and acquire skills that will help her pursue a sustainable livelihood.

“If it was not for CDF, I do not think I would have managed to complete my studies because the Government provided everything I needed to reach this stage,” she stated.

She further urged her fellow graduates to utilise their newly acquired skills through entrepreneurship and innovation to improve their living standards and contribute to national development.

The 2026 graduation ceremony was held under the theme: “Equipped with Skills, Empowered for the Future.”

World.title: OPINION: This is Chipolopolo’s true test without Daka
World.content:
There is a temptation to panic when Germany based striker Patson Daka is ruled out ahead of crucial matches.

He is Zambia’s biggest name, captain in spirit if not always in armband. Losing him, plus Lameck Banda and Gamphani Lungu, for both legs against Burundi feels like a cruel twist just when Chipolopolo needs momentum.

If Zambia cannot beat Burundi without Daka, then it does not deserve to be at AFCON PAMOJA 2027.

Burundi are bottom of Group I with one point. They are not Algeria. They are not a team Zambia should fear. They are a team Zambia should beat – home and away – to show seriousness about returning to Africa’s biggest stage.

This double-header is not about who is missing. It is about who steps up.

This is Edward Chilufya’s chance to remind fans why he was once the next big thing. This is Derrick Bulaya and Prince Mumba’s chance to prove the local league and the less glamorous leagues abroad still produce Chipolopolo quality. This is Kennedy Musonda’s moment – the in-form Zesco striker who has been scoring while others have been on treatment tables.

Interim coach George ‘Chicken’ Lwandamina did not ask for this injury crisis, but he now has a perfect excuse to do what Zambia has needed for years: build a team, not a collection of stars.

For too long, Zambia have played like Chipolopolo is Daka plus ten others. When he is fit, Zambia looks to him. When he is not, the squad some times looks lost.

Friday at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium must be different.

Zambia must press high, move the ball quickly, and trust the system. Burundi will come to Ndola to frustrate, to waste time, to snatch a draw. The National Team cannot allow them to dictate the tempo. Zambia must score early, kill the game, and go to Bujumbura with confidence, not anxiety.

The maths is simple. Algeria lead on four points. Zambia are on three, level with Togo. Six points from Burundi puts Lwandamina’s side on nine and in command. Anything less – a draw in Ndola, a loss in Bujumbura – and Chipolopolo hand the initiative to Togo and Algeria.

Lwandamina is coaching for his future too. An interim tag is a heavy shirt to wear. Win both games, and he forces FAZ to take him seriously. Drop points, and the whispers will start again about needing a foreign coach.

World.title: Three Kalomo Clubs Set to Benefit Over K1 Million Under TRALARD II Project
World.content:
Three clubs in Kalomo district are set to benefit from climate-resilient livelihood interventions valued at over 1 million kwacha under the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development Phase II (TRALARD II) Project.

The interventions seek to strengthen community resilience, improve household livelihoods and promote sustainable management of natural resources ahead of the anticipated Super El Niño conditions.

Project manager James Siakakaba says the interventions are designed to support vulnerable communities with affordable and practical livelihood opportunities that can help them cope with possible drought conditions.

Mr Siakakaba says the project also aims to address challenges associated with water scarcity, reduced agricultural production and the impact of climate variability on household incomes.

The beneficiary groups are Kamudoti Women’s Club, Tubeleke Women’s Club and Kalonda Agro-forestry and Beekeeping Association in Siachitema chiefdom.

Kamudoti Women’s Club will benefit a water reticulation system and horticultural production, small livestock support and the establishment of a tree nursery.

While Tubeleke Women’s Club has been earmarked for horticultural development, goat rearing, establishment of a tree nursery and a solar-powered borehole.

The proposed support is aimed at strengthening the group’s livelihood activities while providing a more reliable water source to support production and improve its ability to withstand climate-related shocks.

And Kalonda Agro-forestry and Beekeeping Association is expected to receive support towards horticulture, water reticulation, beekeeping and tree nursery establishment as part of its agroforestry activities.

The interventions are intended to promote sustainable land-use practices, conserve biodiversity, diversify income sources and improve the economic well-being of its members.

“The selected activities have been considered because they can be rolled out within the current year as they have the potential to deliver immediate and practical benefits to the targeted communities and be rolled out in the coming years,” Mr Sikakaba said.

These interventions are expected to contribute to increased household incomes, improved food and livelihood security, better environmental management and enhanced capacity among communities in the district to respond to climate-related risks and other livelihood challenges

TRALARD II is a five-year World Bank funded programme running from January 2026 to December 2030 in ten districts of Southern Province.

The project is being implemented by line government departments from the Council, Forestry, Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock, Water Resources, Cooperatives and Community Development.

World.title: Government urges church to support Grow Zambia Agenda
World.content:
Southern Province Minister Edgar Sin’gombe has called on the church to use its influence and grassroots presence to mobilise Zambians towards achieving the targets of the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Mr Sin’gombe says the church is a powerful partner in national development, capable of driving public participation and changing mindsets at community level.

The Minister was speaking in Choma when Seventh-day Adventist Church Mosi-Oa-Tunya Conference President, Pastor Maxwell Muvwimi called on him.

Mr Sing’ombe said if the church embraces the Grow Zambia Agenda, it will be easier for ordinary Zambians to understand, accept and participate in the programme.

“We want the church to embrace the Grow Zambia Agenda so that Christians can adapt quickly. When the church speaks, the people listen,” said Mr Sing’ombe.

He explained that government alone cannot drive development, adding that the church has the moral authority to mobilise citizens and encourage hard work, unity and patriotism, and further pledged to be a pressure point of development from President Hakainde Hichilema to the defenceless, orphan’s, widows and widowers.

Meanwhile, Mosi Oa Tunya conference President Maxwell Muvwimi, who led the delegation of other pastors has commended President Hakainde Hichilema for introducing free education, while calling on elected leaders to uphold integrity and fight corruption.

“We thank President Hakainde Hichilema for free education, today, a vulnerable child can go to school without paying.” said Pastor Muvwimi.

Pastor Muvwimi said many families who previously could not afford to send their children to school are now hopeful, describing free education as a true reflection of a government that cares for the poor.

The church leader further urged all elected leaders to put God at the centre of the Grow Zambia Agenda, saying national development without God will not be sustainable.

Pastor Muvwimi said leaders should lead with integrity, prayer and service to the people, and not use their positions for personal gain.

The meeting ended with a commitment by both the government and the church to continue working together for the development of Southern Province.

World.title: FAZ attributes indiscipline as the reason for young players’ failures
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) has attributed the failure by young players to sustain their football careers to lack of self-discipline.

FAZ Media Manager, Godfrey Chikumbi, said many talented players fail to progress to senior and professional football because of poor discipline and lack of guidance.

Chikumbi was speaking in an interview with the media at Football House in Lusaka.

He appealed to parents, guardians and other stakeholders to counsel their children playing football if they are to sustain their careers.

Mr Chikumbi has since called for continuous counselling of young players by parents to help them sustain their careers.

He said FAZ only spends little time with young players as most of the time they are in the communities with parents, hence the need to take good care of them.

“Do not leave the job of counselling players to FAZ alone as they spend very little time with them when they are in camp,” Chikumbi said.

Chikumbi alleged that most young players start indulging in illicit activities such as abusing drugs and other things, when they start doing well and become popular,

He said the behaviour has made most of them fail to excel in their careers.

The FAZ Media Manager also appealed to young players to emulate old players whose football careers lasted long due to self-discipline.

World.title: Journalism is not a favour to those in power
World.content:
THERE is a troubling misconception among some people in positions of power that journalists should know when to stop asking questions, soften their reporting or, more importantly, look the other way.

Sometimes, the expectation comes through telephone calls, intermediaries and colleagues appealing for an end to stories considered damaging to someone’s reputation.

But journalism is not about protecting reputations.

World.title: Sables dealt major blow as Kundiona ruled out with broken arm
World.content:
The Zimbabwe Sables have suffered a major setback ahead of their clash against Uruguay in London, with prop Cleopas Kundiona ruled out for the remainder of the tournament after breaking his arm.

Kundiona, who plays for English Premiership side Northampton Saints, brought valuable experience and physical presence to the Zimbabwe pack, particularly in the set piece. His absence will be a significant loss for head coach Pieter Benade as the Sables prepare for a demanding assignment against the South Americans.

World.title: Mzondo’s historic gold no fluke – NAAZ
World.content:
THE National Athletics Association of Zimbabwe (NAAZ) says Ropafadzo Mzondo’s historic gold medal triumph at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games was no accident, but the result of deliberate planning, preparation and investment in young talent.

NAAZ president Tendai Tagara said the association was delighted by the 17-year-old sprinter’s achievement, which saw Zimbabwe’s flag raised and the national anthem played on the global stage.

Mzondo made history on Tuesday after storming to victory in the men’s 200m final in 21.

World.title: 5 ZIMRA officials in court for bribery
World.content:
Five Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) officials stationed at the Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport have appeared in court on allegations of receiving bribes from returning residents and visitors.

The five—Sithabiso Ncube (47), Aquisilia Mbira (40), Norman Chepi (45), Ratidzo Danda (48), and Tafadzwa Ngwenya (44)—appeared before Harare regional magistrate Marehwanazvo Gofa, who granted them US$200 bail each and remanded the matter to November 27,2026.

It is the State’s case that on November 9, 2026, Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission (ZACC) detectives received a tip-off that some ZIMRA officials and other stakeholders stationed at Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport were allegedly soliciting cash bribes from returning residents and visitors entering Zimbabwe without the requisite documentation.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Developers’ body lobbies for statutory register to protect land buyers
World.content:
The Property Developers Association of Zimbabwe has called for a law compelling all land and property developers to register with a statutory body to restore public confidence in the property sector and protect land buyers from fraud.

Interim chairperson Arnold Khanda made the call on Wednesday in response to a recent government directive for local authorities to demolish all illegal structures in their areas of jurisdiction.

The move has left several families without shelter or a source of livelihood.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 11, 2026
World.content:
DR Congo Faces Growing Fears of a Cholera Resurgence

The Democratic Republic of Congo has reported more than 60,000 cholera cases since the beginning of the year, including 1,800 deaths. World Health Organisation (WHO) Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the situation represents the "worst cholera outbreak in decades." The eastern provinces of North and South Kivu have been hit particularly hard, with violence and insecurity hindering efforts to contain the outbreak. There are also growing concerns over the spread of the disease to the densely populated capital, Kinshasa, amid the rainy season. Health experts have cited poor access to clean water and sanitation, and called for greater prevention, better water systems and vaccination campaigns. Doctors Without Borders has increased its response by providing medical assistance, safe drinking water and sanitation support in affected communities, the agency said. However, insecurity, poor infrastructure and limited access to health care continue to hinder efforts to contain the outbreak.

UNICEF Warns Drones and Drought Are Deepening Sudan's Child Crisis

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

UNICEF has warned that escalating drone attacks on Sudan's power infrastructure, combined with severe drought, are creating a devastating humanitarian crisis for children. The agency said that up to 15 power stations were hit in October, disrupting water supplies, healthcare, irrigation and food production. Failed rains have severely damaged prospects for the 2026-27 harvest. An estimated 825,000 children under five are expected to suffer from severe acute malnutrition this year. UNICEF said that it has supported millions with healthcare, clean water, vaccinations and education but warns its response is only one-third funded. It said that two in three child casualties recorded this year have been caused by drone attacks, bringing the conflict into areas previously considered safe. The agency is calling for an end to attacks on civilian infrastructure, safe humanitarian access and urgent international funding to sustain essential services.

Violence in Northern Nigeria Forces Over 64,000 to Flee Across Borders

More than 64,000 people have fled violence in northern Nigeria to neighbouring Niger, while several hundred others have sought refuge in Benin since the beginning of the year, according to the UN refugee agency. The displacement is being driven by jihadist insurgencies, armed banditry and farmer-herder clashes, placing additional pressure on countries already facing insecurity and climate-related challenges. Many newly arrived refugees, including children, face food shortages, malnutrition, limited access to clean water and inadequate shelter. UNHCR said that only about five percent of this year's Nigerian arrivals have been registered because of funding constraints and is appealing for 11.4 million dollars to support humanitarian operations across Nigeria, Niger and Benin. Conditions are particularly difficult in Niger's Diffa region, where insecurity and drought have further weakened food production and livelihoods. The agency warns that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families could be left without essential humanitarian assistance and protection.

U.S. Issues Highest Travel Warning for 11 African Countries

The United States has issued its highest-level travel warning against 23 countries. It advised American citizens not to travel there under any circumstances because of security threats, unstable conditions, and limited consular assistance. The countries include several African nations: Burkina Faso, the Central African Republic, Chad, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Libya, Mali, Niger, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda. The Level 4 advisory is the highest category in the US State Department's four-tier travel warning system and urges citizens to avoid all travel to the affected destinations. The department said that the warnings are based on local security conditions and the US government's ability to provide assistance to its citizens. Americans have been urged to consult the State Department's travel advisory website for country-specific updates before making international travel arrangements.

How Egypt's Laws Are Being Used to Silence Independent Media

Egyptian authorities are facing renewed criticism over their crackdown on independent journalism following the conviction of Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah. A court ordered the closure of the independent news outlet, fined Attalah three million Egyptian pounds (about U.S.$54,000) and ordered the confiscation of its equipment for operating without a licence, despite repeated attempts by the publication to obtain registration. The Committee to Protect Journalists said that the case highlights how licensing requirements, criminal penalties and website blocking are being used to restrict press freedom. Attalah's legal team disputes claims that she waived her right to appeal, with the first appeal hearing scheduled for November 25. The case has also raised concerns about other independent outlets facing similar licensing difficulties and restrictions.

WHO Warns of Critical Gaps in Africa's Health Data Systems

The World Health Organisation has warned that critical weaknesses in Africa's health information systems are undermining efforts to identify health threats and improve healthcare delivery. A new report assessing 40 countries found that fewer than half notify authorities of at least 80% of deaths, while only 21 countries record causes for a similar proportion of registered deaths. The report also highlights limited capacity to analyse and verify health data, inadequate funding and shortages of trained professionals. However, progress is being made, with 43 of the WHO's 47 African member states having adopted digital platforms to collect and report routine health information. The findings were presented at the first African Health Data Forum in Nairobi, where officials are also discussing how digital technology and artificial intelligence can strengthen healthcare systems. WHO said that responsible use of AI will require appropriate legislation, safeguards and regulatory frameworks.

Close 

South African Olympic Champion Tatjana Smith Switches Allegiance to Netherlands

South Africa's most decorated Olympic athlete, Tatjana Smith, has announced she will switch her sporting allegiance to the Netherlands. She cited financial and practical challenges in sustaining her swimming career. The two-time Olympic gold medallist said she understood the decision could disappoint South African supporters but viewed it as an opportunity to explore her Dutch heritage and access better high-performance support. Smith, who holds dual citizenship, retired after the 2024 Paris Olympics but recently announced her comeback, targeting the 2028 Los Angeles Games. She will continue training in South Africa while representing the Netherlands. She won gold in the 200-metre breaststroke at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and the 100-metre breaststroke in Paris in 2024. She also claimed two silver medals across the two Games, making her South Africa's most successful Olympic athlete.

World.title: South Africa: Matlala Says He Didn't Know Impalas Were for Sibiya - South African News Briefs - November 11, 2026
World.content:
press review

Matlala Says He Didn't Know Impalas Were for Sibiya

Alleged crime kingpin Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala has told the Madlanga Commission that he was unaware 20 impalas he agreed to give away were destined for former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya's home, reports EWN. Matlala said he only discovered the intended recipient when arranging their transportation. He denied allegations that the animals were a gift in exchange for helping him secure a R360 million SAPS tender. He also accused Sibiya of pressuring and extorting him, claiming he feared for his safety and that of his family. His testimony comes amid scrutiny of financial dealings between the two, including payments totalling R550,000 and discussions about purchasing a plot of land.

SABC Warns of Broadcast Disruptions Amid Power Outage



The South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) has warned audiences of disruptions to some broadcasting services following a prolonged power outage in Auckland Park and surrounding areas, reports SABC News. The public broadcaster has been relying on generator power since Sunday, but extended use of backup systems has affected normal transmission across certain platforms. City Power says it cannot confirm when electricity will be restored following a secondary explosion. The SABC says its technical teams are working to minimise disruptions while engaging relevant stakeholders to restore services.

Lottery Operator Sizekhaya Misses Sales Targets by 39%

New national lottery operator Sizekhaya Holdings has fallen 39% short of its projected ticket sales, reports EWN. It generated R2.1 billion against an anticipated R3.5 billion between June 2025 and September 2026. The National Lotteries Commission said that the decline is not unusual during a transition to a new operator. He acknowledged that Sizekhaya has also missed its revised sales targets. This comes after the Pretoria High Court set aside the awarding of the lottery contract over concerns about Trade Minister Parks Tau's tender evaluation process and ordered a fresh process within six months. Sizekhaya will, however, continue operating the lottery for at least another year while legal proceedings are finalised. Tau is still considering whether to appeal the ruling.

World.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Tells UN Envoy Eritrea, Sudan Backing Armed Groups and Drone Attacks
World.content:
Addis Abeba — Ethiopia has accused Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki and Sudan's army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan of supporting, arming and coordinating armed groups operating inside Ethiopia, including through repeated drone attacks, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Horn of Africa adviser Getachew K. Reda said.

Getachew disclosed the accusations following a meeting on Wednesday with Guang Cong, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa, during which they discussed conflicts in Sudan and Somalia, as well as what he described as Eritrea's destabilizing role in the region.

In a statement posted on his official social media account, Getachew said he had presented Ethiopia's position on what he described as activities by the Eritrean and Sudanese leadership to equip and coordinate armed elements inside Ethiopia. He also accused them of carrying out repeated drone attacks inside the country.

Getachew said he had urged both governments to stop supporting and arming the groups, arguing that doing so was necessary for meaningful dialogue and to prevent further escalation.



The discussions also addressed prospects for de-escalating the conflict in Sudan, although Getachew did not provide further details of the envoy's response or identify any specific agreements reached during the meeting.

The accusations come amid heightened regional tensions involving Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan, with Addis Abeba repeatedly raising concerns over alleged external support for armed groups operating inside its territory.

Getachew said he and the UN envoy agreed that dialogue rather than military confrontation offered the best path forward, concluding that "talking, not shooting is the best game in town."

Editorial note: The allegations against Eritrea and Sudan's military leadership have not been independently verified. The statement did not include responses from Asmara or Khartoum.

Getachew's accusations come amid escalating diplomatic tensions between Ethiopia and Sudan, following reciprocal expulsions of diplomatic staff and the closure of consular offices in both countries.

On 4 November 2026, Addis Standard reported that Ethiopia had ordered six Sudanese diplomatic staff members to leave the country within 48 hours, following the closure of Sudan's consulate in Assosa, the administrative centre of Benishangul-Gumuz Regional State. A senior Ethiopian official confirmed the expulsions to Reuters but did not disclose the reason for the decision.

The following day, Addis Standard reported that Sudan had closed Ethiopia's consulate in the eastern city of Gedaref and ordered Ethiopian diplomatic staff to leave in retaliation for the Assosa closure and the expulsion of Sudanese diplomats. Two Sudanese officials confirmed the reciprocal measures to Reuters.

The diplomatic measures came amid competing accusations by the two governments of supporting armed groups operating in each other's territories, adding to concerns over the widening regional tensions.

The reciprocal diplomatic measures come days after Sudan's army-aligned government announced that it had lodged formal complaints against Ethiopia with the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and the African Union Peace and Security Council (AUPSC), accusing Addis Abeba of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to use Ethiopian territory to launch drone attacks against civilian infrastructure in Sudan.

The move adds another layer to an increasingly volatile diplomatic standoff in which both governments accuse the other of supporting their adversaries. Sudan alleges that Ethiopia is facilitating RSF operations, while Addis Abeba accuses Khartoum of backing Tigrayan rebels involved in renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia. Both sides deny the allegations against them.

Close 

The diplomatic escalation also comes amid Ethiopia's deteriorating relations with Eritrea. On 1 October, Addis Standard reported that Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara and declared 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Abeba persona non grata, ordering them to leave within 48 hours. The Ministry cited what it described as Eritrea's "direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence against Ethiopia," alleging that the diplomats had engaged in activities threatening national security without publicly specifying the incidents.

The measures against Sudanese diplomats and Eritrean officials underscore the mounting diplomatic pressures facing Addis Abeba as security disputes increasingly intersect across the Horn of Africa. Ethiopia has also accused Egypt and Eritrea of supporting Tigrayan rebels who launched an offensive against government forces in September. Both countries have denied the allegations.

World.title: Kenya: Sudan Lifts 20-Month Ban On Kenyan Tea Imports After Ruto Talks
World.content:
Nairobi — Sudan has lifted a 20-month ban on Kenyan tea imports following talks between President William Ruto and Prime Minister Kamil Idris, reopening an important export market for Kenyan traders.

The decision was announced by Ruto after his meeting with Idris on the sidelines of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Heads of State and Government Summit in Harare, Zimbabwe.

The restriction had blocked Kenyan tea exporters from accessing the Sudanese market for nearly two years, disrupting trade and limiting opportunities for local traders and producers.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Ruto welcomed the move, saying it would restore market access for exporters and support the livelihoods of tea farmers and their families.

"Kenya welcomes and appreciates this decision, which reopens an important market for our tea, restores opportunities for our exporters and supports the livelihoods of our farmers and their families," he said.

He described the development as evidence of the role of diplomatic engagement in resolving trade barriers and strengthening economic ties between the two countries.

"This progress demonstrates what dialogue and constructive diplomacy can achieve. We look forward to strengthening our bilateral relations, expanding trade and working together for peace, stability and shared prosperity in our region," Ruto said.

The reopening offers Kenyan tea traders an opportunity to resume business with Sudanese buyers after the prolonged interruption, potentially boosting export earnings from one of the country's leading agricultural commodities.

Tea remains a major source of foreign exchange for Kenya, supporting millions of livelihoods across production, processing and marketing.

However, the announcement did not specify when imports would resume or whether any additional conditions would apply to Kenyan tea shipments.

World.title: Nigeria: Nigerian-Born Emehelu Makes History As New Jersey's Lieutenant Governor
World.content:
Nigerian-born American lawyer, Shirley U. Emehelu, has made history as the first immigrant to become Lieutenant Governor of New Jersey, U.S.

Emehelu, who emigrated from Nigeria as a child, was appointed by Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Monday, becoming the fifth Lieutenant Governor of the state.

The appointment also makes history, as New Jersey's two highest executive offices are occupied by women simultaneously for the first time.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The appointment represents a milestone for Nigerian-Americans, whose participation in U.S. public life now includes one of the highest executive positions in American state government.

Emehelu also assumed the position of Secretary of State, consolidating responsibilities in government administration, electoral oversight and public service.

She was sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton by Chief Justice Stuart Rabner, with her husband and children participating in the ceremony.

Announcing the appointment, Sherrill described Emehelu as an experienced public servant whose career demonstrated integrity, accountability and a commitment to protecting residents.

"Shirley embodies those values," the governor declared, referring to her administration's emphasis on accountability and public service.

Sherrill said Emehelu's record in prosecuting financial crimes, protecting consumers, defending civil rights and combating government waste informed her selection.

The governor explained that Emehelu had also demonstrated effective leadership while overseeing the administration of New Jersey's recent elections as Acting Secretary of State.

Accepting the appointment, Emehelu expressed appreciation for the confidence reposed in her and reaffirmed her commitment to serving the state's diverse population.

"I've spent my career upholding the law, protecting families, and rooting out fraud, abuse, and corruption," she said.

Emehelu also acknowledged the significance of her Nigerian heritage and the opportunities her appointment represented for immigrant and minority communities.

"As a Black woman and Nigerian American, I'm proud of what this appointment represents for our state, and especially for the communities that share my heritage," she said.

She expressed hope that the occasion would encourage younger generations to pursue public service and contribute meaningfully to their communities.

"I hope we can inspire the next generation to find their own ways to serve and make a little history of their own too," she said.

The lieutenant governor pledged to support Sherrill's administration in addressing living costs, expanding economic opportunities and ensuring more responsive government.

Reflecting on her years in public service, Emehelu identified the protection of ordinary citizens as the central motivation behind her professional career.

"The throughline across my federal and state service has been defending the people who are counting on government to do right by them," she said.

Emehelu previously served as New Jersey's Acting State Comptroller, overseeing efforts to combat fraud, financial mismanagement and waste involving public resources.

Between 2022 and 2024, she was the state's Executive Assistant Attorney General, the third-ranking official in the Attorney General's Office, overseeing major civil litigation and enforcement matters.

Close 

She also served for nine years as a federal prosecutor in the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of New Jersey, handling complex financial fraud cases.

During her federal service, she became Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, overseeing programmes involving forfeited assets, money laundering and restitution for victims.

A graduate of Yale University and Yale Law School, Emehelu also worked in private legal practice and served as a judicial clerk in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

Her appointment followed the September resignation of former lieutenant governor Dale Caldwell after allegations of misconduct and violations of state ethics rules, which he disputed.

Emehelu is married to Ikenna Emehelu and they have two children, Nnamdi and Amara. (NAN)

World.title: Liberia: Senate Opens Public Hearing On War Crimes, Anti-Corruption Courts
World.content:
The Liberian Senate has invited civil society organizations, victims' groups, human rights advocates, legal practitioners and other stakeholders to participate in a public hearing on proposed legislation seeking to establish a Special War Crimes Court for Liberia (SWCTL) and a Special Economic and Corruption Crimes Court under the proposed National Anti-Corruption Court Act.

The hearing, scheduled for November 25, 2026, at the Senate Chamber Annex in Monrovia, is intended to provide a platform for public consultation, allowing stakeholders to present recommendations and express their views on the proposed laws before they are forwarded to the full Senate for consideration.

The legislative initiative seeks to establish accountability mechanisms for addressing atrocities committed during Liberia's civil conflicts, alongside specialized judicial arrangements for prosecuting economic and corruption-related offenses.

The invitation was extended by the Senate Standing Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights, Claims and Petitions as part of efforts to gather public input and conduct further consultations on the harmonized bills.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The proposed hearing is expected to bring together representatives of civil society organizations, victims' associations, human rights defenders, legal professionals, government institutions and other national and international stakeholders whose contributions could help shape the proposed judicial frameworks.

Welcoming the Senate's decision, Adama K. Dempster, National Secretary General of the Civil Society Human Rights Advocacy Platform of Liberia and a longstanding advocate for the establishment of a War and Economic Crimes Court, described the invitation as an important development in Liberia's pursuit of justice, accountability and the rule of law.

In a statement issued on November 9, Dempster expressed appreciation to the Senate for opening the legislative process to broader public participation, noting that meaningful engagement with citizens and relevant institutions is necessary to ensure that the proposed courts reflect national expectations and accepted international standards.

"We want to thank the Senate for engaging a broad range of stakeholders and conducting due diligence in the legislative process on this matter. This public hearing represents an important milestone in Liberia's quest for justice and accountability," Dempster stated.

He emphasized that consultations involving victims, survivors, legal experts and other citizens would be essential to ensuring that the proposed judicial institutions are appropriately designed, independent and capable of fulfilling their intended mandates.

According to him, the legislative process must adequately address the rights and interests of victims while guaranteeing due process and fair trial protections for accused persons.

He further stressed that the proposed courts should be consistent with international standards, strengthen public confidence in the justice system and establish credible mechanisms for addressing Liberia's history of conflict-related atrocities and corruption.

Dempster said the proposed Special War Crimes Court represents a longstanding demand of Liberia's human rights community, transitional justice advocates and civil society organizations, particularly those calling for the implementation of recommendations contained in the report of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC).

The TRC, established following Liberia's civil conflicts, made recommendations intended to address the country's history of human rights violations, promote national reconciliation and establish accountability for serious crimes committed during the war years.

Dempster noted that the November 25 hearing would also provide an opportunity for national and international experts to contribute technical perspectives on the proposed court's mandate, jurisdiction, institutional independence, organizational structure and operational effectiveness.

He said such contributions would be important in ensuring that the final legislation provides a sound legal and institutional foundation for the proposed accountability mechanisms.

The civil society advocate also commended the Senate for acknowledging the initial submission of a draft War Crimes Court bill by civil society organizations and the Independent National Commission on Human Rights (INCHR) in 2025.

He described the recognition of that submission as an important part of the consultative process, emphasizing that civil society and human rights organizations have consistently advocated for the establishment of accountability institutions to address the consequences of Liberia's civil conflicts.

"We therefore want to appreciate the Liberian Senate for creating this space for public engagement through dialogue and recognizing civil society and the Independent National Commission on Human Rights initial submission of the war court crimes draft bill in 2025.

"Civil society and the human rights community remain committed to participating constructively in these processes and supporting efforts aimed at delivering justice for victims while promoting reconciliation, accountability, and lasting peace," he added.

Dempster further linked the Senate's current legislative initiative to the Joint Resolution adopted in April 2024 by both Houses of the 55th National Legislature, which supported the process toward establishing war and economic crimes courts in Liberia.

The resolution provided a legislative basis for advancing the national conversation and institutional process surrounding accountability for war-era atrocities and economic crimes.

Close 

Against this background, he urged victims' associations, youth and women's organizations, religious institutions, traditional leaders, development partners and members of the wider Liberian public to take advantage of the November 25 hearing to contribute to the national dialogue.

He stressed that the establishment of the proposed courts should not be viewed solely as an effort to address crimes committed during the country's past conflicts but also as part of broader efforts to strengthen democratic governance, combat impunity and promote respect for human rights.

"We believe the establishment of these accountability mechanisms is not only about addressing the crimes of the past; it is about strengthening democratic governance, combating impunity, promoting national healing, and ensuring that future generations inherit a society founded on justice and respect for human rights," Dempster stated.

He maintained that the public hearing represents a significant opportunity for Liberians to participate directly in shaping the country's accountability framework and contribute to the development of institutions capable of addressing serious violations and economic offenses.

The Senate's planned consultation comes amid longstanding national discussions over the implementation of the TRC recommendations and the establishment of specialized judicial institutions to address war-related atrocities and economic and corruption crimes.

World.title: South Africa: Ministers Pocket Pay Hikes As Millions Battle to Survive
World.content:
The increase adds about R97,725 a year to a minister's remuneration package and R46,304 to an ordinary MP's package.

The announcement came on the same day Stats SA reported that unemployment had risen to 33.7%, with 8.6 million people officially unemployed.

Ministers will get nearly R98,000 more a year after President Cyril Ramaphosa approved salary increases for politicians, a decision unions have condemned as millions struggle to make ends meet.

The South African Federation of Trade Unions (Saftu) wants the 3.5% increase reversed, arguing that political leaders should put struggling households first.

The Presidency announced the increases on Tuesday, 10 November. They are backdated to 1 April 2026.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The 3.5% adjustment covers ministers, deputy ministers, members of Parliament, premiers, members of provincial executive councils and provincial legislators.

Based on previously gazetted remuneration, the increase adds about R97,725 a year to a minister's package and R46,304 to an ordinary MP's.

These are increases in total remuneration packages, which include pension contributions, rather than additional take-home pay.

Saftu general secretary Zwelinzima Vavi said the decision could not be justified against the country's unemployment crisis.

"This decision is indefensible in a country where, in the second quarter of 2026, 8.5 million people were officially unemployed and another 4.6 million formed part of the potential labour force. That means 13.1 million people were unemployed or part of the potential labour force," Vavi said, according to The Citizen.

Those figures refer to April to June. Newer figures released by Statistics South Africa on Tuesday show that official unemployment rose to 33.7% in the third quarter, with 8.6 million people unemployed.

The number of unemployed people increased by 97,000, even though employment also grew by 101,000 to 16.8 million.

The potential labour force is counted separately from official unemployment. It includes discouraged jobseekers and others who meet some, but not all, of the criteria for being officially unemployed.

Ramaphosa also approved a separate 4% increase for judges, magistrates, traditional leaders and members of national and provincial houses of traditional and Khoi-San leaders.

The Presidency said the decision followed recommendations from the Independent Commission for the Remuneration of Public Office-Bearers.

The commission considered factors including inflation, the affordability of increases for the state, previous pay decisions and average annual wage increases.

The Presidency said Ramaphosa urged public office-bearers to uphold their responsibilities and honour the public's trust.

Close 

Saftu accepted the separate increase for judges but called on Ramaphosa and Parliament to reverse the 3.5% adjustment for politicians.

"At a time when millions are unemployed, and households are being pushed deeper into hardship, leadership must be measured by service to the people, not by higher pay for those already entrusted with governing them," Vavi said.

World.title: Uganda: Erratic Museveni Son Deactivates X Handle After Threats Against Uganda VP
World.content:
Nairobi — Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has deactivated his X account following a series of threats against Vice President Jessica Alupo, adding to a record of provocative online pronouncements by President Yoweri Museveni's son.

Muhoozi accused Alupo of supporting what he called the "treachery" of former deputy military chief Peter Elwelu, who was arrested on November over allegations of involvement in activities aimed at destabilising the country.

"There are already strong signals that Jessica was supporting the treachery of Elweru. If that is true she will account for it," he posted.

He subsequently threatened to remove her from government.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"As Deputy Commander-in-Chief, Jessica will be dismissed from our government soon. We have very many supporters in Teso. We don't have to rely on traitors."

In another post, Muhoozi suggested that Uganda would be governed on military terms if he became Vice President.

"As Vice President, the government will operate on military terms. There will be no more inefficiency," he wrote.

He later threatened to arrest Alupo if she was found to have supported Elwelu.

"We shall arrest Jessica, without hesitation if she is part of Elweru's treachery," he posted.

Muhoozi also invoked previous confrontations with opposition figures as evidence that his threats should be taken seriously.

"I told you I would arrest Besigye and I did. I told you I would defeat Kabobi and I did. I told you I would arrest Lukwago and I did. And many more. I think you should start believing me," he wrote.

The posts have drawn fresh attention to Muhoozi's use of social media to pronounce on political and security matters, including threats against senior government officials.

Museveni succession contest

The latest outburst comes as Muhoozi increasingly positions himself at the centre of Uganda's succession debate, with his Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU) movement mobilising support for a possible presidential bid in 2031.

Widely viewed as Museveni's presumed successor, Muhoozi faces competing political ambitions within the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM), where supporters of both father and son have increasingly clashed over the country's political future.

PLU has insisted that it operates within the broader NRM framework rather than as a separate political party, even as it pursues a nationwide mobilisation drive for Muhoozi.

During a recent mobilisation meeting, a key PLU figure Jimmy Lwanga warned NRM supporters against attempts to frustrate the movement's activities or undermine Muhoozi's presidential ambitions.

"Everything PLU does has the president's endorsement, and we therefore call upon members of NRM to also join in support of Gen. MK," Lwanga said.

PLU has been distributing endorsement books through its structures across the country as it seeks to consolidate support ahead of the 2031 election.

Muhoozi, however, would have to leave military service before seeking elective political office.

Earlier controversies

Muhoozi's online conduct has previously triggered diplomatic criticism, including from Washington.

In January 2026, US Senator Jim Risch, Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, rejected an apology issued by Muhoozi after a series of controversial posts directed at the United States.

Risch described the apology as hollow and insufficient, saying Muhoozi had crossed a "red line" despite deleting the posts.

The US Senator urged Washington to impose tougher sanctions on Uganda, arguing that an apology did not address wider concerns about the country's conduct and respect for democratic norms.

That same month, Muhoozi threatened to kill opposition leader Bobi Wine following Uganda's disputed presidential election.

"We have killed 22 NUP terrorists since last week. I'm praying the 23rd is Kabobi," he wrote, referring to the opposition leader by a derogatory nickname.

He also issued Wine a 48-hour ultimatum to surrender to police, threatening to treat him as an outlaw or rebel.

The remarks came as Wine remained in hiding following a security raid on his home and rejected the election results that handed Museveni another term.

Muhoozi has also intervened in government administration and military affairs.

In September, he directed ministers to obtain his permission before travelling abroad, threatening a fine of 30 million Ugandan shillings for those who left without his clearance.

The directive followed his questioning of a trip to Türkiye by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Haruna Kasolo, who subsequently said he would seek Muhoozi's guidance and authority before undertaking future travel.

Close 

In November, Muhoozi announced that he intended to leave the position of Chief of Defence Forces within months and dedicate his life to Christ.

"My time as CDF is coming to an end. I have accomplished all the tasks my God gave me. In a few months I will handover this office to a qualified officer. I shall dedicate my life to Christ after that," he wrote, without specifying a handover date or naming a successor.

Days earlier, he had announced the demotion of his former deputy Elwelu from Lieutenant General to private.

Muhoozi's public pronouncements have also previously shifted. In March 2022, he announced his retirement from the army after 28 years of service, prompting speculation about his political ambitions.

"After 28 years of service in my glorious military, the greatest military in the world, I am happy to announce my retirement," he wrote.

He later walked back the announcement, indicating that he would instead retire eight years later.

Appointed Chief of Defence Forces in March 2024, Muhoozi has increasingly become a central figure in Uganda's political succession debate, with his public interventions drawing scrutiny both at home and abroad.

World.title: Former ESPN star Sean Salisbury says political arguments wore out fans who just wanted sports
World.content:
Sean Salisbury thinks ESPN lost sight of the person coming home after a long day at work who just wanted to watch some sports. That viewer wanted highlights and a few laughs. Instead, Salisbury said, too much of the programming became another argument about politics.

"If I want that, I'll get it on a different channel," he told OutKick.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

I spoke with the former NFL quarterback and ESPN analyst in October about the network where we both worked. Salisbury spent 12 years there, leaving in 2008. I arrived in 2012 and stayed until 2021.

ESPN’S FAVORITE INSIDER ACCIDENTALLY EXPLAINED WHY MOST AMERICANS DON’T TRUST THE MEDIA

To me, ESPN was at its best in the early 2000s. Salisbury was part of that, along with the people who made you want to watch a studio show even when you already knew what happened in the games.

"It was sports first with entertainment personalities," Salisbury said.

He remembered watching the same edition of SportsCenter several times because he enjoyed the people delivering the highlights.

Salisbury says ESPN got caught up chasing reactions

Salisbury's father was a blue-collar worker, and that shaped how he thought about the people watching him on television. Someone who had spent all day working construction probably wanted to sit down and enjoy a game or some highlights.

Salisbury believes ESPN made that harder by letting political and social arguments take up too much of its programming.

"We really weren't concerned with what the color of the skin of the quarterback was because we were just talking football," he said of his years at the network.

He also blamed the pressure to generate a reaction on social media. In his view, talking about the sports news increasingly gave way to trying to become the sports news, with arguments designed to get people sharing clips.

CNN PANELIST BLAMES 'CULTURE WAR' RETRIBUTION AS REASON FOR RYAN CLARK'S ESPN DEPARTURE

I think that's a big part of it. Once getting a reaction becomes the goal, there's always a reason to make the next argument more outlandish and controversial. Eventually, the viewer who wanted to hear about his team has to sit through a debate about something an analyst said on another show.

Salisbury acknowledged that politics and sports overlap, and he said those subjects deserve coverage when they're relevant. His complaint was about how much of the programming those discussions consumed.

"That should be the outlier, not the every single day grind," he said.

Our conversation started with the argument over Emmanuel Acho's comments about NFL Live. In July, Acho credited Ryan Clark with building the show into a "juggernaut." He acknowledged that Clark hadn't created it, but dismissed its earlier audience by claiming "nobody was watching NFL Live then."

As I pointed out on social media, that's false. NFL Live averaged around 650,000 daily viewers in 2011 and 2012, before Clark was even hired by ESPN. The version featuring Clark never averaged an audience that size.

Salisbury and former host Trey Wingo both weighed in on social media, as well. Wingo wrote, "'Let your apology be as loud as your disrespect.' I think somebody said that once."

Salisbury posted, "Should one of us tell him" and tagged NFL Live alums Wingo, Mark Schlereth, Mike Golic, Merril Hoge, and Mark Malone.

"Acho was about two decades late to the party on that one, so no shock there," he told me.

He compared overlooking the original group to talking about Led Zeppelin without Jimmy Page. Other people could come along and do good work, but that didn't erase what the earlier crew had built.

And Salisbury's memories of that period went well beyond wanting credit for NFL Live. He talked about learning from broadcasters whose personalities made the shows worth watching, particularly Dan Patrick, Chris Berman and Mike Tirico.

That's the ESPN he wants people to be able to turn on again.

I watched the way people talked about ESPN change

When I got hired at ESPN in 2012, the reaction from my family was pretty much what you'd expect: "You got a job at ESPN? That's incredible!"

By the time I left in 2021, some of those same people had a very different reaction to hearing where I worked. "You work at ESPN? Oh."

I told Salisbury that I don't miss working at ESPN. But I do miss producing live radio.

I'd spend all week preparing a four-hour Saturday show, then news would break while we were on the air and we'd have to adjust. I loved that part of the job. There were a lot of moving pieces, and getting it right gave me an adrenaline rush.

PAUL FINEBAUM SAYS ESPN BANNED HIM FROM SHOWS AFTER TELLING OUTKICK HE MIGHT RUN FOR OFFICE

Salisbury knew exactly what I meant. For him, live television was about as close as broadcasting could get to the feeling of playing quarterback in the NFL.

He recalled sitting beside Tirico on Monday Night Countdown when a camera went down just before the show started. Salisbury was sweating over how they were going to handle it. Tirico made it look routine.

"Nobody at home would have ever known," Salisbury said.

He also repeatedly credited the producers and other employees behind the scenes who made those shows work. His years at ESPN gave him close friends and taught him how to do the broadcasting work he still does.

"Those 12 years changed my life," he said.

Salisbury still sees programming at ESPN that delivers what he's talking about. He singled out College GameDay, calling it "the best studio show on the planet."

Salisbury wants ESPN's analysts saying what they actually believe.

"I think sometimes we all get caught up in it, saying stuff to appease somebody else as opposed to what you actually believe, and I'm just not willing to do that," Salisbury said. "I think it loses credibility."

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The ESPN Salisbury and I remember gave viewers a reason to keep watching after the highlights were over. He thinks the network still has the people to do that, provided it remembers why those viewers turned on a sports channel in the first place.

"Hopefully we can get back to where we're actually talking sports more than we're talking about why somebody should have voted for somebody else," he said.

World.title: Horny bull elk keeps attacking cars, forces Missouri wildlife park to close indefinitely
World.content:
A wildlife park in Missouri has been forced to close indefinitely because one particularly aggressive bull elk won't stop attacking visitors' cars.

Lone Elk Park, located just outside St. Louis, closed Monday after officials decided the animal had become too much of a safety risk. Apparently, the problem is that he's young, he's horny, and he's new to this whole being-in-charge thing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

According to St. Louis Public Radio, the bull recently replaced his own father as the dominant male in the herd. This is his first mating season running the show, and he's not exactly handling his newfound responsibilities gracefully.

"We have a younger, more inexperienced herd bull this year," Eric Johnson, acting director of St. Louis County Parks and Recreation, said. "It's his first year, and he's acting a little bit like a teenager."

One visitor, Theresa Hammer, learned that the hard way.

Hammer told St. Louis Public Radio she was sitting in her Ford Fusion last week when the bull approached her vehicle. She looked away briefly, and when she looked back, he was ramming his antlers into the front of her car.

"I looked back up, and he hit the front of my car with his horns," she said. "He scratched up the whole side of my car, my hood and put a big dent in the rear quarter panel."

Despite the damage, Hammer said she doesn't blame the elk. After all, she's the one driving through his home.

Lone Elk Park is a 546-acre drive-through wildlife park where visitors can observe elk, bison and other animals from their vehicles. Officials had posted warnings about keeping a safe distance from the elk, but visitors weren't always following them.

And with the bull becoming increasingly aggressive, the county decided it was safer to close the park until he settles down.

BULL ELK IN COLORADO NICKNAMED 'SMASH' IS CHASING OFF TRUCKS AND GOLF CARTS

For what it's worth, this kind of behavior isn't unusual during the elk rut, which is the annual breeding season. Bull elk experience a surge in testosterone and become more territorial as they compete for females. That can make them particularly dangerous to people who get too close.

But even by elk standards, this guy is apparently a handful.

Johnson, who has worked for the parks department for 32 years, said it's been roughly a decade since they've dealt with a bull quite this worked up.

"Some of [the bulls] have it figured out and they calmly go about their business, and sometimes it's like this," he said.

Officials haven't announced a reopening date, but they're monitoring the bull's behavior daily and hope to reopen the park within the next several days.



So, for now, an entire wildlife park is closed because one young elk can't get his hormones under control.

Nature is beautiful.

Darchiev served on one of the most critical and demanding fronts of Russian foreign policy."

"We express our deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and loved ones of Alexander Nikitich Darchiev," the statement added. "The cherished memory of our untimely departed colleague will forever remain in our hearts."

Fox News confirmed the death came in Russia and not the U.S.

MELANIA TRUMP HAILS OLESHKY CEASEFIRE AS POTENTIAL ‘SPARK’ FOR PROGRESS AMID UKRAINE-RUSSIA WAR

Russia's Vladimir Putin appointed Darchiev, a veteran diplomat known in the past for his public denunciations of the West, as ambassador to Washington in March 2025 to lead a rapprochement with the Trump administration that has rattled Ukraine, the European Union and NATO.

His death comes less than a week after a White House news conference hailing a temporary ceasefire in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russia.

First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine hailed the ceasefire in the Oleshky region.

"We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark."

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

Shortly after being tapped as ambassador, Darchiev met with Trump administration officials and delivered a message of hope for peace.

"Russia and the United States are destined, as great powers, to have non-confrontational peaceful existence," Darchiev said during a June 10, 2025, Russia Day reception at the Russian Embassy in Washington after delivering his credentials to the White House, adding, "our discussion was very constructive."

Before taking the helm of the Russian Embassy in Washington, Darchiev played a role as the Kremlin’s point man for high-stakes bilateral negotiations, most notably during the delicate discussions that led to prisoner swaps involving imprisoned arms dealer Viktor Bout and detained Americans Brittney Griner and Paul Whelan.

EVAN GERSHKOVICH DETAILS RUSSIAN ARREST, REVEALS MOMENT THAT NEARLY BROKE HIM DURING WRONGFUL DETENTION

In August 2022, while serving as the director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s North American Department, Darchiev provided the first on-the-record Russian confirmation that Moscow and Washington were actively discussing those situations.

"This quite sensitive issue of the swap of convicted Russian and U.S. citizens is being pursued along the channels designated by our presidents," Darchiev told the Russian state news agency TASS. "The individuals are, indeed, being discussed. The Russian side has long been seeking the release of Viktor Bout. The negotiations are bearing fruit."

World.title: Teen charged with murder in fatal shooting of 15-year-old NYC student Javits Frimpong

A 17-year-old boy has been arrested after a teenager was fatally shot while walking to school in New York City last month, police announced Wednesday.

The teen suspect, who has not been publicly identified, faces a murder charge in the Oct. 29 death of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, according to the New York City Police Department (NYPD).

"The NYPD will be relentless in our efforts to get dangerous people out of our communities, especially when it involves the murder of a 15-year-old boy," the department wrote in a post on X.

Javits, a Ghanaian immigrant, was fatally shot in the stomach in the Bronx. His father believes the killing may be linked to ongoing bullying his son experienced at school.

Just two days before the tragedy, the school’s principal had called Thomas Frimpong to report that his son was being targeted and that two students had been suspended as a result.

The tragic killing sparked local protests and urgent calls from community members to end youth violence and bullying.

Last week, NYPD Chief of Detectives Joseph Kenny noted that investigators were exploring multiple angles.

"The alleged bullying is one aspect that we’re looking at, as well as some others," Kenny told the New York Post.

"All three gave chase," Kenny added. "And these cowards shot him in the back. If their intention was to rob him, he dropped his backpack."

PARENTS IN BRONX NEIGHBORHOOD PLEAD FOR NYPD GUARD AS MAMDANI CUTS COPS, HALTS HIRES: 'HORRIBLE SITUATION'

"As of right now, all indications are that he was trying to live the American dream," the chief said. "He was trying to get ahead by going to school. We have nothing in our investigation to indicate he was involved in any gang activity. Seems like he was just a very good kid."

The tragedy also prompted federal intervention to support the grieving family. President Donald Trump agreed to grant Javits’ mother an emergency visa so she could travel to the United States from Ghana to lay her son to rest.

"The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote in a Nov. 2 post on X.

"Javits Frimpong’s mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately."

Actor Jim Caviezel said he nearly turned down the role of Jesus in "The Passion of the Christ," but an encounter he described as a visit from Jesus convinced him to reconsider.

"About 5 something in the morning, this presence came over me, and I know it was him," Caviezel, 58, told Sean Hannity on his "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

"I was awake, but my eyes were closed, and he was sitting Indian style on the foot of my bed, and he said, 'It is not a requirement of you as a Catholic… to play this role.' And I said, 'Good, I won't. Get somebody else.'"

STEPHEN BALDWIN ON CHOOSING BORN-AGAIN CHRISTIANITY OVER HOLLYWOOD AFTER A LIFE-CHANGING ENCOUNTER WITH GOD

Caviezel said the figure appeared sad after he refused, leading to an exchange that prompted him to reconsider.

"I said, 'Get somebody else,' and his countenance changed, and then he says, 'I don't have anybody else,'" Caviezel recalled.

When Caviezel questioned why he had been chosen, he said the figure responded that others would not ask the same question of him. After some exchange, Caviezel was convinced the role was his to play.

"Immediately, I was like, OK, this is part of the plan. I'm in," he said.

MEL GIBSON REVEALS ‘THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST’S’ MOST SURPRISING LEGACY IN NEW RAYMOND ARROYO INTERVIEW

Caviezel is best known for his performance as Christ in the Mel Gibson-directed 2004 film "The Passion of the Christ," which follows the final hours of Jesus' life, including his crucifixion.

The role became a defining performance of his career, but Caviezel said filming took a severe physical toll.

During production, Caviezel said he injured his shoulder, suffered hypothermia and was struck by lightning while filming a scene.

"It nearly killed me," Caviezel recalled of the hypothermia.

"When you watch the end of the movie, I'm blue for a reason. My body's blue. There's no fake stuff there."

The podcast episode comes as the actor returns to the big screen in the action thriller "Ghost Soldier" and prepares for the release of "Zero A.D.: The Birth of Christ," in which he plays King Herod.

During his conversation with Hannity, Caviezel also discussed what he described as a near-death experience, the lasting impact of his work with Mel Gibson and the spiritual battles he believes have shaped his life and career.

Viewers and listeners can find the Fox News host's full conversation with Caviezel on the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast, available on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and iHeartRadio.

World.title: GOP congressman-elect makes unusual Trump request, ejects reporter during profanity-laced victory speech
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Anthony Constantino, a former boxer and the CEO of the printing company Sticker Mule, delivered a profanity-laden victory speech after his election to New York’s 21st Congressional District, kicking a reporter out of the room and calling on President Donald Trump to pardon Sean "Diddy" Combs.

"I think President Trump should consider freeing Diddy," Constantino said, referring to the incarcerated producer.

"A historic New Yorker that did great things for New York State. I think we should consider it."

Constantino’s brazen speech contrasts sharply with the demeanor of the district’s outgoing incumbent, Rep. Elise Stefanik, R-N.Y., the former No. 3 Republican in the House of Representatives. It also raises questions about whether Constantino earnestly hopes to see the administration pardon Combs, who was convicted of prostitution across state lines.

DIDDY'S FEDERAL PRISON RELEASE DELAYED WEEKS AFTER REPORTED SOLITARY CONFINEMENT STINT

"Where’s my lawyer at? I have a very good lawyer. Listen, I’m fighting for New York. I want to bring excitement back to New York. I want to bring jobs back to New York," Constantino said moments before his request.

During his 31-minute speech, Constantino spoke about political allies, enemies, the media, power struggles and his vision for the country. He even had a rapper friend perform a freestyle tribute to his congressional election.

At points, Constantino adopted an openly combative tone — especially with respect to members of the press.

"Listen to me, scumbags. Telling people the truth is the right thing to do. I had to listen to you a--holes say ‘dairy farmer Blake Gendebien,’" Constantino said, referring to news coverage of his Democratic challenger.

"He’s not a dairy farmer; his parents were dairy farmers … but you wouldn’t say that because you’re a bunch of f---ing a--holes," he added.

At one point, Constantino singled out a pair of reporters in the crowd.

"Look at that a--hole right there. Him. Look at that guy. Take a picture of him … and Kay Lisa, another f---ing a--hole."

Constantino then ordered one of the reporters removed from the room, describing him as an "angry motherf---er."

ANTIFA SUPPORTER CHARGED WITH STEALING GOP CAMPAIGN SIGNS IN NY RACE TO REPLACE STEFANIK

"Actually, do me a favor. This guy is so — he’s looking at me. Kick him out. Just kick him out. Get him out of here. You’re just a rude person. If you want to be tough on me, get out. Go right now. I’m not playing games with you. You deleted two of my interviews … bye bye," Constantino said.

Stefanik, a former GOP conference chair and Trump’s first pick to become U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, was considered by many a rising star within the Republican Party.

Although Stefanik began the confirmation process for the nomination, Trump ultimately rescinded his pick, calling on Stefanik to remain in the House, where Republicans held a razor-thin majority. A few months later, Stefanik announced that she would not pursue reelection or a bid for governor, citing a desire to focus on her family and avoid a primary contest.

Notably, Stefanik endorsed Constantino after the GOP primary for New York’s 21st Congressional District.

"In the coming months, I know Anthony will continue to work hard to earn your support. He will put the people first and will be a strong representative in Washington for the incredible hardworking families in our great district," Stefanik said in a post to social media.

Constantino also secured backing from President Donald Trump.

Constantino made headlines in 2024 when he put up a giant 100-foot "VOTE FOR TRUMP" sign atop his company building.

City officials, including Democratic Mayor Michael Cinquanti, argued the sign violated code because it "presents a dangerous distraction and impacts traffic flow," especially at night when it is illuminated.

After a legal battle, courts ruled that Constantino had a right to keep the sign in place, a decision he called an "epic win for free speech."

JOHN RICH SAYS KATHY HOCHUL IS ‘RUNNING OVER’ NY FARMERS WITH RENEWABLE ENERGY AGENDA

Last Tuesday, Constantino narrowly won his race in a 50.9% to 48.8% victory over Gendebien.

During his campaign, Constantino stressed his alignment with Trump, highlighting his record as a business owner, promised to bring reliable cell phone service to northern New York and reduce utility costs, according to his website.

Having secured his congressional race, Constantino will be sworn into office on Jan. 3, 2027, alongside the rest of the 120th Congress.
