World.title: VW scraps production modernization plan citing tough financial straits
World.content:
VW has announced that it will scrap large-scale modernization in light of its current economic situation. Employee representatives accuse leadership of putting short-term profits before long-term company viability.

Volkswagen, Europe's largest automaker, cited financial constraints on Wednesday when announcing that it will not carry out modernization plans as previously outlined in its project "Gamechanger" scheme.

A VW spokesman said all investments at the company are currently under review and that a planned large-scale casting facility at its main Wolfsburg site would not be moving forward despite years of preparation, investment and the stated goal of future-proofing the company for a rapidly evolving production landscape.

In his statement, the spokesman said the scrapping of Gamechanger did not mean the company would forego development of its Scalable Systems Platform (SSP) program, which aims to create a shared electric platform for future VW models like the ID. Roc, T-Roc and electric Golf.

VW, he said, will also continue to streamline production by simplifying its next generation of vehicles at all of its production facilities.

Volkswagen turns to new models, cost-cutting To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What did VW employee representatives say about Gamechanger's cancellation?

Daniela Cavallo, chair of the VW works council, slammed the decision, saying it was an admission of leadership's failure and accusing CEO Oliver Blume of forfeiting all claims of technical leadership in vehicle production.

Cavallo blasted the decision as a "flagrant breach" of agreements reached during difficult collective bargain negotiations in late 2024.

The 2024 agreement between VW and its employees outlined massive investments for facilities in order to create a foundation for the production of new models at VW's German factories and the relocation of internal combustion vehicle manufacturing to VW sites in Mexico.

Wolfsburg was to be the site of modern production technology including new large-scale casting facilities Image: Julian Stratenschulte/dpa/picture alliance

VW's Wolfsburg facilities, for instance, were to be overhauled in order to initiate SSP production there by the end of the decade. The overhaul centered on state-of-the-art manufacturing technologies such as the large-scale casting of body parts on site as envisioned in the Gamechanger project.

Works Council boss Cavallo has demanded the company's board of directors give a clear statement on what the abrupt scrapping of Gamechanger will mean for workers and production volume, adding, "production of the internal combustion Golf is not leaving Wolfsburg until we get transparency on the details of the decision."

Cavallo also accused VW leadership of putting short-term financial gain for investors ahead of the wellbeing of the company and its workers, saying, "Short-term return-driven thinking now stands in the foreground, and no longer the future viability of the VW Group, as was the case for decades."

World.title: Integration of immigrants in Germany: Much has been accomplished but problems remain
World.content:
The Federal office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant history is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate new arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems? Every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter. Since last year, that role has been held by Natalie Pawlik, a parliamentary representative from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD).

Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed. They rightly expect that people who live in Germany permanently will learn our language and abide by our laws." The Commissioner for Integration is part of the Federal Ministry of Labor because ensuring that newcomers find work quickly is especially important.

Employment rate of immigrants in Germany higher than in most EU countries

The integration report was created by a team led by Frank Kalter, director of the German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM) , drawing on official government statistics, surveys and independent studies. They found that when all immigrant groups are counted, about 30% of the population today has some sort of migration background — even if that comes down to only one parent.

Pawlik commented: "This is an important message at a time when the discussion often focuses primarily on problems related to supposedly failed integration." Kalter also pointed out that the employment rate among immigrants in Germany is higher than in most other EU countries — nearly 70%.

And they work primarily in one sector: "In recent years, the biggest increase of workers without German citizenship has been in the health and social services sector." According to the data, there were about 1.8 million people without a German passport working in Germany in 2009. By 2025, this number had more than tripled to 5.8 million.

Berlin initiative helps immigrant moms find their feet To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Concerns about unemployed mothers and violent youth

However, there are still plenty of problems. In nearly all immigrant groups, women have difficulty finding employment, especially if they have children and their husbands are employed. Only about 60% of women in such families are employed, whereas nearly 88% of women in families with German passports are employed.

There are also immigrant groups that face barriers to accessing educational opportunities and the job market. These are mostly young men who came to Germany as refugees. And if one considers citizenship as a distinguishing factor, the percentage of convicted criminals who are not German citizens is far higher — around 40% — than their share of the population. And they are also reported to the police far more frequently. At the same time, individuals without a German passport are also more likely to become victims of crimes.

Germany relies on Syrian workers amid return debates To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Government cuts funding for integration courses

Pawlik emphasizes that language acquisition is the foundation and starting point of any successful integration. But this is precisely where the government tightened its purse strings earlier this year in an effort to save money. Many integration courses are now no longer offered at all or receive less government funding. Pawlik made it clear that she is strongly critical of these cuts, even though she herself is part of the federal government.

Most recently, Pawlik and her fellow Social Democrats have been advocating for people who have been working in Germany for some time to receive more secure residency permits — especially those from Syria and Ukraine. On Tuesday, SPD lawmakers adopted a position paper on the matter. In the paper, they propose that existing legal rights that allow workers to remain in the country should also apply to refugees. In other words, it would give working refugees a more secure status.

But will the conservatives from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) — who lead the coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) — support this? "You'll have to ask the interior minister," Pawlik replied when asked by DW. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is known for being a hardliner on immigration policy.

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
World.content:
The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

Satisfaction with democracy in Germany has hit a new low, while the past is being idealized, and people are expressing a longing for a radical break. Antisemitic sentiments and the desire for an authoritarian leader are also on the rise. These are key findings of the authoritarianism study presented Wednesday in Berlin, which has been conducted every two years since 2002.

The study, led by the Else Frenkel-Brunswik Institute for Democracy Research at the University of Leipzig, is based on the answers to a questionnaire sent in by over 900 respondents, who the researchers say are a representative cross-section of the German population.

For the first time since the study series began, approval of democracy as an idea fell just below the 90% mark, which the study said is primarily attributable to a loss of trust among respondents in the former East Germany (85.7%). The decline in approval of democracy as experienced in everyday life is even more severe: Nationwide, only one-third are satisfied with democracy, with figures having fallen sharply both in eastern (22.8%) and western (36%) states.

Does Germany's Gen Z still feel the East-West divide? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

'Our democracy is under great pressure'

The growing rejection of democracy is also reflected in the desire for some kind of authoritarian nationalist government: Just under a quarter of respondents explicitly supported the idea of a "single strong party that embodies the national community as a whole." In the east, the figure stands at 30.9%, above the Germany-wide average of 22.3%.

"Our democracy is under great pressure. It has lost acceptance among the general population. It is alarming how much an authoritarian yearning is taking its place," concluded social psychologist and study author Oliver Decker.

Nationalism reaches record high

Far-right attitudes have risen for the second consecutive year. Of particular note in the study was what the researchers called a chauvinistic national pride, which, with 19.9% approval, has reached its highest level since the study series began. The proportion of people with a consistently far-right worldview has reached 6.9%, the highest level since 2014, the study found.

Just under 15% of respondents said they explicitly believe that "everything has to fall apart so that something new can emerge," while nearly one in three respondents believes that "something radical is needed for the current state of affairs to change." Another 29.1% agree with this to some extent.

Amid far right's rise, is Germany at a breaking point? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Connection between far right and AfD

According to the study, those who share this yearning for catastrophe exhibit significantly stronger antisemitic sentiments — and both are linked to a preference for certain political parties. The study found that a large proportion of eligible voters with this orientation favor the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD).

"Through its violent rhetoric, the AfD promises to realize the political goals of far-right ideology," the study said. The party's form and content, in other words, correspond exactly to the message that a significant portion of the population wants to hear. "It offers a political home to those who adhere to far-right thinking, while at the same time presenting itself as capable of connecting with a broad segment of society."

Antisemitic attitudes doubled

Study co-author Johannes Kiess calls on political leaders at all levels to find countermeasures. "The rejection of the present state of the world must be countered with compelling democratic alternatives and the ability to take political action today," he said. This also applies to the significant rise in antisemitism, which has more than doubled since 2022.

When asked about the motives behind antisemitic attitudes, the results show that for 16% of respondents, the policies of Israel's government are the decisive factor. This, too, is a record high in the context of the long-term study. While the figure in 2020 was significantly higher in the east (12%) than in the west (8.4%), the figures have since converged. Antisemitism related to Israel is actually slightly stronger in western than in eastern states.

Elif Eralp: From daughter of refugees to Berlin mayor? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Hostility toward Muslims is also on the rise

Hostility toward Muslims is also on the rise. It peaked at over 40% in 2018, before dropping to well below 30%, and currently stands at 34.1%. These figures are based on two statements respondents were asked to agree with in each survey: "Muslims should be prohibited from immigrating to Germany" and "because of the many Muslims here, I sometimes feel like a stranger in my own country."

Misogyny is another issue regularly surveyed in the study. In the current survey, 18.3% agreed with anti-feminist statements. Notably, until now, a higher proportion of East Germans had been opposed to feminist causes. As recently as 2024, the difference between the former East (34.6%) and West (19.6%) was enormous. Two years later, the figure in the east has halved to 17.8%, while in western Germany it has fallen only slightly to 18.4%.

A glimmer of hope

Despite the negative trend, there is a glimmer of hope at the end of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study: While the results are "alarming," long-term trends show that a reversal of this trend is possible: "In earlier surveys, far-right statements already achieved high approval ratings, which then declined again in subsequent years. In addition to the influence of societal crises, political action and its societal perception are of central importance."

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Kenya's last Ebola patient leaves hospital
World.content:
Kenya had nine confirmed cases, while DR Congo continues to battle its deadliest outbreak of the disease.

Kenyan Health Minister Aden Duale said on Wednesday that the east African country had discharged its last remaining Ebola patient from a Nairobi hospital.

The final person to undergo treatment for the disease in Kenya had 11 contact cases, Duale said, who will also undergo 21 days of quarantine.

Kenya will be declared Ebola-free on December 23 if no one else exhibits symptoms until then.

"Through strengthened surveillance and contact tracing, all 135 contacts linked to the index case were successfully traced and monitored," the health ministry said.

"All nine confirmed cases remained within a single transmission cluster, with no community transmission recorded," it added.

Did Ebola start spreading before officials even knew? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The first of its nine cases, reported on October 6, came from a Kenyan man who had recently travelled back from the Demoratic Republic of Congo.

Seven patients recovered, and two passed away.

What is the state of the Ebola outbreak?

DR Congo on Wednesday reported 11,000 cases of the virulent, often fatal disease.

This current outbreak, which began in May, has become Congo's deadliest, claiming 5,387 lives so far.

There has also been one case reported in Nigeria, from a patient who had recently travelled from Uganda, which saw a small cluster of the disease.

World.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
World.content:
The fine came after President Lula's coalition filed a complaint. The court said there was no evidence of intent to influence the election. Meta said it will defend itself against "false allegations."

Brazil's top electoral court has ordered Meta to pay 7.5 million reais ($1.34 million; €1.22 million) for failing to fully comply with judicial orders during last month's presidential election.

However, the judicial body has so far found no evidence that Meta deliberately acted to influence the election outcome.

Ahead of the runoff vote on October 25, leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's coalition filed a complaint, accusing Meta of "algorithmic manipulation" favoring his far-right rival Flavio Bolsonaro.

Platforms owned by Meta include Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

Meta told the court last month that it had implemented measures to guarantee equal treatment for both campaigns.

Meta lacked transparency, court says

The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously ruled on Tuesday to impose the 7.5 million reais fine on the US tech giant.

Meta missed deadlines and lacked transparency in its investigation, the court said.

On the other hand, the court's reporting judge Marco Aurelio Belizze wrote in his ruling that there were no preliminary evidence indicating that any intentional actions were taken to influence the election.

"That ​conclusion would require robust evidence, to be produced through the appropriate legal proceedings," he said.

In his victory speech, Lula reiterated that Brazil would 'not accept being anyone’s backyard,' a recurring campaign message defending the country’s sovereignty against US influence Image: Natacha Pisarenko/AP Photo/picture alliance

According to Bellizze, the fine was based on Meta's overall handling of the court orders, including delays, incomplete disclosures, and challenges in verifying some of the information it provided.

In a statement on Wednesday, Meta strongly denied the court's ruling.

"We will continue to present the facts and defend ourselves against false allegations in the ‌ongoing ​legal proceedings," Meta said in a statement on Wednesday.

Lula vows to rein in social media

Lula defeated Bolsonaro in a tight run-off in October 25 with him winning 51.7% of the vote against Bolsonaro's 48.2%.

In his victory speech, Lula urged more regulation of big tech platforms after allegations that Meta interfered in the race.

"We had to overcome foreign interference in the election, coming from outside through digital platforms that we will have to regulate," he said.

World.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
World.content:
The AIIB has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms and greater transparency are needed.

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story."

South Asia projects boost China's presence in India's sphere To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Call for easier access

The AIIB emphasized that not every issue needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank said in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it said.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts."

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," said Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

She argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

The AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it said, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

For 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

"The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly important documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement plans, vary widely or are missing entirely," said Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond in a timely manner and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

China's plan to dominate the seas To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

'It's not enough'

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, said the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough."

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he said, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

Criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not new.

A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

The AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

For Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she said.

As of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

But Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles."

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive."

The new rules have been in effect for only ten months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank said.

China's plan to never run out of food To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Fear of reprisals?

Steinert said fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

Such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert said.

However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank said that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns."

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat said Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

Hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards."

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
World.content:
At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya said.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud."

Mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager said in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

The youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

As a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

"He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

"Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Wael 'Waffel' Mohya working on and off the pitch

Borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

At the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

Wael Mohya made his debut against Wolfsburg in late 2025 Image: Maximilian Koch/picture alliance

Many clubs interested in Mohya

Even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

With Gladbach currently in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

The 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself says he doesn't even know how much he's currently earning at Gladbach.

"My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me."

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp said with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either."

Decision in favor of Germany over Morocco

Since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open only as long as he hasn't yet played a competitive match for Germany. If Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

This article was adapted from German.

World.title: Italy: Hundreds of schools evacuated after bomb threats
World.content:
Although the government believes the threat to be a hoax, it has nevertheless prompted concerns about "hybrid warfare" in Europe. Similar messages were sent in Northern Ireland, Ireland, and Bulgaria.

At 10 a.m. local time on Wednesday, 312 Italian schools received the same e-mail: "A powerful explosive device with a remote detonator has been left in your building."

Most of the affected schools were in Rome, but several other major cities also got the same message.

Antonello Giannelli, head of the National Association of School Principals, said that it was "clearly the work of a hoaxer" trying to sow chaos.

Defense Minister Guido Crosetto said it was also designed to "sow terror" for thousands of families.

Schools in Naples were also among those affected Image: Sergio Siano/IPA/picture alliance

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's cabinet will convene an emergency meeting this afternoon, the Palazzo Chigi has confirmed.

"The government is closely monitoring the numerous reports of bomb threats at schools," Meloni said in a statement posted to social media.

"Law enforcement agencies and government institutions at every level are working to monitor the situation and reassure citizens, families, and school staff.

"At this time, based on the investigations conducted, there is no evidence to suggest that a concrete danger exists. Rather, the reports appear to be part of a strategy aimed at causing alarm."

Concerns over hybrid warfare

The threatening e-mail sent to Italian schools was signed with the same fake name as similar messages that went out to newsrooms in Bulgaria and Ireland on Friday.

Some 300 schools in Northern Ireland were also affected, though it was not immediately clear if the threats had come from the same sender.

Recent hybrid attacks on supermarkets, air traffic controllers, blood banks and broadcasters across Europe have raised worries amongst leaders that this may be part of a coordinated attempt at hybrid warfare.

France summoned the Iranian ambassador on Tuesday over cyberattacks that caused supermarket freezers to defrost, but Tehran has denied any involvement.

Crosetto also cautioned against jumping to conclusions, saying: "It is not always ​the work of foreign countries or hostile entities. There are also attention-seekers and lunatics who" simply want to unleash mayhem.

World.title: Huelga general 11N y actualidad política, en directo | Miles de personas recorren las calles de numerosas ciudades en las manifestaciones de la huelga general
World.content:
De universitarios a jubilados: varias generaciones se unen en para apoyar la manifestación de Madrid

Desde universitarios en su primer año de carrera hasta funcionarias y abuelas. Personas de todas las edades han acudido esta tarde a la manifestación de Madrid para apoyar la huelga general. Sus situaciones son muy distintas: algunos han conseguido comprar una vivienda, mientras que otros ni siquiera contemplan esa posibilidad.

Maricarmen, de 82 años, que prefiere no dar su apellido, es una veterana de las movilizaciones. Cuando se le pregunta si esta es su primera huelga, se ríe: “Si no he hecho todas, he hecho casi todas”. Ella tiene una vivienda en propiedad, pero algunos de sus hijos y nietos, que rondan ya los 30 años, no han tenido la misma suerte. Aunque lo que más le preocupa son “los sueldos bajos”.

Esa incertidumbre sobre el futuro la comparten Juan Gómez y Alberto Ruiz, dos jóvenes de 18 años que estudian Ingeniería y han viajado desde Toledo para participar en la manifestación. Pese a que esperan acceder a empleos cualificados cuando terminen sus carreras, ni siquiera se plantean por ahora la posibilidad de comprar una casa.

A diferencia de ellos, Miguel Muñoz, de 32 años, ha logrado independizarse, pero tampoco ve cerca la posibilidad de convertirse en propietario. Es autónomo y vive entre Madrid y Galicia. En un pueblo gallego comparte piso con su hermano y la novia de este, mientras que en la capital reside de alquiler con su pareja. Se independizó hace cuatro años y, por el momento, considera “imposible adquirir una vivienda”. Ha acudido a la protesta preocupado por el futuro de su generación, que teme que no pueda acceder a unas condiciones de vida dignas.

A unos metros, Elena Villa, de 55 años, se protege de la lluvia bajo un paraguas mientras corea las consignas de la manifestación junto a su hermana. Es funcionaria del Ayuntamiento de Madrid y este miércoles ha secundado la huelga. Hace tres años terminó de pagar su hipoteca gracias a la ayuda económica de su madre, aunque asegura que sigue sin tener capacidad de ahorro. Tiene dos hijos y uno de ellos tuvo que marcharse a vivir con su abuela a los 17 años porque en la vivienda familiar, de dos habitaciones, no había espacio suficiente para todos. Elena tiene claro el motivo por el que hoy se manifiesta: por la “democracia”.

World.title: Barcelona se queda sin metro más de 10 horas durante la huelga general
World.content:
La huelga general de este miércoles deja a Cataluña durante 10 horas y 30 minutos sin servicio de transporte público tanto ferroviario como por carretera. Desde las 9.30 de la mañana y hasta las 16.30 de la tarde, Rodalies, Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FGC), el metro de Barcelona y los autobuses urbanos e interurbanos han suspendido las circulaciones de acuerdo con los servicios mínimos establecidos por la Generalitat. Tampoco prestarán servicio de las 21.00 hasta la medianoche . En las horas punta -de 6.30 a 9.30 y de 16.30 a 21.00- solo circularán el 25% de los trenes y autobuses habituales. Los servicios mínimos los ha fijado la Generalitat y son inferiores a los de las últimas huelgas generales de 2012 cuando en hora punta se garantizó el 33%. La jornada también ha provocado importantes problemas de movilidad por los cortes de carreteras y la cancelación de 85 vuelos -de los 734 programados- en el aeropuerto de Barcelona-El Prat.

La circulación de Rodalies se ha visto especialmente afectada durante las primeras horas de la mañana. Según Renfe, se ha suprimido el 22,5% de los servicios programados debido a que algunos maquinistas no han podido llegar a las locomotoras debido a los cortes de carreteras provocados por los piquetes. En el AVE, las cancelaciones alcanzan el 27,3% en la línea Madrid-Cataluña, y el la larga distancia el 20% en el corredor de Levante y Mediterráneo.

En el metro de Barcelona, TMB (Transportes Metropolitanos de Barcelona) ha retirado progresivamente los trenes una vez finalizada la primera franja de servicios mínimos y ha cerrado las estaciones hasta las 16.30. Durante las primeras horas de funcionamiento, el suburbano ha circulado con frecuencias inferiores a las habituales y convoyes más llenos. Algunos pasillos de enlace entre líneas han permanecido cerrados lo que ha obligado a los pasajeros a realizar transbordos por el exterior. En estaciones como La Sagrera, se han registrado algunas aglomeraciones en los accesos mientras que en Sants la afluencia ha sido menor de lo habitual.

Los autobuses de Barcelona también han registrado alteraciones durante la primera franja de servicios mínimos. Según TMB, el servicio ha sido ligeramente inferior al 25% establecido porque los vehículos no han podido salir de las cocheras de Triangle, aunque sí lo han hecho de las instalaciones de Horta y Zona Franca. De hecho, la empresa solo ha mantenido los servicios mínimos pese a que en algunas líneas había más trabajadores que los necesarios para garantizarlos.

En cuanto a los autobuses interurbanos, los cortes de carreteras han provocado numerosos retrasos durante las primeras horas de la jornada. Según la Federació Empresarial Catalana d’Autotransport de Viatgers (FECAV), los servicios mínimos se han cumplido sin grandes incidencias adicionales a las derivadas de las restricciones de tráfico. Algunos autobuses han continuado circulando después de las 9.30 debido a los retrasos acumulados.

El Govern ha asegurado que los servicios mínimos se están cumpliendo “de manera generalizada”, aunque ha reconocido la situación complicada de la movilidad. En Madrid, los servicios mínimos establecidos para la huelga general de este miércoles son del 80% en el metro durante las horas punta y del 50% durante el resto de la jornada. En los autobuses urbanos se garantiza entre el 40% y el 50% del servicio, mientras que en los interurbanos los porcentajes son del 50% en las horas de mayor demanda y del 45% durante el resto del día. En Cercanías de Renfe, los servicios mínimos alcanzan el 75% en las horas punta y el 50% fuera de ellas. Por su parte, Metro Ligero y el tranvía de Parla mantienen entre el 45% y el 50% de las circulaciones.

World.title: Cataluña, Galicia, País Vasco y Asturias lideran el seguimiento de una jornada de protesta desigual
World.content:
La primera huelga general desde 2012, cuando los sindicatos llamaron a movilizarse contra los recortes del Gobierno de Mariano Rajoy (PP), ha tenido este miércoles un seguimiento territorial “dispar”, según sus propios promotores, que la han calificado de “éxito”. Cataluña, Galicia, Asturias, País Vasco o Aragón son las regiones en las que el impacto de los paros ha sido mayor, o más visible, debido al seguimiento en el sector naval, la actividad portuaria, la industria pesada o el transporte. En Madrid o Andalucía las movilizaciones han estado condicionadas por el mal tiempo, que ha obligado a suspender las concentraciones de Sevilla, Cádiz y Huelva por el riesgo de la borrasca Charles. Los sindicatos han señalado a Extremadura, Castilla-La Mancha o Castilla y León como las regiones con menos apoyo a las protestas. Así, los convocantes han descrito a primera hora del miércoles, cuando han valorado los datos del turno de noche y el arranque de la jornada diurna, con una horquilla de participación de entre el 41% en comunidades del interior y el 75% en regiones costeras y del arco mediterráneo.

A media jornada, CC OO ha destacado un 84% de seguimiento en Cataluña, y ha cifrado en un 65% el impacto en Madrid. Todas las cifras sindicales han sido discutidas a la baja por la patronal.

Cataluña. La huelga general ha tenido un seguimiento en Cataluña del 84%, según los datos de CC OO, y la ha dejado durante 10 horas y 30 minutos sin servicio de transporte público tanto ferroviario como por carretera. Desde las 9.30 de la mañana y hasta las 16.30 de la tarde, Rodalies, Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FGC), el metro de Barcelona y los autobuses urbanos e interurbanos han suspendido las circulaciones de acuerdo con los servicios mínimos establecidos por la Generalitat. Tampoco está previsto que presten servicio de las 21.00 hasta la medianoche. La jornada también ha provocado importantes problemas de movilidad por los cortes de carreteras y la cancelación de 85 vuelos -de los 734 programados- en el aeropuerto de Barcelona-El Prat.

Así, en el arranque del día se ha suprimido el 22,5% de los servicios programados de Rodalies, el 27,3% en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Cataluña, y el 20% en la larga distancia del corredor de Levante y Mediterráneo.

Además, los piquetes han cortado una veintena de carreteras de Cataluña, entre ellas la AP-7, la A-2 y la B-10, y el sindicato USTEC ha fijado en un 45% el seguimiento de la huelga en los colegios.

En contraste, la principal patronal catalana, Foment del Treball, ha calificado de “baja” la participación en la huelga, que ha calculado en un 7%, y ha criticado por “insuficientes” los servicios mínimos en el transporte establecidos por la Generalitat.

País Vasco. El Gobierno Vasco ha situado el seguimiento de la huelga en un 38% en la administración general y un 60% en Educación en el arranque de la jornada. Los sindicatos ELA y LAB han hablado de seguimiento “amplio”, sobre todo en la industria, y de “gran adhesión” al paro sindical. “Euskadi se ha paralizado”, han asegurado los convocantes. Decenas de miles de vascos han participado en las manifestaciones convocadas en las capitales, donde el transporte público se vio especialmente afectado en Vitoria.

Asturias. CC OO y UGT han valorado este miércoles como un “éxito masivo” el seguimiento en Asturias de la jornada de huelga general por el derecho a la vivienda convocada este 11N, con una cifra global de participación que han situado en torno al 75%. De esta manera, han detallado un seguimiento cercano al 100% en empresas emblemáticas como Arcelor, Thyssen, Fertiberia o Rioglass; han destacado la incidencia en el transporte urbano de Gijón; y también en la recogida de basuras y la plataforma logística de Alimerka. La mayor incidencia ha estado en la industria, el transporte y en los centros logísticos.

Sin embargo, la Federación Asturiana de Empresarios (FADE) ha asegurado que la jornada transcurre con “normalidad” y con una asistencia al trabajo del 94%.

Por su parte, la Administración regional ha cifrado provisionalmente en un 10,12% el seguimiento de los paros entre los empleados públicos.

Aragón. Los sindicatos CC OO y UGT han cifrado en más del 70% el seguimiento de la huelga general en Aragón, según los datos recopilados durante los turnos de noche y mañana en los distintos sectores productivos y las administraciones públicas. Han destacado paros totales en empresas como Saica, CAF o FCC. Por su parte, el Gobierno de Aragón ha cifrado el impacto de la huelga en un 12% en el sector público.

Por territorios, las organizaciones empresariales cifran la participación en el 11,4% en Zaragoza, el 1,8% en Huesca y el 1% en Teruel. Además, apuntan que la demanda eléctrica en Aragón apenas cayó un 1% a mediodía respecto a jornadas comparables.

La policía ante una tienda del centro con los escaparates protegidos. Pablo Blazquez Dominguez (Getty Images)

Madrid. El servicio de Metro de Madrid ha funcionado al 93% de su capacidad entre las 7.30 y las 09.00 del miércoles, cuando los viajeros han caído en un 51%. Esa bajada de usuarios se ha reducido al 42% a las 10.00 (con todos los trenes previstos circulando) y al 39% entre las 14.00 y las 16.00 (con 91% de convoys en marcha), según datos de la compañía. Por su parte, Renfe ha reseñado que los mayores “problemas” en la red de Cercanías se han dado en Madrid, con un 19,63% de trenes suprimidos.

Además, en la capital el tráfico ha caído un 13% en el arranque del día, según el Ayuntamiento, y los usuarios de los autobuses públicos han descendido un 63%, lo que no ha impedido que el alcalde José Luis Martínez Almeida (PP) haya tildado de “pinchazo” la huelga. Finalmente, la patronal ha cifrado el seguimiento del paro en un 10% en el sector privado regional, mientras que el Ejecutivo autonómico lo ha dejado en un 9,6% para el sector público.

Por su parte, Susana Huertas, secretaria general de UGT Madrid, ha afirmado que la huelga general tiene “cifras récord de seguimiento”. CC OO ha cifrado el seguimiento en un 65%.

Los piquetes han cortado la A-1, la A-42, la A-5, la M-30 a la altura de Legazpi, Vallecas y Ventas, y la M-40 en Moratalaz en el inicio de la jornada de protesta. Desde primera hora también ha habido piquetes en Mercamadrid, en el puerto seco del Corredor del Henares y en las cocheras de metro y autobús de Entrevías, Ventas, Fuencarral y Carabanchel. La televisión pública madrileña ha emitido contenido enlatado, y casi medio centenar de sus casi 600 empleados han secundado el paro.

Manifa del sindicato CIG en Vigo. Silvia R. Pontevedra

Galicia. La manifestación de la Central Intersindical Galega (CIG) en la mañana del miércoles ha superado las expectativas y ha convocado a más manifestantes, incluso, que la de CC OO y UGT, que había concentrado a miles de personas por Vigo una hora antes. El seguimiento en las distintas compañías industriales de Galicia ha sido desigual, con un 100% de paro en la fábrica de Alcoa San Cibrao en los turnos de noche y de mañana que contrasta, en el otro extremo, con un 20% del turno de noche en la fábrica de vehículos de Stellantis en la Zona Franca de Vigo.

Por poner otros ejemplos, Comisiones Obreras ha calculado en un 70% el seguimiento en la industria, con fábricas “paralizadas” en la “práctica totalidad” como Navantia Ferrol, GKN Driveline en Vigo y la conservera Profand y DS Smith en Vilagarcía. De la misma manera, en Ence (Pontevedra), han funcionado con “normalidad” los servicios mínimos pactados y Pescanova ha parado al igual que muchas empresas del polígono de O Porriño, al sur de Vigo. En toda Galicia, la lista de factorías que han tenido que cerrar o cuyo personal no ha sido suficiente para poder mantener la actividad es larga. Mientras tanto, el seguimiento de la huelga en la sanidad pública no ha alcanzado el 10%, aunque según la CIG se han tenido que cerrar quirófanos por la falta de personal.

En el sector Transportes, en cambio, los sindicatos afirman que el seguimiento ha sido masivo. CC OO estima en un 80% el porcentaje de seguimiento en el transporte por carretera, un cálculo que “se eleva al 100% en el caso de la empresa Monbus en Lugo”. En el sector ferroviario, el 70% de los trabajadores no acudieron a sus puestos según el mismo sindicato y el 80% de los empleados de la recogida de basuras, tampoco. Los contenedores amanecieron a rebosar en la mayoría de las ciudades gallegas.

Andalucía. “Alto grado de seguimiento” frente a “seguimiento escaso” son las versiones contrapuestas que han ofrecido los dirigentes sindicales de CC OO y UGT en Andalucía y la Confederación de Empresarios Andaluces (CEA) sobre la incidencia de la huelga en Andalucía. Mientras las organizaciones sindicales cifran en al menos un 75% el grado de seguimiento del paro en la industria andaluza (que suben al 100% en el Puerto de Algeciras o al 90% en la agroindustria), la patronal CEA no ha avalado ese balance y ha incidido en que “una parte de esas ausencias responde a la acción de los piquetes coactivos”.

La patronal refuerza esa convicción con el dato de consumo eléctrico que reflejan un descenso del 0,9% respecto del martes y de un 6,5% respecto del miércoles de la semana pasada, “lo que aporta una fotografía real de su seguimiento”, ha concluido en un comunicado.

De acuerdo con la información facilitada por la Junta, el 98,8% de los 108.827 docentes de Andalucía ha asistido a su puesto de trabajo. Además, el seguimiento de la huelga en el personal no docente ha sido del 0,3%; los metros de Málaga y Sevilla han estado funcionando al 100%; y el de Granada, al 60%. Sobre el transporte por carretera, la Junta ha apuntado que “el servicio está muy por encima de los servicios mínimos del 60%”. Y en Sanidad ha trasladado que apenas un 4% de los profesionales del turno de mañana, y un 2% del de tarde, han secundado el paro. La televisión pública andaluza se ha ido a negro.

Comunidad Valenciana. Los puertos de la Comunidad Valenciana han estado “prácticamente paralizados”, según han destacado representantes de los sindicatos UGT y CC OO. Ha habido cortes en la V-21, la Ronda Nord, la avenida del Cid, Paiporta y la entrada de Vila-real.

La patronal valenciana CEV ha situado el seguimiento de la huelga general por debajo del 3%, frente al 60% que han calculado los representantes de los trabajadores.

Extremadura, Castilla-La Mancha y Castilla y León. Los sindicatos sitúan a estas tres comunidades autónomas entre las que menos impacto ha tenido la huelga, aunque han destacado que sí se ha notado en centros logísticos clave para el centro peninsular, como los situados en Guadalajara.

World.title: Los sindicatos avisan: “Si van contra la gente, nos volverán a tener enfrente”
World.content:
Los sindicatos convocantes de la huelga general del 11-N son conscientes de que las concentraciones vividas este miércoles son tan solo un punto y seguido en la hoja de ruta que llevan diseñando desde hace varios meses para denunciar las dificultades para acceder a la vivienda o la amenaza de recorte presupuestario constante sobre los servicios públicos. “Muchas de las formaciones que comparecen en las próximas elecciones están diciendo claramente algunas de las cosas que quieren hacer y muchas de ellas van en contra de la gente. Si van a ir contra la gente, nos volverán a tener enfrente”, precisó Marcelo Picazo, secretario de Comunicación de Comisiones Obreras, en conversación con EL PAÍS en plena manifestación.

Entre los derechos que pueden estar amenazados, citó el posible ajuste que se baraja sobre las pensiones, el endurecimiento de las bajas laborales para acabar con un supuesto absentismo laboral que, por otro lado, negó como realidad o el tijeretazo generalizado de 60.000 millones de euros que propone Vox a partir de una estimación del Instituto de Estudios Económicos (IEE), el servicio de estudios de CEOE.

Alicia del Río, portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, el movimiento que inspiró la primera acampada en Madrid y las posteriores en el resto de ciudades españolas, celebró el éxito de la histórica huelga general y avisó que la de el miércoles es solo la primera de muchas concentraciones. “La movilización social no ha hecho más que empezar y el poder popular no va a parar de crecer. Es un clamor imparable, es un éxito”, reiteró en declaraciones a Efe. Del Río rechazó que la huelga se pensara y organizara contra el futuro gobierno. “Se dirige contra todos los gobiernos, incluido el actual, que lleva ocho años en el poder, contra la patronal y contra los rentistas, que son todos los responsables de esta crisis de vivienda. Necesitamos un nuevo modelo de vivienda y un cambio radical que deje atrás los parches y las políticas que han fracasado”. Por todo ello, la portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas instó a aprobar normativas que expulsen a los especuladores, a movilizar las viviendas vacías y a bajar los precios de alquiler por ley. “No aguantamos más”, concluyó.

Un punto en el que coincidió con Pepe Álvarez, secretario general de UGT. “Deberían de decirnos qué piensan hacer [en clara relación a las propuestas presentadas por PP y VOX para las elecciones del 29-N]. Si las próximas Cortes Generales con una mayoría amplia van a ser capaces de hacer una modificación constitucional que consagre la vivienda como un derecho público y que no tenga ninguna posibilidad de ser vendida aquella que cuente con recursos públicos”, apuntó en declaraciones a Efe.

Al margen de la crisis de vivienda o la falta de inversión en los servicios públicos, la pérdida de poder adquisitivo de los trabajadores al crecer la inflación muy por encima de los salarios es otra de las reivindicaciones que desde UGT quieren llevar a las futuras mesas de negociación. “Exigiremos subidas salariales por encima del 4,9% [el nivel alcanzado por la inflación en octubre] y reclamaremos un salario mínimo interprofesional (SMI) un 7% más alto para 2027″.

El secretario de Comunicación de Comisiones Obreras denunció precisamente la paralización de la negociación colectiva en lo que va de 2026 y culpa a la patronal de ese frenazo en la renovación de los convenios: “Llevan todo el año teniendo la oportunidad de de sentarse a negociar y no han llegado a comparecer, denunciando muchas veces la injerencia del Gobierno en la negociación colectiva. Y ahora parece que ante el adelanto electoral y la posibilidad de que el nuevo gobierno esté más alineado con sus peticiones, hayan optado por esperar a ver si se produce ese escenario”.

Frente a las críticas expresadas por la convocatoria de una huelga general con un gobierno en funciones, Picazo incidió en la anomalía de un gobierno progresista que ha querido aprobar derechos sociales, pero que fueron “tumbados” por un Parlamento con mayoría de derechas. “Impidieron los dos decretos de vivienda o la reducción de la jornada laboral”, remachó.

Todos los portavoces consultados coincidieron en que las convocatorias concertadas entre los sindicatos mayoritarios de clase y los sindicatos vinculados a la sociedad civil son la fórmula idónea para profundizar en una protesta sindical que trasciende el ámbito laboral. “Es necesario confluir con los movimientos de vivienda que son los que generaron esa ola de indignación con el desahucio de Maricarmen”, señaló el secretario de Comunicación de CC OO, quien, en cambio, subrayó que cualquier tipo de movilización laboral en el futuro “pasa por sindicatos de clase articulados organizados, que conocen los funcionamientos de de una movilización y que conocen los resortes de de la organización sindical para poder alcanzar un éxito como el alcanzado el 11-N”.
